Body:
Dear Ulrik,
Thank you very much for your update - and apologies for my belated response. 
There is no doubt that we would easily be able to help procure and deliver mobile health clinics. This is something we have already done with great success as part of the Ebola and COVID responses. We would suggest that these mobile clinics are tied to a hospital, so that the clinics can be utilised even during a post-war scenario. 
We would absolutely align this effort with the Ukrainian healthcare reform. All that we do in Ukraine on behalf of donors (such as Novo Nordisk and Denmark) obviously needs to underpin and be aligned with Ukrainian wishes. 
An approach where we procure and deliver mobile health clinics in connection to the reconstruction of a hospital / health clinics would also align well with the transition from humanitarian and emergency response to recovery and longer term development interventions. 
I am pleased to hear that you are still open to include in a possible new engagement the reconstruction / modernisation of a hospital or minor health clinics. We now have a few locations and scopes that we can consider together: We need to revalidate if Snihurivka and other primary healthcare centres that we discussed initially are still available (they have likely received funds for some of them). Bucha could be a new option where there is a need to modernise a mental health facility plus construct a multi-disciplinary hospital. Procurement of lacking radioactive components to fully enable the Mykolaiv Cancerclinic treatment is also an option that we could discuss depending on your budget level. 
Finally I just want to flag that it would be very likely that mobile clinics would be in a situation of offering health services to wounded soldiers with "dual use" implications that you should be aware of - as these units may contribute to soldiers returning to the battlefield and the overall combat readiness. This is something we can mitigate on paper - and discuss further. 
I have looped in my colleagues from Ukraine to ensure transparency and ease communication. We would be very happy to meet as soon as possible at your convenience to discuss how to take this forward. 
Could you let me know when you are available for an online meeting? 
Thank you in advance. 
Best,Asbjørn

I very quick update from our side in relation to Novo Nordisk support to reconstruction of health infrastructure in Ukraine.

 
I had meeting last week with MoFA and the Danish Embassy in Ukraine. The main item of the meeting was a discussion around the different options which we have been looking at in terms of support
 to the reconstruction of a hospital versus primary healthcare centres. In that connection there was according to MoFA also another possible option which could be to create mobile clinics serving as primary care facilities. The mobile clinics cost 50’000-100’000
 a piece depending on which equipment you put inside and gives a flexibility in providing services as close as possible to the frontline even when it is moving.

 Is this something that you would also consider as an option in UNOPS that can be pursued? If so, it would still need to be integrated into the Ukrainian health services. But it could potentially
 also be integrated to our support to a hospital where patients are referred to from the mobile services. If the mobile clinics is a possible solution, it would be interesting to investigate whether we would be able to give support to both a hospital and mobile
 health service as an integrated part of our support. 
 
Another theme which is recurring in the conversations is the Ukrainian healthcare reform. The reconstruction of healthcare facilities should of course in any case be part of the healthcare reform
 which I realise is more long term but nevertheless important to ensure sustainability of our support.

 
It would be great to have your feedback on above and happy to set up a meeting in first week of January to further discuss the possible options.

 
Kind regards
Ulrik

Kære Daniel, Rikke og Ulrik


 


Som opfølgning på vores dialog tidligere i dag, vedlægger jeg her de slides vi gennemgik med henblik på jeres stillingtagen til, hvilke optioner I ønsker at arbejde
 videre med.


 


Bl.a. af hensyn til tilbagemelding til de ukrainske myndigheder og da situationen udvikler sig hurtigt på jorden, håber vi meget på jeres tilbagemelding senest mandag
 d. 18. september. 


 


Dermed kan vi låse os fast på en af tilgangene, melde dette til de ukrainske myndigheder og få håndteret den kontraktuelle del med jer snarest. Dette også med henblik
 på hurtigst muligt at komme i gang med det konkrete arbejde på jorden.  


 


Som drøftet ses grundlæggende to optioner for den videre vej frem:




Genopbygning og evt. modernisering af Snigurivska City Hospital, Mykolaiv
Genopbygning og evt. modernisering af en håndfuld mindre sundhedsklinikker i Mykolaiv

Som drøftet på mødet er der en række fordele hhv. ulemper ved de to optioner, som jeg på bedste vis har forsøgt at opsummere nedenfor - idet jeg bemærker at der
 ikke er tale om en udtømmende liste. 


 


Ad 1) Snigurivska City Hospital i Mykolaiv




De ukrainske myndigheder (særligt Sundhedsministeriet) foretrækker at dette hospital genopbygges. 
Der er tale om et velanerkendt hospital med relativ stor bevågenhed, herunder fordi hospitalet har været under russisk besættelse i 8 måneder. Se fx
denne artikel. 
Genopbygning af dette hospital vil få relativ stor positiv effekt. 
Selvom hospitalet ligger relativt tæt på frontlinjen (ca. 40 km) vurderes der ikke at være større risiko for, at dette hospital igen rammes af russiske angreb end andre hospitaler i fx Mykolaiv området. 
Der er angiveligt militært personale til stede på visse dele af hospitalet. Det vil skulle afklares - og der vil være behov for klare skriftlige garantier fra de ukrainske myndigheder om, at hospitalet ikke har nogen form for militær anvendelse
 - men fortsat alene fungerer som et civilt hospital (som naturligvis også kan behandle såret militært personel). 
Den nuværende militære tilstedeværelse øger risikoen for en længerevarende periode med forudgående papirarbejde mhp. at sikre de nødvendige garantier for at kunne gennemføre arbejdet. 
Adgang til hospitalet er besværliggjort af den relativt korte afstand til frontlinjen. 

 


Ad 2) Genopbygning af en række mindre sundhedsklinikker i Mykolaiv





Bruttoliste på ca. 25 mindre sundhedsklinikker i Mykolaiv by og i landdistrikterne i regionen. Opdateres løbende. 
Ud af de 25 klinikker udvælger vi sammen de klinikker som vurderes mest hensigtsmæssige at genopbygge/renovere - efter en umiddelbart besigtigelse af vores ingeniører. 
Relativ stor fleksibilitet i udmøntningen, og mulighed for løbende at vise fremskridt på jorden efterhånden som de enkelte klinikker genopbygges. 
Mindre bevågenhed på de mindre klinikker - idet der dog også er stor reel efterspørgsel i fx landdistrikterne. 
Mulighed for at udstyre de fleste af klinikkerne med relevant udstyr til håndtering af ikke-smitsomme sygdomme - efter dialog med de lokale ukrainske myndigheder. 

Jeg håber det nogenlunde opsummerede vores samtale. 



 


Vi er helt til jeres rådighed for evt. opfølgende spørgsmål, behov for afklaring eller andet. 


 


Jeg ser meget frem til at høre fra jer snarest muligt. 


 


På forhånd tak. 


 


Mvh


Asbjørn

Subject: Denmark Infrastructure Mykolaiv - monthly update meeting Dec '23
Body:
Dear Asbjorn,
A quick update as we just come out of the (newly established) monthly update meeting with donor (Embassy: Olga, CPH: Jasmin and Torben), and stakeholders (city - Sergey Kohiniiv and Andrii, and oblast - deputy governor Mykola Marinov, and Andrii) on the project progress.
The government stakeholders' sense of urgency that things need to happen faster, is palpable. This position they have taken and will continue to take in every meeting, and it is a justified one, considering the context.
Our, as justified, position on the required quality in the process (Design Review, effective procurement in a high corruption environment, etc) to achieve long-term results, is often mistaken for bureaucracy and too slow processes.
Whilst - internally - there of course always are ways to improve process efficiency, they are instrumental to our mandate and directly contribute to sustainable outcomes.
Concerns by the city were raised also on the costing of bomb-shelters for which we have preliminary figures following the feasibility studies, but will only have exact amounts once the respective designs are finalized. 
The city thinks to hold comparative shelter construction information from other oblasts which are more economical and quicker to construct. We remind them that no single shelter is the same, and that cost benchmarking needs to compare same with same.
Value for money is an underpinning principle for all our interventions, so if there are real and significant costing discrepancies between similar shelter projects, we will analyse why that would be the case. But, frankly, costing is very comparable across similar projects, we find.                 
The above points were again raised by a single participant, Andrii, who uses the setting, with superiors and donor in the meeting, to repeat the same points - that he is fully briefed on from the weekly project interaction with him. 
It is clear that going forward we will be more tactical in our communication, specifically for this format meeting, and focus on marketing the progress (of which there is a lot, though not yet tangible on the ground).
For 2024 we will be leading the monthly update meetings and are now scheduling the next for the end of January. It is all our interest to move to construction as soon as possible, but also to note that this is a three year project for a quality reason.
This briefback to you, in case a conversation should come again from the UKR ambassador, who obviously is closely connected to Mykolaiv.
@Teresa MOLERO RODRIGUEZ @Arun NARAYANAN @Elene AGLADZE please complement as needed.
Asbjorn, if I don't speak to you prior: Happy Holidays and happy end of year!
Best,
Philip   Jan Philip Klever | Head of Programme | Ukraine Office | Kyiv, Ukraine | Tel. (+380) 95 278 4072  | Email: janphilipk@unops.org

Dear Agnes, 
Following up on our recent conversation, I wanted to confirm that the office of the new Senior Coordinator (Ms. Sigrid Kaag) is currently developing a reconstruction strategy - involving all the relevant parties. There is no timeline as to when this will be finalised. Therefore I am unfortunately unable to share this with you for now. 
As you know, following the recent approval of Security Council Resolution 2720, the UN Secretary General appointed Ms Sigrid Kaag as Senior Humanitarian and Reconstruction Coordinator for Gaza (see news flash here). The UN SG has tasked UNOPS to 1) supporting the full operationalization of the Office of Senior Humanitarian and Reconstruction Coordinator for Gaza; and 2) the establishment of the UN mechanism to facilitate, coordinate, monitor, and verify humanitarian relief consignments to Gaza.

I know there is already a good contact between the FCDO and our local office in Amman that coordinates the work (Marija Bateman - marijab@unops.org). Don't hesitate to have your team on the ground reach out to her for any detailed info etc. 
For your information I am attaching a brief overview of UNOPS' work so far in Gaza as well as our capacity to rapidly procure and deliver much needed items for the population. 
Currently we have a strong presence on the ground to implement life saving projects. UNOPS' office in Egypt supports the management and oversight of the logistics chains required for delivery of humanitarian assistance into Gaza. Our UNOPS team in Gaza stands ready to support delivery of humanitarian assistance and early recovery responses. 
So far during the ongoing crisis, UNOPS has been - and continues to - supply fuel for humanitarian operations. UNOPS procures the fuel from Egypt and delivers it through the Rafah Crossings, and ensures that the fuel is only distributed to the humanitarian locations.  We have established a coordinated communication with DSS to ensure the deconfliction and safety of the deployed staff on the ground.
In addition, UNOPS continues to support the operations of the Access Support Unit with its key role in access of humanitarian actors, evacuation of staff and rotation of humanitarian staff.

Finally we are currently delivering various humanitarian supplies into Gaza including NFIs, health items and others.

Please feel free to relay this information to the relevant FCDO team as we would be happy to support the implementation of the UK's much needed help in Gaza. 
Best,Asbjørn

Subject: Follow-up: Novo Nordisk/UNOPS engagement in Mykolaiv, Ukraine
Body:
Dear Ulrik
Thank you for a constructive conversation today on how we can help Novo Nordisk implement much needed help for the Ukrainian health care. Below I have - to the best of my ability - tried to summarise what we discussed and agreed upon. 
Upon your green light, we will engage in conversations with the relevant Ukrainian authorities (Health Ministry, region and city) to get more technical details about concrete sites and needed equipment. Before doing so, we would need a commitment from Novo Nordisk to move ahead with the project so that we do not generate too high expectations among Ukrainian stakeholders. 
An engagement between Novo Nordisk and UNOPS should contain the following:3 overall tracks of intervention:Infrastructure: Reconstruction/modernisation of a health care hospital/clinic(s)Procurement: Delivery of mobile health care clinicsProcurement: Delivery of medical supplies - focused on diagnosing and treating NCDs. The engagement should be in Mykolaiv - city and region. Sustainable infrastructure and procurement must be prioritised. In concrete terms it would mean that we would eg. ensure sustainable procurement of goods and services, minimising carbon footprint, buying from local ukrainian suppliers where feasible, favouring women owned businesses, hiring local ukrainian contractors where feasible, etc. It would also mean that we would prioritise climate friendly infrastructure for the modernisation / reconstruction element. For example by increasing energy efficiency. The mobile health clinics should be attached to a specific hospital / clinic. Focus for the infrastructure track would be on one (or more) major hospitals. Selection of the site for modernisation / reconstruction should be in line with the Ukrainian health reform / Ministry of Health’s requests and the number of potential patients to be reached should be maximised. 
I hope this somewhat reflects your priorities and I look forward to hearing back from you as soon as possible so that we can start getting things done on the ground. 

Best,Asbjørn

Kære Ulla, 
I lige måde. Det var godt lige hurtigt at møde dig. 
Kære Asbjørn, jeg håber, at du er nået godt frem til New York. Direktør for Nordic Representation for UNFPA, Ulla E. Müller kom forbi vores kontor i dag.  Regeringen er ved at forberede en lovændring, der skal gøre det lettere for udlandsdanskere at vende hjem til Danmark med deres udenlandske ægtefæller. Som international embedsmand tjener man riget og alligevel er der betingelser, der gør det vanskeligt for udlandsdanskere at vende hjem med deres ægtefæller, der ikke er danske statsborgere, efter endt tjeneste. Se vedhæftet et dokument, der tydeliggør udfordringen, som danske FN-ansatte i udlandet står overfor. 
Her er forslaget: https://hoeringsportalen.dk/Hearing/Details/68337
Ulla foreslår, at vi sammen udarbejder et høringssvar, der fjerner restriktioner for danskere, der har været i tjeneste for FN i udlandet og vender hjem med deres familier. Som Ulla skriver, er høringsfristen den 14. februar, og FN Forbundet forventes også at fremsende et høringssvar.
Jeg ved, at du står over nogle ret travle uger i New York. Ulla tager gerne lead på dette, men har naturligvis brug for hjælp fra UNOPS, særligt fra en dansker med erfaring fra ministerier eller med jura baggrund. 
Bedste hilsener Naimo

On Mon, Jan 22, 2024 at 10:16 AM Ulla mueller <umueller@unfpa.org> wrote:
Kære Naimo, 
Det var fint at møde dig netop nu, tak for hjælpen. 
Som aftalt sender jeg her et link til lovforslaget på høringsportalen. 
Det fremgår af forslaget at der stadig vil være betingelser for at udlandsdanskere kan vende hjem med ægtefælle der ikke er dansk, og det jeg mener vi skal gøre er, at udarbejde et  høringssvar der fjerne restriktioner for dansker der har været ude og vender hjem med deres familie. 
Forslaget findes her: 
https://hoeringsportalen.dk/Hearing/Details/68337

Jeg håber, Asbjørn kan hjælpe, eller guide mig det rigtige sted hen. Høringsfristen er 14 Februar, og  FN Forbundet samt venner af FN forbundet forventes også at fremsende høringssvar. 

Sluttelig et skriv, der helt tydeligt fortæller problemstillingen, og hvor vi efterlod det i landeaftalen. Det er udarbejdet af Erik Blas, som jeg har talt med tidligere. 

Mange hilsener Ulla

Body:
Kære Constantin og Stein Erik,
Jeg håber I har haft et godt nytår og nu er tilbage ved fuld kraft. 
Jeg håber også at I fandt den uformelle session vedrørende kulturændringerne i UNOPS, overskuds-reserven samt handlingsplanen nyttige. Der er som bekendt kalendersat to yderligere uformelle sessioner vedrørende revisions-bemærkningerne (i morgen) og UNOPS' portefølje (på torsdag). 
Jeg er selv i NYC denne uge samt næste uge - og vil meget gerne mødes til en uformel dialog, hvis I har tid og lyst. Må jeg spørge om en af jer forventer at deltage i selve bestyrelsesmødet eller hvordan Norge ventes repræsenteret? 
Hvis I finder det hensigtsmæssigt står jeg som nævnt nedenfor også helt til jeres rådighed for en online og uformel dialog i løbet af denne uge. 
Jeg ser frem til at høre fra jer. 
På forhånd mange tak. 
MvhAsbjørn
On Tue, 19 Dec 2023 at 05:34, Asbjorn BRINK <asbjornb@unops.org> wrote:
Kære Constantin og Stein Erik,
Som tidligere annonceret hermed de centrale dokumenter, der skal drøftes på det næste bestyrelsesmøde den 29. januar til 2. februar. Dokumenterne er også tilgængelige på vores hjemmeside her .
For at hjælpe med at fordøje den omfattende information har jeg også givet min egen læsning / sammenfatning af dokumenterne og de centrale emner, der skal diskuteres nedenfor. Jeg beklager på forhånd den (meget) lange mail – men jeg håber, at dette kan hjælpe igennem de endnu længere vedhæftede dokumenter.
For at lette den kommende diskussion i EB håber jeg, at vi kan mødes i begyndelsen af januar mhp. at drøfte jeres første, uformelle reaktioner og forsøge at afklare eventuelle spørgsmål på forhånd. Alt dette mhp. at sikre bedre og mere konstruktive drøftelser på selve EB.
Lad mig derfor meget gerne vide hvornår det kunne passe at mødes i starten af januar for uformelt at drøfte de fem centrale emner. 
Fem hovedemner skal diskuteres:Comprehensive Response PlanHer kan du finde UNOPS-notatet, der opsummerer implementeringen af den omfattende indsatsplan indtil nu.Bemærk venligst, at KPMG's uafhængige gennemgang af implementeringen endnu ikke er færdig. Jeg forstår på KPMG, at den forventes færdig i slutningen af december eller begyndelsen af januar. Så snart rapporten er endelig, vil den blive sendt til EB.

Mandat og porteføljeHer kan du finde informationsnotatet om UNOPS mandat og portefølje som anmodet om ved sidste EB-session og bilag 2 med fakta, tal og eksempler til at facilitere drøftelserne.

Skift i organisationskulturHer kan du finde informationsnotatet om UNOPS organisationskultur og informationsnotatet om gennemgang af kontraktmodaliteter på tværs af UNOPS 

Fordeling af den overskydende reserveSe her notatet om status for fordelingen af de overskydende reserver samt optioner for håndtering af de resterende midler.

UNBOA anbefalinger til UNOPSHer kan du finde rapporten om UNOPS implementering af anbefalingerne fra FN-revisorerne for 2022 .  
Ad 1: Implementering Comprehensive Response Plan og vejen fremMens vi venter på KPMG's uafhængige gennemgang af implementeringen - som naturligvis vil være afgørende for diskussionerne - ville jeg fremhæve hovedpunkterne fra vores egen statusrapport.Af de 43 oprindelige KPMG-anbefalinger er 32 afsluttet ved udgangen af 2023. 7 vil blive afsluttet i løbet af 2024, 1 fortsætter indtil 2027 og 1 ledes af FN's juridiske kontor. 2 er ikke blevet operationaliseret, da vi har lukket helt ned for S3i-arbejdssporet.De 7, der vil blive afsluttet i 2024, vedrører:1) At gøre risikostyring til en integreret del af alle centrale beslutningsprocesser og 2) en vurdering af UNOPS' portefølje og skjulte risici.3) Revision af whistleblowing-processen, 4) oprettelse af protokoller for klager og undersøgelser og 5) en ny organisationskultur.6) Investeringer kapaciteter til at forbedre resultatrapportering og 7) styrkelse af due diligence (hvilket indebærer en omfattende revision af vores finansielle regler).Den, der fortsætter frem til 2027, vedrører digitaliseringstransformationen. Dette er en kompleks og vigtig transformation, som vil tage tid.
Det igangværende arbejde med de resterende anbefalinger er helt afgørende for, at UNOPS kommer tilbage i en meget bedre form. Disse vedrører især, hvordan vi håndterer risici, etik/kultur og at vi bliver bedre til at dokumentere resultaterne af det arbejde, vi udfører på stedet.

Fremskridt med risikostyring, kultur og måling af resultater er komplekse og vigtige. Derfor har vi brug for tid til at gennemføre reformerne. Det giver derfor ikke nødvendigvis længere mening, at UNOPS ED giver opdateringer til EB hver eneste måned, da der ikke vil være meget substans at rapportere hver måned, og da disse emner bliver meget tekniske. Det kan derfor være hensigtsmæssigt at drøfte, hvordan vi fremadrettet bruger tiden mere effektivt. For eksempel ved at give opdateringer hvert kvartal og/eller at opdateringerne sker på et mere teknisk niveau end ED.

Ad 2: Mandat og porteføljeSom du sikkert ved, anmodede den sidste EB-session om, at UNOPS skulle give detaljerede oplysninger om tidligere og fremtidige sammensætning af UNOPS-porteføljen af projekter. Vi blev bedt om især at vise, hvordan det er forankret i det oprindelige UNOPS-mandat.
Som svar har vi udarbejdet et informationsnotat om UNOPS' mandat og portefølje. Den forklarer facetter af UNOPS-mandatet, og hvordan det operationaliseres i den nye strategiske plan - vedtaget af EB i 2023.

Analysen af vores globale portefølje af projekter er kontekstualiseret i mandatet. Den illustrerer, hvorfor UNOPS gør, hvad det gør, med hvem og hvor. Den giver omfattende information om den tidligere og forventede fremtidige UNOPS-portefølje, som er forankret i resolution 65/176 - altså UNOPS' oprindelige mandat.
Analysen bygger på porteføljeanalysen for perioden 2014-2022 præsenteret som et bilag til midtvejsevalueringen i 2023. Et bilag til informationsnotatet indeholder yderligere fakta, tal og eksempler om UNOPS' mandat og portefølje. Det giver også en prognose for 2023 og estimater for 2024-2025, som tyder på fortsat vækst i efterspørgslen efter projektydelser inden for områder af UNOPS' oprindelige mandat.
På årsbasis omfatter UNOPS-porteføljen omkring 700 forskellige engagementer med partnere. I 2022 leverede det projektydelser til en værdi af 2,5 milliarder dollars, ekskl. omkring 1 milliard dollars til farmaceutiske indkøb på vegne af Mexico.

Analysen illustrerer, hvordan hele porteføljen er solidt forankret i UNOPS-mandatet for projektydelser, som funktionelt spænder over infrastruktur, indkøb og projektledelse, herunder HR og økonomistyring. Dette suppleres af en oversigt over UNOPS' servicemodeller samt en række projekteksempler, herunder med erfaringer fra eksterne evalueringer.
Notatet illustrerer, hvordan alle projekter i porteføljen har været knyttet til bæredygtighedsmålene. Den giver også en opdatering om foranstaltninger, der er truffet for at fremme den faste strategiske forpligtelse til at bekæmpe klimaændringer.

Informationsnotatet fremhæver, at alle aktiviteter forbundet med S3i er blevet indstillet, inklusive kontoret i Helsinki, som forvaltede den separate portefølje af effektinvesteringsinitiativer og innovationscentre. FN-sekretariatet styrer processen med at inddrive de 63,6 millioner, der er forbundet med S3i-initiativets separate portefølje.

Som det klart fremgår af den strategiske plan, vil UNOPS ikke længere foretage nogen form for direkte investeringer fra sine reserver. Så S3i-aktiviteter vil ikke være en del af vores fremtidige arbejde.
Notatet giver information om, hvordan beslutninger om nye engagementer træffes. Det fremhæver også påtænkte foranstaltninger til yderligere sikkerhed for, at porteføljen forbliver inden for mandatet.

Jeg håber, at I med denne omfattende analyse af forankringen af UNOPS-porteføljen i det oprindelige mandat, kombineret med den omformulerede strategiske plan, er forsikret om, at UNOPS fuldt ud har forstået og internaliseret det klare budskab og forventning om, at vi fokuserer vores nuværende og fremtidige arbejde på det oprindelige mandat.
Den 25. januar 2024 arrangerer vi en uformel EB-briefing om UNOPS mandat og portefølje. For at lette samtalen er I meget velkommen til at sende eventuelle skriftlige spørgsmål til PortfolioQ@unops.org senest den 15. januar 2024.

Ad 3: Skift i organisationskulturNotatet, der er sendt til EB, er vores (første) svar på den uafhængige KPMG-vurdering af organisationskultur ved UNOPS . Denne vurdering viste, at UNOPS' forpligtelse til at levere i vanskelige sammenhænge har påvirket kulturen, som vi nu søger at justere.

KPMG's gennemgang indeholdte også anbefalinger relateret til tonen fra den øverste ledelse, gennemsigtighed og kommunikation, ansvarlighed, investering i personale og fremtidssikret kultur. 

Jeg vil gerne bemærke, at vi siden midten af 2022 allerede har igangsat meget betydelige strategiske transformationer gennem reformer fokuseret på strateginulstilling, ansvarlighedsforbedringer, procesforbedringer og personaleinvesteringer. Disse er opsummeret i noten til EB for at minde om, at dette er en rejse, som vi allerede har startet.

I erkendelse af, at kultur initieres i toppen, testes i midten og leves i bunden, vil vi bruge en iterativ 3-trins organisationskulturmodel med fokus på adfærd, processer og incitamenter, der styrker det kulturelle skift - hvilket vil tage tid.

Prioriterede initiativer inden for de fem hovedindsatsområder vil være:
Tone fra toppen: kommunikation til inspiration for kulturændringer; tilskynde til samarbejde mellem hovedkvarter og regioner for at fjerne siloer; indlejre FN-værdier i adfærd på alle niveauer, forenet af UNOPS-kerneværdier.Ansvarlighed: udvikle og implementere en ny adfærdskodeks; forny whistleblowing mekanisme; forbedre ansvarlighed og designe lederskabskompetencer.Gennemsigtighed og åben kommunikation: udvikle en ny kommunikationsstrategi for at styrke forventet adfærd; forstærke beskeder gennem flere kanaler; styrke personaleengagementet; udnævne kulturændringsambassadører.Investering i mennesker: opdatere HR-politikker for at styrke forventet adfærd; reform af præstationsstyringscyklus; styrke interne klage processer, støtte til ofre og engagement; udforme og lancere en mobilitetspolitik.Fremtidssikret kultur: definere værdier, der repræsenterer ønsket kultur; genkende og belønne konsekvent demonstration af ønsket adfærd og fejre succeser; muliggør åbne feedback-steder; løbende måle udviklingen af kulturskiftet.For at facilitere denne kulturelle transformation har vi oprettet et nyt kontor med fokus specifikt på Organisationskultur og Engagement, som vil blive støttet af en ekstern konsulent.

Selvom denne note hovedsageligt identificerer "hvad" der skal arbejdes med i den langsigtede kulturelle transformation, mangler vi endnu at definere "hvordan" for mange områder. Dette vil ske i løbet af 2024 - da jeg er sikker på, at vi vil skulle drøfte dette emne igen i EB i de kommende måneder og år.
Ad 4: Fordeling af den overskydende reserveVi har det seneste år arbejdet hårdt på at fordele de overskydende midler fra reserve. Det har ikke været en nem proces - for os eller for vores +250 partnere. Ud af de 124 millioner USD i den overskydende reserve modtog vi instruktioner for i alt 95 millioner USD og formåede at udbetale USD 92 millioner. Det svarer til 76% af det samlede beløb, der skal refunderes pr. 12. december 2023.
Vi er ret stolte af denne præstation i betragtning af kompleksiteten. Især da beregningerne og processen blev fuldt valideret i den uafhængige Deloitte-gennemgang. Vi håber derfor, at denne proces har været endnu et skridt i retning af at genopbygge tilliden til UNOPS.

Fordelingen af de overskydende reserver har været særlig vanskelig for projekter med flere partnere, nogle med hundredvis af partnere involveret. Derudover var der i nogle tilfælde tale om lån fra internationale finansielle institutioner, hvilket også gav unikke udfordringer. Vi har brugt en betydelig mængde tid og ressourcer på at udrede de finansielle strømme og juridiske aftaler for disse engagementer. Da det også er første gang for os, har det taget os og partnerne noget tid.
Dette har også betydet, at vi ikke havde tid til at engagere os tilstrækkeligt med alle partnere, især dem med ret små kuverter. Derudover er vi stadig i dialog med mange partnere om at finde konkrete løsninger på deres individuelle kompleksitet.
I bestyrelsesdokumentet, der vil blive præsenteret for EB i en uformel session den 18. januar 2023, præsenterer vi 5 muligheder for, hvordan man håndterer de resterende midler.
Som forberedelse til næste bestyrelsesmøde vil vi også sende et supplement til ovenstående bestyrelsesdokument med en oversigt over alle partnere og beløb, for hvilke vi ikke har modtaget instruktioner om hvor midlerne skal overføres til.
For at kunne håndtere kompleksiteten og de resterende partnerengagementer, foreslår vi at forlænge fristen for fordeling af 2021-overskudsreserven med et år - indtil udgangen af 2024. Det vil give tilstrækkelig tid til os og for vores mange partnere. Det vil også sikre ligebehandling af de partnere, der ikke er repræsenteret i direktionen.
Ad 5: UNBOA anbefalinger
I 2022 modtog UNOPS en ukvalificeret (ren) revisionspåtegning fra UNBOA , hvori det anføres, at: "Efter vores opfattelse giver det medfølgende regnskab retvisende, i alle væsentlige henseender, UNOPS' finansielle stilling pr. 31. december 2022 og dets økonomiske resultater. og pengestrømme for det år, der sluttede, i overensstemmelse med International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS).
Med hensyn til anbefalinger fra UNBOA har vi 31 åbne anbefalinger ved udgangen af regnskabsåret 2022. 12 af disse anbefalinger er for 2021 og tidligere perioder.
Ved udgangen af regnskabsåret 2023 forventer vi, at 19 ud af 31 anbefalinger er implementeret. Det svarer til en implementeringsrate på 61%. 11 ud af de 31 anbefalinger anses for at have høj prioritet.

Vi indsender vores regnskab for 2023 den 31. marts 2024. Revisionsberetningen forventes at blive udsendt i juli 2024 og at være offentlig tilgængelig i september 2024.

Specifikt om personale-kontraktmodaliteter
Vi har foretaget en omfattende gennemgang af kontraktmodaliteter for at efterleve UNBOA-anbefalingen om at få de stillinger, der indebærer "iboende FN-aktiviteter", udført af fastansat personale.

Den første fase af projektet fokuserede på at konvertere alle forretningskritiske roller til tidsubegrænsede ansættelser inden januar 2024. Ved udgangen af januar 2024 vil alle forretningskritiske roller (hvor der ikke eksisterer nogen præstationsproblemer) være blevet konverteret til tidsubegrænsede ansættelsesstillinger.

Projektet har øget vores medarbejderstab med 167 stillinger, hvor 107 afspejles i 2023 og 60 flere i fremtiden.

Vi arbejder konstant på at optimere vores arbejdsstyrke ved at finde den rette balance mellem FN-medarbejdere og kontraktansættelser. I den forbindelse er det afgørende at anerkende den fortsatte relevans af begge typer kontrakter (FN-personale og kontraktansættelser), som afspejler de mange forskellige omstændigheder, som vi opererer under og især vores projektbaserede forretningsmodel.

Jeg håber, at denne - lange og omfattende - information har været en hjælp i jeres forberedelser forud for den kommende EB-session.
Til sidst ønsker jeg jer og jeres kære en rigtig glædelig juleferie! Jeg ser meget frem til vores fortsatte samarbejde næste år!
Varmeste hilsener,Asbjørn

Subject: Notes from ED meeting with Sweden's Deputy Permanent Representative, 22. January 2023
Body:
Dear colleagues, 
Earlier today Jorge met with the Swedish Deputy Permanent Representative (Mr. Andreas von Uexküll) accompanied by ECOSOC ambassador (Ms.Charlotta Schlyter) and the caseworker (Ms. Anna Svensson). 
The Swedish DPR pointed out that progress in recovering missing S3i funds and especially holding individuals responsible for the mismanagement were important points for Sweden. They therefore encouraged UNOPS to facilitate a confidential briefing done by OLA and UNOPS and to elaborate on how findings in the forensic audit would be handled. 
Sweden appreciated Jorge's reassurance that UNOPS would stick to its original mandate as this had also been a grave concern for Stockholm.   
The Swedish DPR pointed out that the UNOPS management focus shifting the organisational culture and asked which concrete action points would be prioritized out of the many on the list presented. The staff surveys showed there was still a very long way to go to address the many personnel problems. Jorge reiterated the many cultural changes in the past 1.5 years and encouraged Member States to help shift the narrative about UNOPS away from crisis mode to focusing on the work being done on the ground. This would also help UNOPS colleagues who were just doing their jobs - and should not be blamed for past mistakes. 
Finally, upon a question from the Swedish DPR, Jorge explained the role of UNOPS in relation to Sigrid Kaag's new position in Gaza. 
***
Jorge initially complimented Sweden's active role in the Executive Board sessions which showed that they took the role very seriously. Sweden had been instrumental in getting UNOPS back in shape. Now only a few action points remained from the Comprehensive Response Plan which related to culture, risk and digitalisation. Jorge also underlined that UNOPS would continue reforming even beyond the CPR. Especially the culture shift would require special attention and it would take time. 
Jorge also pointed out that UNOPS experienced an increasing demand from partners. For example UNOPS was hired for the Santiago network and to operationalise Sigrid Kaag's office in relation to the situation in Gaza. 
Jorge mentioned that he would have liked to speak directly with the Secretary of State in Stockholm to clarify any questions or outstanding Swedish concerns.   
The DPR appreciated the direct outreach and presented 3 questions / comments to UNOPS:  From a Swedish perspective, accountability remained a key issue to be handled. It was important that the people involved in mismanagement in relation to S3i would be held accountable, and Sweden wanted to know when and how this would be handled - as the forensic audit would be taken forward.  Recovering the missing S3i funds was also a key issue and Sweden wanted to know how the work to recover the missing funds would be intensified.  Finally Sweden reiterated the request for more information on the investigation progress. They hoped that UNOPS could facilitate a confidential session together with OLA as a prolonged process would make matters even worse for all. Jorge agreed that it would be good to have a confidential briefing by OLA but could not promise such. UNOPS was in a difficult position where Jorge was getting all the questions while OLA was the unit in charge of the investigation. Jorge had spoken with OLA to try to facilitate a confidential briefing. 
With regards to holding individual persons accountable, Jorge recalled that almost all senior managers had been replaced in the past 1.5 years. 
Jorge underlined that everything UNOPS was currently doing was clearly within the original mandate - which was non-programmatic. This was appreciated by the DRP as this had also been a great concern for Sweden.  
The DPR then pointed out that the organisational culture shift was an important task for UNOPS and the KPMG recommendations should be taken seriously. The staff surveys were informative but the results showed that UNOPS still had a very long way to go. The responsibility for addressing the staff issues was clearly with the UNOPS management. Although Sweden appreciated the many changes in the past 1.5 years and the many initiatives presented, Sweden asked which key initiatives would be prioritised from the very long list.  
Jorge reiterated that although there were no silver bullet to fix the culture, many key issues had already been fixed. For example separation of powers between two DED, de-central decision makings and the involvement of regional directors in the management team. But other issues would go beyond that. 
To sincerely change the organisational culture at UNOPS Jorge needed the help of Member States to change the narrative away from the crisis of the past. UNOPS staff was not to blame for a few individuals' misconduct so the narrative about UNOPS should focus on the work being done on the ground - which they should be proud of.  
Asbjørn explained that HR colleagues had been analysing "what" issues had to be addressed and were now working hard on "how" to address the issues with specific actions which would be presented to Member States at a later stage. 
Jorge pointed out that he did not find the continued critique of UNOPS to be fair. A lot had been done and a massive amount of reforms had been pushed through to address the issues. But still too much time was being spent on talking about the past which prevented UNOPS from moving on, and maintained the culture focus on past crisis. This was especially unfair to colleagues in the field who were just doing their job. Jorge hoped that Swedish colleagues in Stockholm would understand this and that he would be given an opportunity to speak with the State Secretary at some point.  
The DPR pointed to the Swedish government's zero tolerance for fraud and misconduct which was the reason behind the tough Swedish stance. The DPR assured Jorge about the Swedish recognition of the good work done by UNOPS colleagues on the ground.  
The DPR then asked for Jorge to elaborate about UNOPS' work with Sigrid Kaag in relation to Gaza - and what Member States could do to help. Jorge explained UNOPS' role and asked that Member States push for a ceasefire and independent verifications at the border - or at least a less restrictive approach by the Israelis as way too many items were rejected. 

/Asbjørn

SDC is interested in supporting the Access Support Unit (ASU) with a contribution of CHF 720K.
UNOPS office is in discussion with the SDC office in Jerusalem, Ms Sabina Handschin (sabina.handschin@eda.admin.ch
First Secretary, Development Cooperation & Humanitarian Aid in the Swiss Reps office about Potential funding)
SDC have shared with UNOPS the global agreement between UNOPS and Switzerland and there are TWO main points that we would like to discuss further and see how they can be adapted in the agreement to fit the purpose/nature of the ASU being a highly political multi-donor project.
The two points are the following:
1) The UNOPS indirect cost: The agreement stipulates an indirect fee of  3%. Body:
Dear Martin
Greetings from chilly Geneva - I hope this finds you well. Further to my previous email on this subject, I wanted to quickly follow up - and I would be happy to have a call this week if that's easier for you.
As you know SDC is interested in supporting the Access Support Unit (ASU) for Gaza with a contribution of CHF 625,000.Our local UNOPS office is in discussion with Ms Sabina Handschin (sabina.handschin@eda.admin.ch First Secretary, Development Cooperation & Humanitarian Aid in the Swiss Reps office in Jerusalem) in this regard. 
As you know, we have our global agreement in place between UNOPS and Switzerland, however, there are two points that we would like to discuss further to see how they can be adapted to fit the purpose/nature of the ASU, being a highly political, multi-donor project.
1) The UNOPS indirect cost: 
The agreement stipulates an indirect fee of 3%. However, the ASU is a multi-donor project with a fixed management fee of 7% for all partners. As we have seen in other agreements it is critical that we maintain a harmonized approach with all the donors, and have one budget for the project to maximise efficiencies in both management and reporting.To make the change, we would need SDC approval in writing to apply the 7% as mentioned in the related clause in the agreement (I believe we did this in our Serbia agreement).
2) The requirement for an evaluationConsidering the multi-donor nature of this support and the political context, any evaluation would require the buy-in of all donors under the leadership of UNSCO/UNOCHA, and the agreement on the intent/purpose of such an evaluation. This will require elaborate discussions with the relevant stakeholders, the timing for which might not be the best considering the ongoing conflict and access dynamics. All this would delay the conclusion of this very time sensitive funding agreement. We would suggest removing this evaluation from the agreement while relying on a continued flow of project monitoring data. Alternatively, while not ideal, we could agree with you on a 'lighter' mid-term review. 
Looking forward to hearing from you soon.All best wishesLouise

Hi all, 
Yesterday afternoon, Luke, Kelsey and myself met with Joe Lightfoot and Hannah Mozley from FCDO communications team. 
In short, FDCO is keen to do a joint-communications effort on the work of the Access Support Unit (ASU). 
We highlighted that while we too are keen, that we would have to seek guidance from OCHA on any final product and also that we could not focus solely on a single donor on what is a multi-donor project. This point was accepted (with some caveats)
FCDO’s ideas were in two areas: digital and press. 
DigitalProduce a video to be shared across FCDO social media channels as well as their minister’s own social media channels;UNOPS would also post footage across our social media channels;The video would focus on telling the story of how the project is helping on-the-ground. Although, specifics will have to be developed further once we know what footage we can gather;This could include b-roll footage from our work together in Gaza (but this would need to be gathered by UNOPS team on the ground);This could be mixed with a piece-to-camera of one or more individuals working directly on the project or similar project spokesperson close to the operationPotentially, it could also include comment from key people in FCDO (such as the British Foreign Secretary) and UNOPS Executive Director - especially focussing on Jorge’s thoughts following his recent mission to Gaza but their primary focus is on what is happening on the groundFCDO already has some footage, but this is only up until the border. They do not have any footage from inside Gaza;
PressFCDO would like a key UNOPS spokesperson (suggested Jorge) to potentially be available for interviews on flagship UK television and radio shows (such as BBC Breakfast and ITV’s Good Morning Britain);We highlighted that this could be possible, but would depend on the exact subject and we also made the point that if  the ASU project and the UK’s contribution to it should be referenced, then this would likely require endorsement from the multi-donor group as part of an agreed comms planFCDO also asked what the appetite would be to organise an international press team to come and visit the project on the ground for a tour. We highlighted the immediate sensitivities and challenges around such a visit, but we agreed we would bring it back to colleagues for further discussion. (It may be possible, for example, to connect a local spokesperson with a BBC correspondent on the ground)
TimelineFCDO are keen to move quicker rather than slower. They asked if we could provide an update to them by the end of the week?

Looking forward to hearing your feedback from our discussions. 
Best, 
Tom.

Subject: Project 2023-23202 / 24129. Progress Arkas Gymnasium
Body:
Dear Franciska,

I trust this mail finds you well.

I am writing to inform you about the progress of our work at the Arkas Gymnasium.

As you know, UNOPS decided to divide the complete restoration design into three phases: 1) long-term stabilization of the building, 2) installation of shelter, and 3) restoration of the interior of the building. 

The most urgent part is the stabilization of the building with the aim to prevent it from collapsing. Dividing the design into three phases allows us to work on the stabilization implementation without waiting for the complete design to be finished (and for the funding to be secured).

We have completed the design for the stabilization process, and our quality assurance group is currently reviewing it. We are also currently gathering all relevant information to begin the procurement process shortly. We are working to start implementing stabilization works at the beginning of Q2.

I want to highlight that during one of our periodic monitoring visits at the end of January, our engineering team noticed that the left wall of the main entrance has continued to slightly displace, which increases the risk of collapsing. 

To prepare for the stabilization works, and in addition to ensuring the safety of the area in case of a potential collapse of the wall, we have taken the following actions:

As discussed, the whole area of the main entrance will be closed off for any unauthorized access by setting up a fence in line with city regulations/fencing requirements (expected to be in place next week).A formal letter has been sent to the Mykolaiv Town Hall to request permission to place the fence, which will close the area.Every week, the wall will be measured by our engineering team to closely monitor any further displacement. 
This risk pertains to the health and safety considerations of the project, and we are taking all necessary measures to ensure that no persons are in danger. 

I will continue to update you on any developments, and as you know, you are always more than welcome to reach out for any follow-up inquiries. 

I look forward to catching up with you when it suits you, and I would also be happy to elaborate on the progress made so far, the mitigating measures taken, and the planned next steps. 

Best,
Teresa

Subject: Italy's Piano Mattei for Africa
Body:
Dear colleagues,As you may know, on 29 January Italy (current Presidency of the G7) held the Italy-Africa Summit in Rome, gathering 25 Leaders from Africa.The so-called Piano Mattei was launched.---Here is a summary:It includes 5.5 BIL EUR of which 3 BIL EUR from the Italian Climate fund and 2,5 BIL EUR from the Cooperation to Development fund. The idea is also to mobilize more funds through the Banks (Cassa Depositi e Prestiti, EIB etc.), the EU and other donors.PILOT PROJECTS IN 9 COUNTRIES - At least 9 African countries are involved in pilot projects: Morocco, Tunisia, Algeria, Egypt, Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Kenya, Democratic Republic of Congo and Mozambique.EDUCATION AND TRAINING - The Plan intends to promote the training of teachers, the launch of new professional courses in line with the needs of the labor market and collaboration with companies, involving in particular Italian operators and exploiting the Italian SMEs mode. For example, the Prime Minister announced the creation in Morocco of "a large center of excellence for professional training on the topic of renewable energy", while in Tunisia, a structural reform of schools and exchanges between students and teachers are planned as early as 2024.
AGRICULTURE - The aim is to reduce malnutrition rates, encourage the development of agri-food chains, support the development of non-fossil bio-fuels. For Algeria "a project of satellite monitoring on agriculture" is planned; in Mozambique "an agri-food center that enhances the excellence and export of local products", while in Egypt the Plan intends to "support in an area which is 200 kilometers far from Alessandria the production of wheat, soya, corn and sunflower, with investments in machinery, seeds, technologies and new cultivation methods".HEALTH - The Plan aims at strengthening health systems, improving the accessibility and quality of primary maternal and child services (objective of a project in Côte d'Ivoire), to strengthen local capacities in terms of management of health personnel and research; develop strategies for preventing and containing health threats, in particular pandemics and natural disasters.ENERGY - It is one of the central sectors of the Plan with the aim of making Italy an energy hub, a bridge between Europe and Africa, as with "the Elmed electrical interconnection between Italy and Tunisia and the new corridor for the transport of hydrogen from North Africa to Central Europe via Italy". The climate-energy connection is central, with interventions to strengthen energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy. It is a commitment that will also include the development of technologies applied to energy and innovation centers, where Italian companies will be able to select local start-ups and thus support employment. This pillar includes "an initiative in Kenya dedicated to the development of the biofuels supply chain, which aims to involve up to approximately 400 thousand farmers by 2027".WATER - The interventions include the drilling of wells, powered by photovoltaic systems, and investments in distribution networks. For example, one of the projects for DRC involves the "construction of wells and water distribution networks, especially for agricultural purposes, powered exclusively by renewable energy", while in Ethiopia there will be "water purification interventions".———I suggest that you reach out to the Embassies/AICS offices in the listed countries and see how you could help.I know some of you are already well positioned but please let us know as we could support also through our current outreach to the Banks.Please keep us in the loop so that we can further support at our bestArrivederciCarmenMariacarmen Colitti | Head of Office and Representative | Partnerships and Liaison Group | Brussels Liaison Office | Brussels, Belgium | Tel: + 32 2 7881840| www.unops.org Keep up-to-date with UNOPS. Subject: 🇯🇵 Official launch of the UNOPS Japan Parliamentary Association 🇯🇵
Body:
Colleagues,
In Tokyo, earlier this week, we held the inaugural meeting of the UNOPS Parliamentary Association in Japan. The main objective of this bipartisan group is to raise UNOPS’ profile with key decision makers (Parliamentarians and senior officials) and demonstrate how we can contribute to advancing Japan’s foreign policy objectives. The President of the Association is Mr. Gen Nakatani, former Defense Minister of Japan and the PM’s former advisor on international human rights issues. The Secretary-General is Mr. Kiyoto Tsuji, State Minister for Foreign Affairs. 
On the bureaucracy side, we were pleased to see that all major ministries were represented: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA), Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), and Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI).
This inaugural meeting allowed us to present UNOPS’ business model and value proposition and update the group on our recent work in Gaza, Ukraine and Myanmar. There was particular interest when we highlighted that, for the last three years, UNOPS is the UN agency that procures the most products from Japanese companies. There were several interventions and questions from parliamentarians asking MOFA why UNOPS was not used more regularly by the Government in order to fulfill Japan’s foreign policy and international development priorities. 
The next meeting is planned for June 2024, and we aim to have official meetings every six months. In this regard, we are hoping DEDs, RDs and other UNOPS leaders will be able to share their work with the group- depending on interests.
UNICEF, UNHCR, WFP and the World Bank (to name a few) established parliamentary associations in Japan several years ago and they have become key forums for discussion. We are confident this new association will allow us to better position UNOPS with this important partner. Finally, this  milestone for us in Japan comes as a result of the Tokyo Liaison Office’s two years of engagements with parliamentarians which culminated with Jorge’s visit last November. 
Thank you Yuko and the TLO team for getting us here! Thank you Jorge for coming last November to ensure we were able to seal the deal! 
Émilie

Subject: FN Byens høringssvar
Body:
Hej Julia, 
Som kort nævnt g.d. har regeringen fremsendt lovforslag om ændring af udlændingeloven og lov om danskuddannelse, jf. høringsportalen her. 
Lovændringen har til formål at lempe visse krav for familiesammenføring for udlandsdanskere som vender hjem til Danmark efter en årrække i udlandet. 
Lovændringen tager dog desværre ikke højde for, at danske statsborgere ansat ved FN ikke automatisk har ret til at vende hjem til Danmark efter endt tjeneste sammen med deres familie, såfremt ægtefællen ikke er dansk statsborger. I sådanne tilfælde vil den udenlandske ægtefælle gennemføre opholdstilladelsesprøver ligesom der er krav om økonomisk sikkerhedsstillelse. Endvidere er der risiko for, at en evt. opholdstilladelse til den udenlandske ægtefælle frafaldes i tilfælde af den danske ægtefælles død.  
Reglerne gør det derfor vanskeligt og risikofyldt for danske FN-ansatte, der er gift med en udenlandsk ægtefælle, at vende hjem til Danmark med deres familier efter endt tjeneste ved FN. Den usikre retstilstand på området mindsker incitamentet for danskere til at gøre tjeneste ved FN – og dermed udøve dansk indflydelse i FN.  
FN Byen foreslår derfor, danske statsborgere efter endt tjeneste ved FN i minimum 4 år, har ret til at vende hjem til Danmark sammen med deres udenlandske ægtefælle og børn, uden krav om prøver og sikkerhedsstillelse for udstedelse af permanent opholdstilladelse i Danmark. FN Byen foreslår endvidere, at opholdstilladelsen ikke bortfalder ved den danske ægtefælles død.
Jeg vedlægger t.o. vores fremsendte høringssvar til lovforslaget.

Subject: RE: Feeder roads proposal


 
Dear Piotr,
 
Thank you for this information. We would be definitively interested in the opportunity of accessing new funding for a feeder roads project in South Sudan. Such a project would be particularly useful for a number
 of reasons listed below. Moreover, connectivity infrastructure particularly in rural areas is something the country really needs.
 
-     
Such a project will continue and consolidate our ongoing (but soon to be completed) projects supporting feeder roads and access roads construction, in particular the one implemented by UNOPS;
-     
It will complement the activities envisaged under the new Green and Resilient Economy package (cca. EUR 80 million) that we will be contracting in the course of next year (and/or in 2025); as we want to
 focus as much as possible on boosting productivity as well as value chains, value addition, private sector development and market led growth, it is obvious that roads providing access to markets and facilitating interaction between farmers and other stakeholders
 would have a positive impact; in our current thinking for the above mentioned EUR 80 million package we would have not prioritised new feeder roads because the constructions costs are increasing and would deviate too many resources from other much needed priority
 activities; but having new funding for new feeder roads would be very useful because the needs in the country are high;
-     
As for the ongoing projects, a new project will consolidate linkages with the envisaged regional corridor 11 which is a Global gateway priority (maybe the only Global gateway related activities we can
 realistically envisage in South Sudan).
 
One important element that will greatly facilitate the success of a possible new feeder roads project is our positive relationship with UNOPS. I have discussed with the and they would be ready to engage in a
 new project should we receive the greenlight. Under our ongoing project they have built infrastructure of good quality and their work is appreciated also by the government and local authorities and communities. Initially, under the ongoing projects, some locations
 have been identified and preparations conducted, including design and review documentation produced. Yet, because the increased costs of feeder roads construction, not all the envisaged kilometres of roads could be constructed. With a new project that could
 be done rather quickly as preparatory work is already done. That could be a quick start and then new locations could be identified. Moreover, various teams of experts are already involved in the ongoing project and they could be easily and quickly transitioned
 to work under a new project.
 
UNOPS projects include to a certain extent cash for work and local workers are hired either directly by UNOPS or by contractors. Returnees could be included in such cash for work schemes and in that regard the
 project could benefit from the experience of another UNOPS implemented program on social protection that is active in Greater Bahr el-Ghazal, Upper Nile and Unity state.
 
For information, under the ongoing project, the average cost per kilometre for a 4.5 meters wide road has been 151.000 USD and for a 6 meters  wide road, including drainage structures, has been around 211.000
 USD. Most likely, the current costs would be higher, about 20% higher. Sill, if we could mobilise a substantial amount, as you indicated, ranging from EUR 20 to 50 million we could do significant work and that would be worthwhile .
 
Please let u know what are the next steps and what is expected from the Delegation (and by when). We stand ready.
 
Best regards,


Gabriel

INVITATION 

Kick-off: Regeringens arbejde med styrket engagement i Afrika
11. marts 2024
  
Verden er i hastig forandring, og partnerskaber og dialog er vigtigere end nogen sinde før i en geopolitisk brydningstid. Regeringens udenrigs- og sikkerhedspolitiske
 strategi fremhæver, at Europas vægt i verden mindskes, mens andre lande og regioner vokser både økonomisk, befolkningsmæssigt og teknologisk. Det gælder også i Afrika, et kontinent i vækst, som både rummer et stort potentiale og omfattende udfordringer.

 
Over de kommende måneder vil regeringen derfor stille skarpt på hvordan Danmarks og EU’s engagement med afrikanske partnere kan styrkes. Regeringen vil udarbejde
 en plan for dansk engagement i Afrika, der skal styre Danmarks indsats, og analysere hvordan der kan sikres stærkere samtænkning og styrkelse af danske tiltag gennem EU. Planen forventes lanceret i sommeren 2024. Målet er stærkere og mere ligeværdige partnerskaber
 for en bedre fælles fremtid. 
 
I den forbindelse inviterer Udenrigsministeriet til et kick-off arrangement, som vil finde sted
mandag d. 11. marts kl. 10:15-12:15 i Dronningesalen, Den Sorte Diamant.
 
Her vil statsministeren, udenrigsministeren og ministeren for udviklingssamarbejde og global klimapolitik præsentere overvejelserne for arbejdet. Afrikanske partnere
 forventes også at deltage i dialogen under arrangementet. 
 
Issa Jeppesen vil moderere arrangementet, herunder en paneldebat, der vil berøre, hvordan Danmark kan arbejde for ligeværdige partnerskaber med afrikanske lande,

INVITATION
 
Kick-off: The Danish Government’s approach to strengthened engagement in Africa
11 March 2024
 
The world is rapidly changing, and partnerships and dialogue are more important than ever in a new geopolitical reality. The government’s foreign
 and security policy emphasizes that Europe’s weight in the world is decreasing while other countries and regions are growing economically, population-wise and technologically. This also applies to Africa, a continent in growth with both great potential and
 extensive challenges. 
 
During the course of the coming months, the Danish government will undertake work to determine how Denmark’s and the EU’s engagement with African
 partners can be strengthened. This will lead to the establishment of a plan for strengthened Danish engagement with African partners, which will guide Denmark’s efforts going forward, including by analysing how stronger synergies between strengthened Danish
 actions and EU actions can be promoted. The plan is expected to be launched in the summer of 2024 with the aim of supporting stronger and more equal partnerships for a better shared future.

 
In relation to this, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs invites you to a kick-off event, which will take place on
Monday, March 11, from 10:15-12:15 in Dronningesalen, The Black Diamond. 
 
The Prime Minister, the Minister for Foreign Affairs, and the Minister for Development Cooperation and Global Climate Policy will present the Government’s
 reflections on the work ahead. High-level representation from invited African partners is also expected at the event.

 
The event will be moderated by journalist Issa Jeppesen, which will include a panel debate that will reflect upon how Denmark can work for strengthening
 equal partnerships with African countries, including through the EU. Participants are expected to include a wide range of relevant actors, including international organizations, business representatives, think tanks and civil society organizations. 

 
This is not a personal invitation, and it will thus be possible to pass the invitation to a colleague, if you are prevented from participating.

on this site in the days leading up to the event.
 
Kindly confirm your attendance

here at the latest on 4th of march.
 
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is collaborating with ARENA, the event department of Altinget on the organization of the conference.
 
Sincerely,
Department for Africa, Development Policy, and Financing (AFRPOL)

Body:
Dear Marianne, 
Thank you very much for your questions and your patience with us. 
Please find below responses to your queries. If you have time, I would suggest that you and I briefly touch base tomorrow on the next steps. When would it be convenient for you? 

Q1: Will this project be registered as a separate project through the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine or whether it has already been registered as part of a multi-donor program.UNOPS registers projects following signing of a donor agreement; WFP does not register separately but the project will sit within the WFP/Gov Interim Country Strategic Plan (ICSP).
Q2: Since our meeting in January, we have decided to allocate DKK 40 million to a multilateral partner and DKK 35 million as part of a civil society call for proposals. We consider this to be an initial allocation to a multi-annual engagement in mine action. Please let us know whether the allocation size for 2024 would result in any changes to the received proposal.The figure of DKK 40m is less than anticipated and therefore the project will have a scaled back ambition of outputs in the short term. We welcome the consideration that this may be multi-year engagement and therefore this reduced allocation will provide a strong platform for further implementation which will be more effective in terms of measuring mine action outcomes.

We would suggest to provide you with an updated and concrete proposal with scaled back output based on the reduced allocation, in which we can lay the foundation for a multi-year engagement with increased outputs as a result. 

Q3: Kindly let us know whether there would be any reservations at your end in terms of allocating funding through the UN Community Fund, which we are currently considering.While we greatly appreciate the idea of channelling funds via the UN Community Funds, this would add timelies, administrative burden and management fees. As a donor you would therefore end up paying a higher fee. Therefore we would suggest channeling the funds directly to UNOPS and WFP thereby getting more value for your money.

Q4: What is the anticipated geographical split between Mykolaiv and other regions (Kharkiv) for this project?Implementation will be in Mykolaiv only for this specific project but can of course be widened in a multi-year engagement upon your requests. 

Q5: Are there any updates with regards to funding from other donors?We suggest that this specific engagement will only be sponsored by Denmark - contributing to Denmark's visibility and engagement in the Mykolaiv region. 

UNOPS will soon sign an agreement with Italy for Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) capability in Mykolaiv region, to include a capacity development component with the National Police of Ukraine (NPU). 

WFP and FAO have several donors at the national level, including Croatia, France, Finland and Norway. These funds are not earmarked for a specific oblast but funds will be drawn on to complement Danish support to address objectives under this proposal. How this will be specifically allocated is yet to be defined.

Q6: Could you provide for further details as to how this programme will align to agricultural cycles and seasonal deadlines (sowing, harvesting etc.). When is clearance of contaminated land expected to be cleared for farming and at what stage are involved farmers informed of the de-mining timeline? When do you expect that land confirmed as being uncontaminated to be released?The mobilisation and implementation of the project will not see benefits for the spring planting season; the outputs from the land release components will be generated in Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 (subject to the signing of the agreement during Q1 2024). This will benefit winter crops in 2024. Targeted households and farms may also receive cash and other context-specific support under Phase 3 to off-set losses caused by explosive contamination and help to prepare for the resumption of cultivation activities. Targeted households and farms will be informed of the mine action timelines according to priorities established under Phase 1.

Q7: We understand that the FSD will be the main implementing partner. Kindly confirm that this understanding is correct and to what extent they are accredited to carry out the various stages of mine action.No. FSD is an implementing partner in Kharkiv Oblast under the wider WFP/FAO project. WFP will engage a separate international partner for mine action in Mykolaiv as well as a partner for the livelihood component. In addition, UNOPS will be considering other national partners for the mine action component.

Q8: Who are the national NGOs/companies mentioned as preferred partner to deliver on selected land release priorities?WFP are considering the accredited international NGOs HALO Trust, MAG and/or Norwegian People’s Aid but are open to deconflict with any decisions regarding Danish support through the civil society component of your planned support. UNOPS are viewing national implementing partners to include Demining Solutions (DS), Ukrainian Demining Association (UDA) and Ukroboronservice.

Best regards,Guy, Charles, David, Aleksandra and Asbjørn

Subject: Oplæg til debat mellem UM'en og UNOPS ED på Folkemødet
Body:
Kære Rikke og Julia, 
Som tidligere kort drøftet, tænker vi at en debat mellem udenrigsministeren og Jorge på Folkemødet kunne være en god mulighed for at øge den generelle opmærksomhed på FN's stærke tilstedeværelse i Danmark - ligesom det kunne være en mulighed for at I kan pege på danske prioriteter ifm. jeres kandidatur til FN's Sikkerhedsråd i 2025. 
Samtidigt kunne det være en mulighed for en offentlig debat om FN's rolle i en forandret verden, hvor der er stigende udfordringer med bæredygtighed, klimaforandringer, humanitære kriser, finansiering, konflikter osv. - hvor vi forhåbentligt også kan engagere publikum en smule. 
Med henblik på at facilitere en sådan debat, har vi udarbejdet dette udkast til en konceptnote for debatten, som vi vil foreslå at vi pitcher til hovedscenen på Folkemødet. Konceptnoten er blot et første udkast, som ikke er clearet hele vejen rundt i FN-Byen. Sender den derfor til jer nu, med henblik på at få jeres uformelle input så vi sammen sikrer at vi rammer skiven ift. vores chefer. 
Jeg vil derfor sætte stor pris på at modtage jeres feedback, forslag til justeringer mv. til oplægget. Når vi på kontorniveau er blevet enige om et udkast, kan vi parallelt cleare i vores respektive huse. 
Flemming og jeg står naturligvis også til rådighed hvis vi lige skal drøfte mundtligt. 
Jeg ser meget frem til at høre fra jer.

Dear Louise,
 
Thanks again for the discussion yesterday.

 
I just wanted to follow up on the meeting that we were suggesting organizing between 17 and 30 April and check if you have been able to coordinate with your colleagues so that we
 can agree on a date. 
 
Following yesterday’s discussion and the comments on the time that this negotiation is taking, I wanted to take the opportunity to re-affirm our commitment to get this LFA agreement
 over the line as showed throughout our constant engagement and follow up to finalize this contract before the end of the extension.
 
As you will recall Maia sent the LFA agreement with our comments on 17 January and a meeting had been scheduled on 19 January but was canceled by UNOPS.
We then met on 1 February at the GHC and the following day Maia sent an email with several slots to discuss the content of the agreement. We got a response from UNOPS on 6 February
 offering to discuss on 13 February. After the 13 February meeting, Maia sent an invite to set up another meeting on 16 February and shared a revised draft contract on 15 February. The meeting was cancelled as Maryam was sick, and Maia followed up on 26 February
 to reschedule the call, which took place yesterday. Unfortunately, no revised draft has been shared by UNOPS since 15 February and the travel policies deviations were only shared on 5 March.
 
For UNOPS and the Global Fund to finalize the agreement shortly, we would be very grateful if UNOPS could share their proposed revisions on the draft agreement ASAP (ideally today
 or by tomorrow COB), and at any rate before we set up another meeting, so that we can expedite the review from our end.
 
Thanks again for your collaboration and support.
 
Best,
 
Hélène

Subject: UNOPS-Danmark projekter til brug for ekstern kommunikation
Body:
Kære Camilla og Gwen 
Tusind tak for god kaffe og snak på Asiatisk Plads og beklager meget mit sene svar. 
Som lovet får I lidt flere info om vores to øvrige igangværende projekter for Danmark. 
1) Rising Nations Initiative: 
På vegne af Danmark, Korea, Italien samt Tyskland og i samarbejde med Tuvalu, Marshalløerne og Kiribati udfører UNOPS projektet Rising Nations Initiatives. Projektet består af tre komplementerende komponenter; forskning, etablering af partnerskaber og advocacy. Det overordnede mål er at bidrage til at beskytte Stillehavslandenes ret og muligheder som selvstændige stater, bevare deres suverænitet og beskytte rettighederne og arven for den berørte befolkning. 
Stillehavslande som Tuvalu står desværre på frontlinjen af den globale klimanødsituation, hvor stigende havniveauer truer deres territorium. På trods af bestræbelser på at rette opmærksomheden mod denne forestående katastrofe er der gjort meget lidt for at modvirke klimaforandringer, og det internationale samfund har heller ikke tilbudt løsninger på de unikke udfordringer, som Stillehavslandene står over for som følge af klimakrisen.
Kontrakten med Danida blev underskrevet i december 2023, og projektet er stadig i startfasen. Jeg vil holde jer opdateret og dele al relevant kommunikationsmateriale med jer.

2) Strategic Advisory and Technical Assistance for the Water and Sanitation  in India with Denmark Government: 
Dette projekt blev kåret som årets projekt ved en intern UNOPS-ceremoni i 2023 og er fuldt ud finansieret af den danske stat. Det er en betydelig anerkendelse, især taget i betragtning af, at UNOPS har over 670 aktive projekter i 163 lande. Projektet blev særligt fremhævet for sit bidrag til ligestillingen. Kønsuligheder er mest markante inden for områderne vand, sanitet og hygiejne (WASH).. Uden ordentlige WASH-tjenester står kvinder og piger over det udbetalte og ekstremt tidskrævende arbejde ved at gå flere kilometer for at hente rent drikkevand. Alt i mens drengene er i skole. Foruden for rent vand har kvinderne også fået en uddannelse i at behandle vand. I Indien bor næsten 900 millioner mennesker i et af landets 600.000 landsbyer på landet. Cirka 45 procent af denne befolkning kan stadig ikke få adgang til sikkert drikkevand. Det svarer til cirka 400 millioner mennesker uden ordentlig adgang til livsvigtige ressourcer. I 2019 iværksatte den indiske regering Jal Jeevan Mission med det formål at sikre tilstrækkeligt, sikkert og pålideligt drikkevand til alle husstande i landsbyerne i Indien inden 2024 gennem installation af fungerende vandhaneforbindelser til husholdningen.På vegne af den danske regering støtter UNOPS Jal Jeevan Mission i Indien ved at yde strategisk, teknisk og uddannelsesmæssig støtte.Arbejdet er fokuseret på 137 landsbyer i delstaten Uttar Pradesh i det nordlige Indien. De mennesker, der bor i denne del af landet, lever i ekstrem fattigdom og står over for alvorlige udfordringer med vandmangel og forurening.
Vi har eksternt kommunikeret om projektet på vores hjemmeside. Jeg synes personligt, at det er en god historie, som på mange måder er Danmarks udviklingspolitiske DNA; den berører ligestilling, klimaet samt rent vand og sanitet. Vi har et hav af kommunikationsmaterialer, hvis I ønsker at kommunikere om den. Projektperioden er frem til marts 2025. 
De bedste hilsener Naimo
--

Subject: Launch of a new, reinforced Danish engagement in Africa: Call for dialogue with Danish embassies
Body:
Dear Dalila and colleagues, 
Yesterday I attended an event that launched the drafting of a new reinforced Danish approach to engagements in Africa - spearheaded by the Danish Prime Minister (Mette Frederiksen), the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Lars Løkke Rasmussen) and the Minister for Development Cooperation and Global Climate (Dan Jørgensen). The kick-off event also featured Kenya's Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr. Musalia Mudavadi) as well as Sierra Leone's Chief Minister (David Sengeh). 
The event marked the initiation of a dialogue with partners that will lead to a new Africa plan for the Danish government - to be finalised by August, 2024. The Danish government has encouraged stakeholders to engage and to inform them about what this new strategy should contain. 
Now is therefore an excellent opportunity to engage in conversations with our local colleagues at the Danish embassies throughout Africa on how UNOPS' capacities can underpin the strengthened Danish engagement. 
At the kick-off event the Prime Minister emphasised that the new Africa strategy must be based on an equal and respectful partnership that took into consideration that Africa consists of 54 individual countries.
The Prime Minister also underlined her own personal engagement with Africa, being one of the only western prime ministers with a master in Africa studies.  
Some of the key topics for the new Africa strategy would likely be: EducationGreen transition Sustainable energyPublic-Private PartnershipsFighting poverty and hungerCreating jobs and growthAs this event marked the launch of the dialogue, I hope that colleagues would use this as an opportunity to approach local Danish embassies and engage in conversations on which areas UNOPS can support. 

My colleague @Naimo HASSAN HIRSI and I remain at your disposal for any further intel on Danish development aid, contact points, tips & tricks, etc. when engaging with the Danes.

Subject: Muligt projekt i Moldova: Håndtering af ukrainske flygtninge
Body:
Kære Anne, Marianne og Jasmin, 
Jeg rækker ud til jer for at flage et mindre projekt i Moldova, som muligvis kunne være i dansk interesse. 
Projektet handler om at hjælpe Moldova med håndteringen af de op mod 1 million flygtninge, som er flygtet fra Ukraine til Moldova siden december 2023. En meget stor andel af de ukrainske flygtninge er udsatte personer, som kræver særlig hjælp. 
Myndighederne i Moldova har meget vanskeligt ved at håndtere situationen, som de ikke har administrativ kapacitet til - endsige den fysiske infrastruktur. Den centrale myndighed udgøres af Generaldirektoratet for Migration ("Inspectorate General for Migration" - GIM) som står for håndteringen af flygtningenes sikkerhed, ansøgningsprocessen osv. 
Generaldirektoratet for Migration har pt. en meget gammel og faldefærdig bygning i Chisinau (se billede øverst i vedlagte), som ikke kan håndtere det voldsomme flygtningepres. Myndighederne i Moldova har derfor bedt om hjælp til at opgradere bygningen for at kunne håndtere flygtningene og sørge for ordentlige faciliteter for dem. 
I samarbejde med Moldovas indenrigsministerium har vi udarbejdet vedlagte konceptnote, som angiver en første fase i et projekt som senere kan udvides til en egentlig opgradering af bygningen. I denne første fase klarlægges de konkrete behov, der udarbejdes optioner for et evt. efterfølgende opgraderingarbejde og der udarbejdes budgetestimater for det efterfølgende genopbygningsarbejde. Altså forarbejdet til en egentlig reparation / udvidelse af Generaldirektoratet for Migration. 
Projektet estimeres til omkring 1-1,2 mio. kr. og kan udføres på ca. 3 måneder, hvorefter der vil forelægge en plan for det efterfølgende konstruktionsarbejde, budget herfor, optioner mv. Men nærværende projekt forpligtiger man sig således ikke til mere end ovenstående - hvorefter en evt. anden (eller flere) donorer vil kunne gennemføre selve konstruktionsarbejdet. 
Jeg håber at projektet muligvis har vakt jeres interesse. Jeg forstår at der er en stor prioritet for regeringen i Moldova. 
Både jeg og vores kolleger i Ukraine og Moldova står naturligvis til jeres rådighed for en evt. opfølgende dialog - såfremt dette kunne have jeres interesse. 
På forhånd mange tak.
