Subject: Ukraine event: Invitation to a high level discussion mine action as the foundation for food Security and resilient infrastructure in Ukraine
Body:
Dear Lesya, 

Please allow me to introduce myself. My name is Naimo Hirsi and I am a Partnerships Analyst in the Northern Europe Liaison Office at the United Nations Office for Project Services, UNOPS. I am reaching out to you together with my colleague Camille Fogtdal, Partnerships and Communications Officer at the United Nations World Food Programme, WFP.

As you know,  February marked two years since Russia’s illegal invasion of Ukraine. The war has caused a severe humanitarian, social and economic crisis with long-term consequences for the Ukrainian people. Today, Ukraine is the most mined country in the world. Landmines and other explosive remnants are designed to inflict maximum harm on victims. They threaten civilians not only physically, but also psychologically and economically.  Crucial infrastructure such as roads, railways, power lines and residential houses have been affected.

We are currently organising an event at Folkemødet - the Danish Democracy Festival in Bornholm, that aims to bring together experts and stakeholders to discuss the threat that landmines and other explosive remnants pose for people of Ukraine and explores  ways to support the government of Ukraine in securing a safer tomorrow for its citizens. 

With your great inside of the current situation in Ukraine and the breath of the work that you do connecting investors and businesses in Scandinavia with Ukraine, we would like to invite to a panel discussing at the event: Ukraine two years on: From the breadbasket of Europe to the most mined country in the world. The event seeks to explore: how we turn minefields into productive agricultural fields and how a unified effort involving governments, private sector, and international organizations best support the rebuilding of Ukraine's agricultural sector and infrastructure for lasting resilience. 

You will join a panel with government bodies, UN agencies and possibly the private sector. 

Thank you for confirming the reception of this email. 

Warm regards, 
Naimo

 cannot agree to be bound to the GAVI rules and regulations and policies.
 The edits made to the document reflect these limitations which in particular impact the Annexes C and E and the Audit and Investigation requirements, including obligations relating to Misuse of funds and liability in relation to third parties. It is to be
 also noted that current tripartite agreements between UNOPS, GAVI and Governments, whereas UNOPS implements projects in Africa, are subject to UNOPS Standard Project Terms and Conditions. 


Specific
 comments 





Annex C and E:
Reference to GAVI-specific
 templates and policies are difficult for UNOPS to automatically follow as UNOPS has its own UN Principles and obligations to follow that stem from its legal status as a subsidiary organ of the United Nations. UNOPS has a requirement to harmonize its approach
 under the UN framework, but also cannot agree to be bound to comply with every funding sources’ policies and framework as it would limit UNOPS ability to independently and autonomously work and operate in fragile contexts. Additionally by agreeing to follow
 every funding sources’ policy/framework, there is a great possibility that it will be in breach with another funding source’s framework. For this reason, UNOPS has established its own Financial Rules and Regulations and legislative framework, which includes
 its own Environmental and Social Safeguard requirements.






2.8:
 As permits, licenses, consents, approvals and authorizations are under the ownership of the Government/Host Country, UNOPS cannot take full responsibility or liability for duties/obligations that are outside of its own control. UNOPS is more than happy to
 engage with the Government to receive all of the required approvals and authorizations, but it cannot ensure or own the process of receiving such approvals. 


2.9:
 UNOPS has agreements in place with third party contractors and subcontractors that put into place the terms and conditions in line with the UN requirements/principles for contracts. UNOPS is more than happy to engage with GAVI to identify necessary obligations
 that should be flown down as mandatory terms and conditions for its third party vendors where they are in line with UNOPS rules and regulations. However, UNOPS cannot flow down obligations “on the same terms as those imposed on UNOPS” due to the fact that
 UNOPS has a very specific status as a UN system organization with Privileges and Immunities, thereby making it impossible for UNOPS to bestow the terms and conditions identically to non-UN, non-state entities (NUNSE). All terms and conditions would need to
 be adjusted to match the status of the NUNSE third parties with whom we engage. Additionally, due to UNOPS privileges and immunities, UNOPS is unable to be responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors nor remain responsible for the performance
 of the obligations. UNOPS is responsible for the identified obligations under the Agreement and has rules and regulations, and terms and conditions in place with its third party contractors to ensure that if there are any breaches to the contractual obligations
 or acts/omissions which rise to the level of a proscribed practice, to take action to remedy such situation. UNOPS is happy to go further into what remedies UNOPS has in place where a contractor has breached a contract and/or has acted in a way that rises
 to the level of a proscribed practice.


2.10:
 UNOPS has inserted our standard language on legal coverage to ensure that all Parties are aware of UNOPS right to implement within the borders of the Host Country.


4.1 and 4.3:
 UNOPS, in line with the IAIG MOU with GAVI counterparts, is able to provide reasonable supplementary information as long as it is provided subject to its privileges and immunities and rules/regulations. This is carried forward into the 4.3 request on capacity
 assessments for implementing partners - noting that UNOPS’s due diligence assessments are confidential, but we may be able to give relevant information subject to our rules/regulations. Additionally, UNOPS has a Due Diligence Operational Instruction which
 states that UNOPS performs DD only on non-UN, non-state entities.


4.10:
Any reference to an
 audit must be undertaken in line with the UN single audit principle. 


4.11 and 4.12:
These are the IAIG
 requirements that I believe are supported and referenced by the MOU between GAVI and UNOPS. Due to the due process rights of individuals involved and the protection to not jeopardize an ongoing investigation, UNOPS promptly informs of any non-frivolous allegation. 


4.13, 15:
 UNOPS, due to its legal status under the Convention on Privileges and Immunities and due to the fact that it is a self-financed organization (not receiving assessed budget from the United Nations), cannot agree to repay funds that have been misused as UNOPS,
 under its financial rules and regulations, can only trigger disbursements where project activities, defined under our legislative framework, has been identified and committed for that purpose. UNOPS will take reasonable measures to recover the funds and will
 repay any funds that have been duly recovered.

Med henblik på at fremme FN-Byens synlighed i den danske offentlighed og at sætte fokus på det danske kandidatur til FNs sikkerhedsråd, reformer af FN, mv., håber vi fortsat meget på, at I ville være interesserede i et debatarrangement mellem udenrigsministeren og Jorge på Folkemødet. Ser frem til at høre fra jer!
På forhånd mange tak.

On Thu, 29 Feb 2024 at 11:05, Asbjorn BRINK <asbjornb@unops.org> wrote:
Kære Rikke og Julia, 
Som tidligere kort drøftet, tænker vi at en debat mellem udenrigsministeren og Jorge på Folkemødet kunne være en god mulighed for at øge den generelle opmærksomhed på FN's stærke tilstedeværelse i Danmark - ligesom det kunne være en mulighed for at I kan pege på danske prioriteter ifm. jeres kandidatur til FN's Sikkerhedsråd i 2025. 
Samtidigt kunne det være en mulighed for en offentlig debat om FN's rolle i en forandret verden, hvor der er stigende udfordringer med bæredygtighed, klimaforandringer, humanitære kriser, finansiering, konflikter osv. - hvor vi forhåbentligt også kan engagere publikum en smule. 
Med henblik på at facilitere en sådan debat, har vi udarbejdet dette udkast til en konceptnote for debatten, som vi vil foreslå at vi pitcher til hovedscenen på Folkemødet. Konceptnoten er blot et første udkast, som ikke er clearet hele vejen rundt i FN-Byen. Sender den derfor til jer nu, med henblik på at få jeres uformelle input så vi sammen sikrer at vi rammer skiven ift. vores chefer. 
Jeg vil derfor sætte stor pris på at modtage jeres feedback, forslag til justeringer mv. til oplægget. Når vi på kontorniveau er blevet enige om et udkast, kan vi parallelt cleare i vores respektive huse. 
Flemming og jeg står naturligvis også til rådighed hvis vi lige skal drøfte mundtligt. 
Jeg ser meget frem til at høre fra jer.

Dear Mr Lee,

I hope this email finds you well. I wanted to follow up on our last discussion and was wondering whether you had managed to discuss the UNOPS client board with your senior management. In addition, I wanted to provide some additional background about its role and establishment.
  
On 19 March 2019, the Secretary-General decided to establish a UNOPS client board and abolish the Policy Advisory Committee he established in 2008. On 7 June 2019, the Executive Board “notes that Client Board functions are advisory and do not supplant or duplicate any governance functions of the Executive Board” (decision 2019/12).

The client board is advisory to the Executive Director and completely detached from the UNOPS governance framework. It is not a governance body with decision-making authority. 
The client board provides structured feedback from operational partners who can advise the Executive Director based on the performance of project services and operational activities.
The client board was held in 2020, 2021, 2022 and twice in 2023. 

I hope this helps, and I look forward to our discussion on Thursday.

Kind regards,

Arnaud

Description:
To: oletho@um.dk; marweg@um.dk
CC: naimoh@unops.org
BCC: 
Attachment: --none--

Subject: Mulighed for briefing af relevante kontorer i UM om Cities Alliance?
Body:
Kære Ole,

Vi har forsøgt at få et intromøde i stand mellem UNOPS' deputy executive director (Sonja - som jeg tror du kender fra din fortid i Nairobi) og du de sidste par uger. Det viser sig at I begge har lidt pressede kalendere. Jeg håber vi finder tid til et hilse på møde. 
Som du muligvis er bekendt, har vi endvidere netop hyret den anden deputy executive director som bliver danske Kirstine Damkjær. Kirstine tiltræder d. 27. maj - og jeg vil også sigte efter at vi kommer over forbi for at hilse på snarest efter hendes tiltrædelse. 
Jeg rækker ud til dig, da vi medio juni får besøg af vores kolleger fra Cities Alliance og da vi meget gerne ville have mulighed for at præsentere deres kompetencer for evt. relevante medarbejdere på Asiatisk Plads. 
Der kan være gode strategiske synergier mellem Cities Alliances og Danmarks udviklingsprioriteter; klimaforandringer, ligestilling, fattigdom og migration.

Cities Alliance er en FN-multi-donor fond, der ligger under UNOPS, med det mål at bekæmpe fattigdom i byområder og fremme bæredygtig udvikling. 

Fonden opererer i 88 lande, og har et unikt medlemskab, som består af offentlig støtte, civilsamfundet, lokale myndigheder og multilaterale organisationer.  Medlemslandene inkluderer bl.a Sverige, Tyskland, Frankrig, Storbritannien og USA.
Hvis det har interesse, ville vi derfor meget gerne komme forbi Asiatisk Plads medio juni med vores kolleger fra Cities Alliance og give en kort orientering om de kapaciteter de har - og hvordan de evt. kan bidrage til at indfri danske udviklingspolitiske prioriteter. Jeg tænker umiddelbart at det kan være relevant for kolleger i AFPOL, HUMCIV, MIGSTAB og KLIMA. 
Hvis I finder det interessant. kunne jeg i så fald venligst bede om din hjælp til at få kontakt til de relevante i UM, så vi kan sætte et kort møde op? 
På forhånd mange tak for hjælpen! 
MvhAsbjørn

Hi Daniel, 

Apologies for not getting back to you sooner given holidays. 

Considering your suggestion and to keep our conversation focused, we would be happy to reconvene with the UN Women colleagues we met with in February to advance the discussions. 

We would be keen to hear their feedback as we are hoping to share a draft MoU for UN Women’s comments in the next few weeks, with a view of a potential signing ceremony between our EDs over the coming months in New York. 

Much appreciated if you can let me know who would be the focal point on UN Women’s side that we can liaise and follow-up on to finalize and sign the MoU. 

Hopefully we will have an opportunity to meet on another occasion.

Kind regards, 
Emilie and UNOPS team

Dear Daniel, Hodan, Maria, Akhtar,
Colleagues,
 
I hope this finds you well. 
 
I would like to extend our sincere thanks to everyone engaged for your time and active participation in the discussions we held over the past week.
 
Teams covered a wide range of topics, highlighting the strong potential for a formal UNOPS-UN Women partnership. We believe these discussions have laid a strong
 foundation for further enhancing our global collaboration - and paved the way for the possibility of establishing a global MoU. 
 
We have taken note of specific concrete areas of collaboration discussed over the series of meetings, including, for instance, joint project implementation (e.g.
 on infrastructure or cash-based intervention projects) as well as the various possibilities for exchange of knowledge and expertise in the format of events, campaigns, training, etc. 
 
As agreed, we have attached the presentation from yesterday’s meeting, as well as collated the potential areas of collaboration into
this working document,
 to which we warmly invite your and colleagues’ further comments and input. 
 
I very much hope that we can find time in the coming weeks to connect and discuss the way forward. 
 
In the meantime, my team is available to address any specific questions, discuss additions to the working document and facilitate connections with counterparts
 within UNOPS, globally.
 
Looking forward to hearing from you soon.

Jeg vedlægger til din orientering et slidedæk om Cities Alliance. 
Hvis det har interesse, ville vi derfor meget gerne komme forbi Asiatisk Plads med Cities Alliance kolleger en times tid d. 10 eller 11 juni og give en kort orientering om de kapaciteter de har - og hvordan de evt. kan bidrage til at indfri danske udviklingspolitiske prioriteter. 
Jeg tænker umiddelbart at det kan være relevant for kolleger i AFPOL, HUMCIV, MIGSTAB og KLIMA. 
Kunne du hjælpe med at samle et par relevante kolleger som har en times penge til at mødes på et tidspunkt som passer jer?

Invitation til FN-Event på Folkemødet: Hvem er de bedste brobyggere?

Kære Sophie Hæstorp Andersen

Vi tillader os at række ud til dig som repræsentanter for FN’s infrastruktur-agentur, UNOPS, og FN’s miljøorganisation, UNEP Copenhagen Climate Centre - begge med base i FN-Byen her i København.

UNOPS og UNEP er gået sammen på Folkemødet for at tackle det højaktuelle spørgsmål: Hvordan kan vi håndtere klimaudfordringerne, når vi opfører infrastruktur?

Vi ved, at inddragelse, medbestemmelse og medansvar øger borgernes tillid til at adressere de udfordringer, som vores samfund står overfor. Vi vil derfor meget gerne skabe et engagerende miljø på Folkemødet, hvor borgerne ikke blot er tilskuere til traditionelle paneler, men aktivt deltager i uformelle samtaler og løser konkrete, sjove opgaver med beslutningstagerne, og hvor I sammen skaber et helt konkret produkt: En bæredygtig bro.

Klimakampen er ikke en kamp mellem rød og blå; den vedrører os alle, og det er i fællesskab, at vi må finde løsningerne. I denne ånd ønsker vi at invitere dig og dine kolleger, både fra Christiansborg og kommunerne, til at afprøve jeres kreative kræfter og sammen med borgerne bygge (i ordets bogstaveligste forstand) en bæredygtig bro.

Selve broen består af træstave og der medfølger hjælpemidler. Hvert hold ledes af et par politikere og I er sammen om at bygge én bro, som I har ca. 30 minutter til. I forbindelse med brobygningen tager vi fat på de presserende klimaudfordringer, som vi står over for - herunder særligt hvilke rolle infrastruktur spiller.

Vores arrangement afholdes i FN Byens telt på Folkemødet i Allinge, Bornholm, torsdag den 13. juni fra kl. 13:00 til 14:45. 
Vi håber derfor at du har mulighed for at afsætte 30 min til tidsrummet 13:00 - 13:45 eller 14:00 - 14:45.
 
Vi håber at vores ide om en lidt anderledes event på Folkemødet har vakt din interesse. Hvis du er interesseret, vil vi meget gerne mødes med henblik på at tale nærmere om eventet - samt udvikle en detaljeret drejebog sammen.

Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig og ser frem til at arbejde sammen om at skabe bæredygtige forbindelser.
 
De bedste hilsener
Mette og Asbjørn

Subject: Modernisering af børnehospital i Mykolaiv i samarbejde med Novo Nordisk
Body:
Kære Anne og Marianne, 
Som I ved, har vi over en længere periode været i dialog med Novo Nordisk om mulige projekter i Ukraine. 
Vi har nu indsnævret Novo Nordisks præferencer og budget, som bl.a. indebærer at de stiller med i størrelsesordenen 50 mio. kr. med ønske om medfinansiering fra andre donorer. 
Vi forstår, at der i Sundhedsministeriet er et meget stort ønske om at modernisere og opgradere børnehospitalet i Mykolaiv, hvilket vi umiddelbart vurderer kan gøres for i størrelsesordenen omkring 115 mio. kr. 
I vedlagte slides s. 4-7 kan I se helt kort overblik over projektet, som vil udbygge børnehospitalets kapacitet fra nuværende 10.000 patienter årligt til ca. 15-20.000 årligt. Konkret lægges op til: Etablering af en dedikeret etage til kræftramte børn med individuelle rum. Modernisering af 4 operationsstuer som vil muliggøre gennemførelse af komplicerede hjerne og hjerteoperationerEtablering af en radiologi-afdeling med MRI scanner, røntgenscanner mv. Omorganisering af akutafdelingen som vil muliggøre mindre operationer på børnOpgradering af sygestuer Installation af efficient klimaanlægIsolering af bygningen mhp. at øge energieffektiviteten Faciliterer til undervisningsformål I første omgang vil jeg forhøre om I kunne være interesserede i tale sammen om projektet - og evt. brainstorme om hvordan vi kunne realisere det. 
Indtil da: rigtig god weekend!

Subject: Partnership with AP Møller Foundation and Olena Zelenska Foundation to construct homes for foster families
Body:
Dear colleagues, 
Yesterday I met with the CEO of The Export and Investment Fund of Denmark (EIFO) as they have been acting as the facilitator of a potential project funded by the AP Møller Foundation (the fund that owns the shipping company Maersk) to construct up to 10 new homes for foster families in Ukraine done by the Olena Zelenska Foundation. 
Discussions have been ongoing for some time as the AP Møller Foundation is not comfortable handing over funds directly to the Olena Zelenska Foundation. Thanks to the amazing work done on the ground by you guys in Ukraine so far, UNOPS has a strong reputation here in Denmark as a trusted partner and as a pragmatic problem solver. 
They have therefore reached out to us, to ask if we could be a partner in this project, as they would prefer that the money flows from the AP Møller Foundation to UNOPS. We would then partner with the Olena Zelenska Foundation on the implementation work. 
The Olena Zelenska Foundation has already developed a full concept for the foster homes incl. a budget proposal, timeline etc. which does not make things less complicated. 
I have agreed with the CEO of EIFO that we would brainstorm on a possible setup that might work and revert to them asap. A possible way forward could be that UNOPS acts as the recipient of the funds, validate and monitor the implementation work done by Olena Zelenska Foundation with on-spot checks etc., develop a detailed project proposal and tri-party agreement in which we specify the concrete division of labour, reporting requirements, responsibilities etc.  
The AP Møller Foundation will allocate approx. 5 million USD to the project tomorrow.
Although I am painfully aware of the complexities of this project - which is also rather small - I am thinking that it might be worthwhile trying to see if we can engage in it to diversify our partners and establish a longer term partnership with both the Olena Zelenska Foundation and the AP Møller Foundation. 
I will try to find availability in your calendars to discuss how we could take this forward. 
Thanks!

Subject: Re: Management Fee for UNOPS?
Body:
Kære Anne
Jeg er allerede i tæt dialog med EIFO (som er i dialog med AP Møller Fonden) om vores management fee. 
Som du muligvis allerede ved, har vi ikke et fast niveau for vores management fee, idet det afhænger af: Størrelsen på budgettet (større budget = mindre management fee og vice versa)Kompleksiteten i projektet (mere kompleks = højere management fee og vice versa)Det er korrekt at vores gennemsnitlige management fee er i størrelsesordenen 5,1-5,5%. Det vil dog ikke være retvisende ift. et muligt infrastrukturprojekt med en relativ lille budgetvolumen. Vi vil skulle foretage en konkret vurdering af projektet for at kunne vurdere udgiftsniveauet til management fee. Det er vores team i Kyiv allerede i gang med ift. det konkrete mulige projekt (hvor jeg helt personligt tror vi kommer over +10% - bl.a. afhængig af lokationen). Jeg har aftalt med EIFO, at vi vender tilbage næste uge med et foreløbigt, groft overslag.   
Jeg vedlægger til jeres orientering en kort, relativ let forståelig gennemgang af vores fee setting struktur, som du er velkommen til at dele. 
MvhAsbjørn

Hej Asbjørn, 
Har du mulighed for at læse denne mail til Stein Erik igennem? Den er med stor inspiration fra din mail til UM. 
Bh Naimo 
Kære Stein Erik

Jeg håber, at alt er vel.

Jeg skriver til dig på vegne af en af vores "hosted entities", Sanitation og Hygiejne Fund, der opererer under UNOPS' paraply.
Vi vil meget gerne have muligheden for et kort møde med relevante medarbejdere på Utenriksdepartementet og evt NORAD, hvor kollegerne fra SHF kunne præsentere deres arbejde, kapaciteter og kompetencer med henblik på at identificere områder, hvor de kan understøtte norsk udviklingspolitik.  
Vi ser gode synergier og muligheder for samarbejde på områder som klima, global sundhed og ligestilling. 
Vi forestiller os, at det kan være relevant for kolleger i Avdeling for bærekraftig utvikling, herunder Sektion for energi, klima og miljø samt Helse. I og med at de fleste mennesker uden adgang til hygiejne og sanitation er i Afrika syd for Sahara, tænker vi at Afrikaseksjonen i Utenriksdepartementet også kunne være relevant at række ud til. Hos NORAD vil vi meget gerne række ud til departementet for partnerskaber og innovation. Vi kan naturligvis selv række ud til NORAD, hvis det er lettere, men vi ser størst værdi i en samlet briefing. 
Vi vil værdsætte muligheden for at briefe de relevante kolleger om SHL’s arbejde i ca. en time i løbet af maj og juni. Asbjørn og jeg samt vores kolleger i SHF vil naturligvis meget gerne aflægge et besøg til Oslo. 
Sanitation and Hygiene Fund (SHF) blev oprettet i 2021 og er den eneste af FN globale fonde, der har fokus på at fremme sanitet, hygiejne og menstruationshygiejne (SDG-mål 6.2) i lav- og mellemindkomstlande gennem markedsbaserede tilgange og katalytisk finansiering. Med det centrale og transformative præmis for verdensmålene, leaving no one behind, vil SHF’s arbejde  for bedre adgang til hygiejne, sanitet og menstruationshygiejne føre til forbedrede sundheds- og uddannelsesresultater, skabe jobmuligheder og økonomisk vækst, tilbyde en lysere fremtid for kvinder og piger samt mindske klimaforandringer.
Til orientering vedlægger jeg et slidedeck om SHL. 
Jeg ser frem til at høre fra dig.  
De bedste hilsener Naimo

Dear Matthias, 
 
Thank you for the call yesterday.  As discussed, I am sending this joint-email on behalf of UNDRR and UNOPS to confirm the following:  
 
The MOU signed in March 2024 by the COP/CMA, UNDRR and UNOPS stipulates that funds contributed to the Santiago Network shall be managed through
 UNOPS, and “where required” by UNDRR. 
 
UNDRR could receive funds e.g. to cover its own costs, however UNDRR did not foresee receiving funds to cover the costs of the Secretariat functions
 beyond providing technical assistance to implementing partners / countries (e.g. for staffing, recruitments, office space, procurement, travel, etc.) which are agreed to be contracted and paid for by UNOPS.  In effect, this would lead to parallel fund management
 and implementation structures, one under UNOPS regulations and rules and another  under UNDRR’s regulations and rules, which would negatively impact management effectiveness and cost efficiency of the Santiago network secretariat’s work programme implementation.
 
UNDRR and UNOPS were selected by the COP/CMA to co-host the Santiago network secretariat in November 2023, with clearly delineated and complementary
 tasks and responsibilities: UNDRR being responsible for providing technical advisory services and UNOPS providing programme management support. It is on this basis that the MOU between the COP/CMA, UNDRR and UNOPS was cleared by the UN Office of Legal Affairs
 and ultimately by the General Assembly
 
So far UNDRR has not accepted to receive and manage funds from other donor countries for the Santiago Network.  This was agreed to be done by UNOPS,
 which has already received $7.8 million from the USA and Spain, and is currently discussing the EUR 3 million contribution from the EU. 
 
Introducing parallel fund management structures would not only lead to duplication of work and inefficiencies, but would also result in additional
 unnecessary costs as UNDRR would need to hire additional resources to manage the funds and implement activities which were not foreseen in the 2024-2025 work programme.  In addition to the direct costs, UNDRR as a Secretariat entity has to charge an indirect
 overhead cost of 13% to all donor funding, which would result in additional operating costs for the Santiago Network. While UNOPS, benefitting from a flexible pricing policy and leveraging economies of scale, would charge a management fee of 4.44% (which could
 further decrease with additional pledges beyond the current $47 million).
 
Finally, the funds received by UNOPS on behalf of the Santiago Network will be used in accordance with the workplan and annual budget approved by
 the Advisory Board at its first session in Geneva in March.  The workplan and budget will be subject to regular narrative and financial progress reports and an annual financial audit, thus providing full accountability and transparency.
 
Please let me know if you would like more information from us or our UNDRR colleagues.
 
Thanks and best wishes,

Subject: Draft suggestions on setup and budget for building homes for foster families in Ukraine
Body:
Dear colleagues at EIFO, Ministry of Business and Ministry of Foreign Affairs. 
In advance of our meeting in half an hour, please find here for your reference, a preliminary overall description of the two potential setups and accompanying budgets for the construction of foster family homes in Ukraine in collaboration between UNOPS and the Olena Zelenska Foundation. 
We have described in overall terms an option 1, that would entail that UNOPS does the full implementation of the project by which we would also take upon us the full responsibility and liability for the project outcome. The implementation would still happen in close collaboration with the Olena Zelenska Foundation - and we have made suggestions on the concrete division of labour and responsibilities - all of which would have to be described in detail in a legal agreement The UNOPS fee for this option is 6,0%. Our recommendation would be option 1 as it would eliminate the donor's concerns. 
We have also described in overall terms an option 2 where UNOPS would provide technical advise and supervision of the project implementation. As UNOPS will not be in control of the implementing parts of the project, UNOPS cannot undertake the responsibility and liability for the outcome of the project under option 2. UNOPS' management fee for this option is 13,7%. 
With regards to the preliminary budget estimates, kindly notice that for option 1 (full implementation) the cost estimate is for the full project while the cost estimate for option 2 is only for the services provided by UNOPS. I understand that different options on how to fund the budget gap are being discussed between Danish stakeholders. At the meeting, we can discuss how these different options could affect the budget estimates from our end. 
We look very much forward to elaborating out suggestions for potential setups that could realise this project and minimize the donor's concerns. 
See you all soon.

Subject: UNHCR EOL for 2024 and 2025 - Signed
Body:
Dear colleagues,
We are delighted to announce that the Exchange of Letters (EOL) for the provision of HR services to UNHCR has been extended for a duration of two years, valid until December 31, 2025.Please be advised that the updates made to the existing documentation are minimal, primarily cosmetic in nature, and do not affect the functioning parameters of our operations. All previous elements, including budget financial templates and the centralized advance funds mechanism, remain unchanged.Despite the minimal updates, the latest templates for any operations covering 2024-2025 must be used. Similar to the current setup, the following requirements will continue for the next two years:Refrain from advising UNHCR offices on applicable fees, as fee setting remains the sole responsibility of the hiring UNHCR office, as per Section 5 REMUNERATION of Annex II of the Administrative Instruction.The advance funds mechanism will continue to be managed centrally from HQ, and therefore no advances are required to be made by individual operations under DAs
For sections in Annex B - The Matrix of Responsibilities where UNOPS is required to act as a depository, please ensure full compliance with the requirement. 
Summary of Changes for the 2024-2025 Documents:01 UNHCR-UNOPS 2024-2025 Exchange of Letters (EoL)Additional sentence to paragraph 6: Contract management and administration (including but not limited to initial contract issuance, amendment, extension, and termination), payroll services and insurance management will be conducted by UNOPS.Financial terminology has been updated in section 2.3.12: LMDC -> LSS,  CMDC-P -> GSS-P, CMDC-NP -> GSS-NP. 
02 UNHCR-UNOPS 2024 - 2025 - ANNEX A - Disbursement Agreement - TemplateNo change.Footnote removed as this requirement is standard “From 2022 onwards no advances are required to be made by individual operations under DAs.” 
03 UNHCR-UNOPS 2024-2025 - ANNEX A1234 - Financial Templates:No change.
04 UNHCR-UNOPS 2024-2025 - ANNEX B - Roles and Responsibilities of the Parties:Removed the reference of the Personal History Form (PHF) and its Supplementary Sheet, which is now replaced by UNHCR’s online application form (generated from Workday)The coordination of medical evacuations is now shared responsibility and it is done in cooperation with the partner. This was already the case in 2023, but not reflected in the matrix.  Reiterating the importance of ensuring the collection of documents for processes where UNOPS acts as a depository.
05 UNHCR-UNOPS 2024-2025 - ANNEX B1 - SOP for ICA Contract Processing:Removed the reference of the Personal History Form (PHF) and its Supplementary Sheet, which is now replaced by UNHCR’s online application form (generated from Workday).Added a new paragraph on page 11 reading: “In accordance with UNHCR’s request, UNOPS will place ICA holders to Special Leave Without or Partial Pay. UNOPS will also process salary advance payments upon UNHCR’s request. Such actions need to be clearly communicated to the respective UNOPS office."Added references to Workday throughout the document, as it is now the default system used by UNHCR DHR. (The references to Workday are relevant to a great extent to UNHCR personnel providing you with the required information needed for contract issuance),  
06 UNHCR-UNOPS 2023 - ANNEX C - Business Innovations Group (BIG) Principles:No change.Please refer to the SharePoint folder for the UNHCR ICA administration documentation. The 2024-2025 EOL is now also active in OU. You are able to link new engagements to the respective information 10029-04.
With this comprehensive update, we trust that you can now commence the necessary procedures to ensure compliance with the deadlines stipulated by BSSC. 
Should you require any further clarification or assistance during this process, please do not hesitate to reach out.

Best Regards,
Lorraine--

Dear Victoria and Sofia,

As promised, I have prepared some background information about Norway and Denmark. As Asbjørn mentioned, we do see a great potential for increased engagement with both Denmark and Sweden. 
Key figures for Norway 
USD 5.2 billion on ODA in 2022, 0,86 og the GNI having spent approximately 1% of GNI on ODA yearly since 2009, 3rd largest provider in terms of percentage of GNI. Norway's development policy is based on the Sustainable Development Goals adopted by all UN member states in 2015. The following areas are given priority; Education, Health, Climate change, the environment and the oceans, Private sector development, agriculture and renewable energy Humanitarian aid.
Substantial regional focus on Africa with USD 831.7 million in 2021. In 2021, the Norwegian MoFA launched the 2021-2025 strategies for Norway’s efforts in the Sahel region. The strategy's primary focus is on peace, stability and development in the Sahel region. Yesterday (May 15, 2024), Norway launched a five year strategy for their humanitarian assistance policy where the main themes are fighting poverty and climate action.
Mine action: Norway is increasing its contribution to Mine action with NOK 200 million. The Norwegian Government had already allocated NOK 164 million for mine clearance activities. The country is the 6th largest contributor to mine action. 
Partnership with Norway 2021 Procurement:  USD 59,31 million. 77th largest supplier in the UN system Delivery by UNOPS:  2024 (YTD): USD 1.6M 2023: USD 7.3 million, 2022: USD 2,6 million, 2021: USD 18,8 million, 2020: USD 5.3 million, 2019: USD 12.2 million  Engagement with UNOPS: 10 active engagements

Key Figures for Denmark 
USD 2,9 billion on ODA in 2022, 0.70% of GNI, 5th largest ODA provider in terms of percentage of GNI, having met the UN target of 0.70% of GNI since 1978. Denmark is committed to maintaining its ODA level at 0.70% of GNI.
The Danish government has strategically chosen to bring together the two areas; Development Cooperation and Global Climate Policy under one ministry. The dual ministerial role aligns with UNOPS’ mandate and efforts to promote sustainable development and address climate change.
Denmark's development two main priorities as set out in the The World we Share’  areTo create hope and future opportunities, and provide better help to more people where it is most difficult – in regions neighboring humanitarian crisis and conflict zones, and in fragile states; To take the lead in the fight for climate, nature and environment, which means fulfilling its international climate commitments, including climate financing. 
Substantial regional focus on Africa with USD 708,1 million in 2021. In August 2024, Denmark will launch a new partnership strategy with Africa. Denmark announced that DKK 400 million will be allocated to fight irregular migration in 2024 and has allocated a total budget of DKK 1.1 million between 2024-2029
 Partnership with Denmark:  Delivery: 2024 (YTD): 2,4K 2023: $16.2M; 2022: $829.3K; 2021: $2.1M; 2020: $2.3M.2022 UN Procurement: USD 1.30 billion.  Making Denmark the 4th largest supplier in the UN system. Recently, UNOPS has engaged with Denmark on rebuilding Ukraine. We also have engagements with Denmark in India on the Strategic Advisory and Technical Assistance for the Water and Sanitation project in India that also won UNOPS project of the year. Furthermore, UNOPS has built a migration center in Somalia and is currently providing technical assistance in passport production for Somalia on behalf of Denmark
Please let me know if you need further information on Denmark and Norway. You can also find more information on both countries and other Northern European partners on our Intranet page.

Dear Colleagues,
 
Many thanks for your patience last week while we finalized the UN’s Delegation to the Brussels 8 Conference for Syria. Kindly ensure that your delegation is made aware of the below.

 
I wanted to share with you all the final list of UN Participants at the Brussels 8 Conference.
 
Some logistical pieces for your kind attention please:

Registration confirmation: Elke, Sofia and myself sent out all the registration confirmations last week to individual delegations. Please let us know ASAP if you didn’t receive
 it from us. The EU will be validating registrations this week. 
 

Requests for Bilateral Space: If you are intending to have bilateral meetings in the margins of the Ministerial Event, we are managing those requests on behalf of the EU. Please
 fill out the form https://forms.office.com/e/bF40KCeJaB to request space. We will do our best to accommodate everyone in 30 minute slots.  Please ensure your bilateral requests are submitted at the latest
 by 25th May as we have to submit them to the EU. Please note that there will be no flags in the bilateral space this year and that the EU will generously provide, tea, coffee and water to support bilateral meetings.

 

Badge Collection: With thanks to our colleagues in UN Brussels, badge collection will take place as follows:
The badges will be available for collection from Sofia at the UN Office in Brussels on the 6th floor, on Monday, 27 May, from
 9h to 13:45h.

 

Floater badges: We have submitted a request for each delegation to have at least 1 red floater badge and that everyone who does not receive a red floater badge receive pink
 floater badges for the listening room. We will revert once this is confirmed by the EU partners.

 

Changes to the delegation: At this time, it is not possible to add additional members of delegation. The only changes that are permitted are to heads of delegation.  If you
 have a change in HoD, please reach out to 
bxl8accreditation@un.org. 
 
Thanks again for all your kind support to the process for the UN’s attendance at BXL8! Please let us know if you have any questions.

From: Asbjorn BRINK <asbjornb@unops.org>


Sent: Tuesday, May 14, 2024 3:25 PM

Cc: Naimo HASSAN HIRSI <naimoh@unops.org>

Subject: Muligt projekt i Moldova vedr. håndtering af ukrainske flygtninge

 

Kære Tale, 

 


Jeg håber alt er godt i Oslo - og at sommeren også langsomt er ved at komme til jer med varmere vejr og sol. 


 


Jeg rækker ud til dig mhp. at drøfte et projekt som muligvis kunne være i norsk interesse i Moldova. Jeg vedlægger en kort konceptnote om projektet, som handler om migrationsbygningen i Chișinău, som er i meget dårlig stand. Bygningen er
 modtagecenter for de over 115.000 ukrainske flygtninge som indtil videre er flygtet til Moldova, hvoraf langt de fleste er udsatte borgere. 


 


Myndighederne i Moldova har meget vanskeligt ved at håndtere den store strøm af flygtninge og har ad flere omgange anmodet om hjælp til genopbygning af infrastruktur til håndteringen. Det vedlagte projekt er en særlig stor prioritet fra
 Moldova, som omhandler en første fase som vil skulle kortlægge behovene og udarbejde et konkret forslag til udbygningen af faciliteterne. 


 


Konkret er der tale om en mindre projekt til omkring 150.000-175.000 USD, som vil finansiere forberedelsen af en egentlig udbygning af migrationsmyndigheden (som evt. kan finansieres af andre eller flere donorer). Dvs. en analyse af hob,
 et concept design, en projekt plan samt budgetestimater for en fuld genopbygning. 


 


Jeg håber at I finder projektet interessant, der som bekendt er meget efterspurgt i Moldova til håndtering af de mange ukrainske flygtninge. 


 


Hvis I har interesse for projektet, vil vi naturligvis meget gerne mødes med henblik på at drøfte nærmere om videre vej frem. 


 


Mvh


Asbjørn

On Thu, 23 May 2024 at 16:11, Rikke Enggaard Olsen <rikoln@um.dk> wrote:








Kære Tue,

 
Jeg har blandt relevante FN-partnere forhørt mig om muligheden for at oprette en fund under deres administration til finansielt at støtte deltagelse
 i FN-processer af civilsamfund og evt. øvrige repræsentanter fra udviklingslande.

 
Konklusionen: Det er ikke en oplagt opgave for UNDPs MPTFO, men UNOPS er interesseret i at påtage sig en sådan opgave ud fra DKs specifikationer og
 har også erfaring med fonds-administration. Deres nordiske liaison Asbjørn Brink (asbjornb@unops.org) kan hjælpe med at få sat et møde op med relevante kollegaer i UNOPS, med henblik på at nå til en fælles forståelse
 inden for nærmeste fremtid. Over til HUMCIV herfra J   
 
Bedste hilsner,
Rikke

 


From: Tue Kristoffer Westhoff <tuewes@um.dk>

 - Ledelse (INTERNAL) DL <humcivledelse@um.dk>

Subject: RE: Finansiering af SYD's deltagelse i diverse FN konferencer


 
Kære Rikke
 
Mange tak for denne.
 
Som drøftet i går, så kan jeg hermed bekræfte, at HUMCIV er villige til at håndtere den administrative indsats i forbindelse med etablering af bevillingen
 for fonden således at fonden allerede kan præsenteres på dette års UNGA. 
 
Dette forstået således, at MULTI fortsat, i fællesskab med HUMCIV, understøtter dialogen med UNDP og andre stakeholders, samt processen for mobilisering
 af andre donorer. 
 
Såfremt der er enighed herom vil HUMCIV forberede et udkast til en forelæggelsesnotits til UGKMen forud for UNGAen og afsøge mulighed for finansiering
 for 2025, samt forberede en kontrakt med UNDP.
 
Mvh Tue

 
 


From: Rikke Enggaard Olsen


Sent: 05 April 2024 10:09

 Westhoff <tuewes@um.dk>

 Nete Kyndesen <netkyn@um.dk>; HCE - Ledelse (INTERNAL) DL <HCELedelse@um.dk>

Subject: RE: Finansiering af SYD's deltagelse i diverse FN konferencer


 
Kære kollegaer,
 
Resultatet af drøftelse på AP om FNNYs forslag om DK bidrag til finansiering af Syd-deltagelse i FN-processer, er at både MULTI og HUMCIV bakker op
 om forslaget (der konkret f.eks. kunne støttes med 7 mio. årligt over en flerårlig periode). MULTI foreslår oprettelse af en trust fond til formålet (f.eks. administreret af UNDPs MPTFO), da dette vil lette administrationsbyrden og skabe grundlag for at også
 andre donorer kan bidrage. Ifht. det bredere landskab/allerede eksisterende lignende finansieringsmodaliteter og initiativer oplyser FNNY at ikke umiddelbart være bekendt med sådanne. Har vendt henvendelse til MPTFO vedr. deres aktuelle trust fund portefølje,
 og afventer svar. Ifht. civilsamfundets SoTF-budskaber kan der være god musik i at annoncere en sådan DK-initieret trust fund på SoTF i 2025.

 
Ifht. vejen frem så foreslår MULTI at vente til FL26 med at spille forslaget ind.
 Der vil skulle træffes beslutning om hvor bevillingen skal forankres. MULTI kan ikke påtage sig opgaven med at sætte en trust fund op til udmøntning under FL25. Såfremt øvrige kontorer har kapacitet til at løfte opgaven i forbindelse med FL25, bakker MULTI
 fuldt ud op om at et andet kontor spiller forslaget ind til AFRPOL og tager lead på processen.

 
Bedste hilsner,
Rikke  
 
 


From: Mikael Erbs <mikerb@um.dk>


Sent: 14 March 2024 15:55

To: Rikke Enggaard Olsen <rikoln@um.dk>

Cc: New York UN, Udvikling (INTERNAL) DL <nycmisudvintdl@um.dk>; Michael Blichfeldt
 <micbli@um.dk>; Erik Laursen <erilau@um.dk>;
 MUS - Ledelsen (INTERNAL) DL <musledelseintdl@um.dk>; Anine Hagemann <aninha@um.dk>;
 Tue Kristoffer Westhoff <tuewes@um.dk>

Subject: Finansiering af SYD's deltagelse i diverse FN konferencer


 
Kære Rikke,
 
Tak for hurtigt at spille bold på denne!
 
Der bør nok ikke kun være at støtte civilsamfund, men også regeringer (fra DACable lande) og måske også academia.
 
Der vil sikkert også være sådanne ønsker fra bl.a. FN Geneve, Rom, Nairobi og andre enheder afhængig af, hvilke FN partnerskaber, man dækker (fx WTO
 i Geneve).
 
Så sikkert godt, at se på alle organisationsstrategier/FN prioriteter = alle de enheder, som kunne have ønske om at kunne hjælpe med at sende nogen
 til en given FN-konference (måske lave en høring).
 
Nu er det en helt ny ide, så har endnu ikke her talt om vi skulle spille det ind ift. FL25 – men måske er det i sagens natur mere oplagt forankret i
 MULTI?
 
VH Mikael
 


Fra: Rikke Enggaard Olsen <rikoln@um.dk>


Sendt: 14. marts 2024 10:25

Til: Mikael Erbs <mikerb@um.dk>; Anine Hagemann <aninha@um.dk>;
 Tue Kristoffer Westhoff <tuewes@um.dk>

 Erik Laursen <erilau@um.dk>; MUS - Ledelsen (INTERNAL) DL <musledelseintdl@um.dk>

Emne: RE: Har vi før støttet NGO/Civilsamfundsorganisationer fra SYD's deltagelse i diverse FN konferencer?


 
Kære Mikael,

 
Fin idé, kunne evt. skæres over samme model som støtten til CIVICUS og Digital Democracy Initative. Hvad tænker du @Tue?
 
Ville være et oplagt commitment at kunne erklære under SoTF, som illustration af DKs opbakning til civilsamfundsdeltagelse.

 
Har FNNY overvejet at pitche idéen til FL25?

 
Bedste hilsner,
Rikke

 


From: Mikael Erbs <mikerb@um.dk>


Sent: 14 March 2024 14:20

To: Rikke Enggaard Olsen <rikoln@um.dk>; Anine Hagemann <aninha@um.dk>

Cc: New York UN, Udvikling (INTERNAL) DL <nycmisudvintdl@um.dk>; Michael Blichfeldt
 <micbli@um.dk>; Erik Laursen <erilau@um.dk>

Subject: VS: Har vi før støttet NGO/Civilsamfundsorganisationer fra SYD's deltagelse i diverse FN konferencer?


 
Kære Rikke og Anine,
 
Det viser sig, at den pågældende fond er relateret til UNFCCC.
 
Men det kunne nok med fordel overvejes at oprette en, som kunne dække deltagelse i FN-konferencer mere bredt (i stedet for, at vi hopper fra tue til
 tue som f.eks. SIDS4, LLDC3 og FFD4).
 
VH Mikael
 


Fra: Jacob Strange-Thomsen <jacstr@um.dk>


Sendt: 14. marts 2024 05:41

Til: Mikael Erbs <mikerb@um.dk>

Cc: Erik Laursen <erilau@um.dk>

Emne: SV: Har vi før støttet NGO/Civilsamfundsorganisationer fra SYD's deltagelse i diverse FN konferencer?


 
Kære Mikael
 
Ja, Rasmus har desværre forladt Ministeriet fra starten af denne måned.

 
I forhold til den støttemodalitet som Rasmus nævner, at vi har i forhold til regeringer, har dette været i forhold til deltagelse i COP’en, hvor vi
 har støttet en UNFCCC trustfund, der finansierer deltagelse fra udviklingslande. I kan se bevillingen i PMI via dette link:
PMI - Project - Contribution to UNFCCC Trust Fund for Participation for COP28
 
I forhold til dit andet spørgsmål tror jeg ikke umiddelbart, at UNFCCC trustfunden kan finansiere deltagelse i ”FN Financing for Development Topmødet”,
 da det antageligvis ligger udenfor dens formål.
 
Hilsen
 
Jacob
 
 
 


Fra: Mikael Erbs <mikerb@um.dk>


Sendt: 12. marts 2024 23:14

Til: Jacob Strange-Thomsen <jacstr@um.dk>

Cc: Erik Laursen <erilau@um.dk>

Emne: SV: Har vi før støttet NGO/Civilsamfundsorganisationer fra SYD's deltagelse i diverse FN konferencer?


 
Kære Jacob,
 
Undrede mig over, at jeg ikke havde hørt fra Rasmus, men kan nu se, at han har forladt ministeriet.
 
Så kan du mon svare på det spørgsmål vi stillede?
 
VH Mikael
 


Fra: Mikael Erbs


Sendt: 22. februar 2024 18:15

Til: Rasmus Tvorup Ewald <rasewa@um.dk>

Cc: Maria Ana Petrera <marape@um.dk>; Cornelia Hempel Krüger Mogensen <cormoe@um.dk>;
 Emma Ringer Mogensen <emmmog@um.dk>; Jacob Strange-Thomsen <jacstr@um.dk>;
 Michael Schou Olsen <michol@um.dk>; Betina Vorsøe Andersen <betian@um.dk>;
 New York UN, Udvikling (INTERNAL) DL <nycmisudvintdl@um.dk>; Maria Stage <marsta@um.dk>;
 Nina Berg <ninber@um.dk>; Michael Blichfeldt <micbli@um.dk>;
 Rikke Enggaard Olsen <rikoln@um.dk>; Anine Hagemann <aninha@um.dk>;
 Jakob Tvede <jaktve@um.dk>; Jesper Hilsted Andersen <jehian@um.dk>

Emne: SV: Har vi før støttet NGO/Civilsamfundsorganisationer fra SYD's deltagelse i diverse FN konferencer?


 
Kære Rasmus,
 
Tak for dette – Som Michael også gør opmærksom på har vi bl.a. herfra FNNY lavet bevillinger til at støtte CSO + regeringer fra Syd ift. kommende LLDC3
 (1 mio. kr.) + SIDS4.
 
Og det kunne være skønt om man kunne rationalisere det ved at samle det i en større dansk fond til det formål, så vi ikke mange steder skal bakse med
 mikrobevillinger.
 
Kan du kaste lidt mere lys over, hvordan den fond du nævner allerede støtter regeringer fra Syd?
 
Er der evt. mulighed for, at den kan støtte deltagelse i FN Financing for Development Topmøde forudset til juni/juli
 i Spanien 2025?
 
Og måske også LLDC3 og SIDS4, da det vi har bidraget med er begrænset?
 
Tænker også at vi kan blive gode venner med ret mange i Syd ved at have en sådan udvidet fond!
 
Sætter også kolleger i MULTI på i kopi (Rikke og Anine).
 
VH Mikael
 
 


Fra: Michael Blichfeldt <micbli@um.dk>


Sendt: 22. februar 2024 07:32

Til: Rasmus Tvorup Ewald <rasewa@um.dk>

Cc: Maria Ana Petrera <marape@um.dk>; Cornelia Hempel Krüger Mogensen <cormoe@um.dk>;
 Emma Ringer Mogensen <emmmog@um.dk>; Jacob Strange-Thomsen <jacstr@um.dk>;
 Michael Schou Olsen <michol@um.dk>; Betina Vorsøe Andersen <betian@um.dk>;
 New York UN, Udvikling (INTERNAL) DL <nycmisudvintdl@um.dk>; Maria Stage <marsta@um.dk>;
 Nina Berg <ninber@um.dk>

Emne: SV: Har vi før støttet NGO/Civilsamfundsorganisationer fra SYD's deltagelse i diverse FN konferencer?


 
Kære Rasmus
 
New York er faktisk pt. ved at forberede en bevilling til DPPA/PBSO vedr. CSO-UN Dialogue om Peacebuilding finansieret over APDs konference- og seminarkonto,
 og vi har været i dialog med Betina om netop ODA-vinklen i sådanne typer bevillinger. Her er civilsamfundsperspektivet meget nyttigt for en positiv ODA-vurdering.  
 
Det lyder interessant med en bevilling, der løber over flere år – det kunne være interessant at høre om I arbejder på en ny model i stedet for individuelle

Dear Julia, dear Mette, colleagues,
 
Thank you for keeping us informed about the dialog with the A. P. Møller Foundation. We are ready to meet with UNOPS and discuss our project with the colleagues.
 But we would like to be transparent that
 Option 2 suits us better, when UNOPS is involved as a consultant. And we would like to discuss the terms of the consultancy
 and what it includes. After all, we already have a developed project, visualizations of the house, specifications, estimate calculations,
 a list of furniture, terms of reference for the selection of land plots, etc. This project is being successfully implemented: within the first wave, we built 14 houses for large foster families in 8 regions of Ukraine. 
 
In addition, the Olena Zelenska Foundation, as the initiator of the project to build homes for large foster families, is now acting as a consultant to the Coordination Center for
 the Development of Family Upbringing and Child Care, which operates under the Government of Ukraine and implements the deinstitutionalization reform, as well as to local authorities, which are scaling up our project to the regions.
 
We strive for full transparency, so the Foundation is ready to provide A. P. Møller Foundation, EIFO and, if necessary, UNOPS, with reports on the project and its implementation.
 
Regarding Option 1, when UNOPS takes over the project implementation, we would not like to move forward with this scenario. This could significantly delay the implementation in time,
 as well as duplicate the functions of participants and project components. And this would be inefficient.
 
We are ready to discuss further steps with you and UNOPS. We are eager to implement this important initiative for Ukraine together.
 
Iryna

Dear Iryna,
 
I am getting back to you regarding the Room for Childhood project.

 
In our continued dialogue with the A. P. Møller Foundation on securing a donation for the project, the foundation has expressed a wish for external monitoring.
 To my understanding, this is standard procedure for projects that the Danish state is involved in. We have been in contact with UNOPS, as they are the agency most used by the Danish state.

                                                                              

UNOPS has drafted a preliminary overall description of two potential setups for the construction in close collaboration between UNOPS and the Olena Zelenska Foundation. Option
 1 would entail that UNOPS does the full implementation of the project by which, they would also take upon the full responsibility and liability for the project outcome. The implementation will still happen in close collaboration with you, the Olena Zelenska
 Foundation. The concrete division of labour and responsibilities will be described in detail in a legal agreement, that you will be directly involved in. Option 2 would entail that UNOPS would provide technical advice and supervision of the project implementation.
 As UNOPS will not be in control of the implementing parts of the project, UNOPS cannot undertake the responsibility and liability for the outcome of the project under option 2.
 
We have indications, that the A. P. Møller Foundation prefers model 1. Please consider this a means to securing the donation for the project. As we see it, this
 might also be an opportunity for the Olena Zelenska Foundation to enter into collaboration with a respected United Nations organ, that can be leveraged in future projects as well.

 
UNOPS has asked us to emphasize that they truly wish a collaboration, that both parties are happy with. UNOPS have people in Kyiv that are open to initiate dialogue
 (in ukrainian), initially collaborating on outlining who does what in the project as well as kickstarting the due diligence process.

 
Let me know what you think, and do not hesitate to reach out, if you have any questions.

 
Best regards,

OFFICIAL
 

Dear Asbjorn,
 
Thanks very much for your message and the reminders of the issues I owe you responses on.

 
I’m attaching the agenda for the UN Women dialogue – I think we could use this sort of structure as a starting point but there are some tweaks I would probably make. We started
 the dialogue with a bilateral meeting between our DG Development and Humanitarian and a DED, which was followed by an opening session that looked at the overarching relationship. Then we selected a few areas for a more in depth discussion. In general, I think
 objectives are very well aligned so I think we don’t need to spend too much time talking about that. We could increase the time for discussion if we prepare some discussion papers/background reading in advance and focus the discussion around 3 or so key questions/challenges
 we are each trying to address? It would be great to hear any ideas of areas we should focus on. The UNDP dialogue is happening today so there may be other lessons we can apply.
 
In terms of dates, we’ve got some transitions happening in the team over the summer so I would suggest that we look at something from October? That way the Boards/UNGA ministerial
 week etc will be out of the way too. Let me do some initial scoping at my end – the really key person for us to pin down is Melinda Bohannan, our DG Humanitarian and Development.

 
I’m still following up on the Somalia Police Programme, and will find out who is attending the SIDs conference for the UK and who is leading on arrangements and let you know.

 
Look forward to catching up ahead of the Boards - it feels like they’ll be here in no time!
 
All the best,
 
Agnes

Subject: UNOPS 2023 annual report: Practical solutions where needs are greatest
Body:
Dear Agnes,
Following the formal EB document on UNOPS' 2023 annual report, we have also developed a more plain English brochure that focuses on operations and highlights from the annual results. 
The brochure “Practical solutions where needs are greatest” showcases a selection of UNOPS' work in support of our partners. It follows four main topics as identified in the UNOPS restated Strategic Plan 2022-2025 - the three primary themes of climate action, health and renewable energy, and four: our core context –  the ability to operate responding to conflicts and crises in the most difficult of circumstances.
Som examples are: - 7 hospitals and 49 health centres - 55 schools - 187 km of roads - More than 2.2 million days of paid work undertaken by women - More than 23 million days of paid work created for local people - Procured $1.6 billion in goods and services – 41% from local suppliers - Across more than 80 countries, UNOPS implemented almost 1,100 projects - More than 50% of our work delivered in fragile and conflict-affected areas- Delivered around $2.7 billion worth of services on behalf of partners 

It is available from our website in three languages here.

Subject: Gavi / UNOPS Guinea Bissau support
Body:
Dear Seydou and Danielle,
Thanks for the call this morning - it was great to e-meet you and get us all connected at the country, regional and global level! Sorry we missed Marius on this occasion!
Following our discussion, we duly note the upcoming 3-7 June Gavi mission in Guinea Bissau, and @Marius if possible will find time in the schedule for our country teams to meet. The objective being to discuss some of the operational challenges that UNOPS could support MOH / Gavi / other in-country partners with going forward - with a focus on complementary activities, and where we can add value or help expand / accelerate existing activities. 
As requested by Seydou please see below a few of our "capacity statements" to give you an idea of how we are helping countries and their partners expand implementation capacity to improve health infrastructure, health procurement and health programme management. 
I will keep you updated on the UNOPS / Gavi Framework Agreement that is being finalised in case of need (I'm working with Irina Petkova and Laurent in your Legal team on this).
Looking forward to hearing back on the in-country discussions - and I am often at GHC in case you are free for a coffee any time :) !

Dear Oleg and Liviu!

Since I left WHO in 2022 I have been busy helping my UNOPS colleagues understand the global public health world (not always easy to navigate!) and connect them with health partners to help expand implementation capacity, esp to accelerate progress in SDG3.
You may know UNOPS is the "operational arm" of the UN, mandated in Infrastructure, Procurement and Project Management.  Of our total portfolio (USD 1.3 bn per year) over 1/3 is Health focused, we are self financing, and all our projects are needs-driven based on requests from our Partners (member states, international organisations and financing institutions).
I understand there has been a request in KGZ for some support with the construction of a national vaccine storage warehouse. We stand ready to help you and MOH / EPI (and other key stakeholders) move this forward, if we can be of assistance, given the time and budget constraints as I understand them (from Gavi). My colleague Victor in copy is our partnerships specialist and also Civil Engineer, so he knows his construction stuff :) and is well placed to support.
I believe Oleg has provided MOH assistance a while back on needs assessment and there are also some WHO guidelines available for vaccine warehouses. We have significant experience in this type of construction (examples include Kosovo, Panama). I would be happy to convene a call for the four of us, if useful, to see if we can help move this forward as a partnership effort on behalf of MOH. Will either of you be at the WHA in Geneva next week?

for your info--
EU allocates €201 million in humanitarian aid for Sahel and Africa's Lake Chad countries

The Commission is providing €201 million in EU humanitarian funding to address the needs of the most vulnerable people affected by the humanitarian crisis in Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Chad, Mali, Mauritania, Niger and Nigeria. The announcement comes on the occasion of the Senior Officials Meeting on Sahel and Lake Chad, attended on 28 May 2024 by Commissioner Janez Lenarčič in Brussels.The funding will support food security and assistance for malnutrition, health care and protection, water, sanitation and hygiene, shelter and education activities, as well as the transportation of humanitarian workers and supplies to remote and inaccessible locations. The EU humanitarian aid response will continue to focus on the countries and areas directly affected by ongoing insecurity and conflict, including West Africa's coastal countries already impacted by the spill-over from Central Sahel.The overall funding will support humanitarian projects in:- Burkina Faso (€26.9 million);- Cameroon (€21 million);- Chad (€57.9 million, including the newly allocated €8.7 million in response to the consequences of the conflict in Sudan to the neighbouring countries and another €3.1 million to support an EU Humanitarian Air Bridge operation in the East, in addition to the initial €45.3 million announced by Commissioner Lenarčič during his visit to the country at the end of January 2024);- Mali (€24 million);- Mauritania (€5.7 million, including the reinforcement of €3 million allocated in January 2024 in response to the increasing number of Malian refugees in Mauritania);- Niger (€24.6 million);- Nigeria (€31.5 million).

I trust this email finds you well.
I am writing to summarize the multiple emails (May 3 and May 22, attached) that have been received regarding the MONUSCO ICs complaints.  
Overview: UNOPS manages contracts for 804 personnel under the ICA modality for MONUSCO, with 740 based in DRC. Additionally, 298 Short Term Daily Workers (STWA) are managed for short-term assignments. STWAs are not entitled to leave or medical insurance but are covered by Malicious Acts Insurance and Service-incurred insurance. They are paid manually via PO payments and are not part of the regular payroll cycle. Attempts to convert STWAs to the LICA setup were unsuccessful. 
Summary of complaints: the identification system used by UNOPS creates confusion and is perceived as tarnishing MONUSCO's image; salary grades are determined by section chiefs rather than a standardized system; no salary increases or grade advancements have occurred for over 10 years; and UNOPS is accused of abusing power and threatening job security. These issues lead to dissatisfaction and calls for better identification, fair salary adjustments, grade consideration, and an end to perceived power abuse. Around 60 people have signed a petition against UNOPS.

It addresses both the historical and current dimensions of the issues highlighting that Jeanne, the Project Manager, is working closely with the UN Mission to address these challenges. Despite efforts to manage the situation, the Project Manager and her team still receive unwarranted complaints periodically.
Our concern: Given the briefing above, we have a few questions regarding the memorandums shared with the Individual Contractors. Dear Alejo,
I trust this email finds you well.
I am writing to summarize the multiple emails (May 3 and May 22, attached) that have been received regarding the MONUSCO ICs complaints.  
Overview: UNOPS manages contracts for 804 personnel under the ICA modality for MONUSCO, with 740 based in DRC. Additionally, 298 Short Term Daily Workers (STWA) are managed for short-term assignments. STWAs are not entitled to leave or medical insurance but are covered by Malicious Acts Insurance and Service-incurred insurance. They are paid manually via PO payments and are not part of the regular payroll cycle. Attempts to convert STWAs to the LICA setup were unsuccessful. 
Summary of complaints: the identification system used by UNOPS creates confusion and is perceived as tarnishing MONUSCO's image; salary grades are determined by section chiefs rather than a standardized system; no salary increases or grade advancements have occurred for over 10 years; and UNOPS is accused of abusing power and threatening job security. These issues lead to dissatisfaction and calls for better identification, fair salary adjustments, grade consideration, and an end to perceived power abuse. Around 60 people have signed a petition against UNOPS. 
Response from UNOPS DRC Office: The matter of complaints has been discussed with the MONUSCO Contracts Management section and is currently being handled by the partner, MONUSCO.The OIC, Contracts management officer will share a draft response to ICs with UNOPS to review.UNOPS HOP’s email explains the complexities involved in managing IC contracts under UNOPS, highlighting the continuous efforts to address concerns. It addresses both the historical and current dimensions of the issues highlighting that Jeanne, the Project Manager, is working closely with the UN Mission to address these challenges. Despite efforts to manage the situation, the Project Manager and her team still receive unwarranted complaints periodically.
Our concern: Given the briefing above, we have a few questions regarding the memorandums shared with the Individual Contractors. These memos, dating from 2017 and 2023, do not seem to align with the context of HR services to partners. Both memos indicate that UNOPS is responsible for the individual contractors, which does not conform to our policy.1. Memorandum Ref; 002-UNOPS DRC Goma -2017.01(Mathieu VANDAL UNOPS Project Manager)2. Memorandum, ref: 248.UNOPS-DRC-Goma-2023.07,We would like to schedule a call on Tuesday at 11am CPH to discuss PCG's stance on this matter and determine the best approach to address this with our colleagues in DRC.
Best regards,Lorraine

Subject: Re: Touching base and notice of dinner invitation 28th May 2024
Body:
Dear Tim,
Just a quick update on the dinner I attended yesterday, hosted by Friends of Europe on " Winning Peace: building a secure and democratic future in Ukraine".
The dinner was attended by some 40 people. Among them, senior diplomats to NATO, the EU, EEAS reps, former Presidents of Croatia and Lithuania, GIZ Rep here and in Ukraine, think tanks and private sector.
The keynote speech was made by Olha Stefanishyna, Deputy Prime Minister for European and Euro-Atlantic Integration of Ukraine. I had the opportunity to exchange with her and she said that she knows UNOPS from her role of coordination of humanitarian work there and was glad of our presence and work.
The main theme of the dinner was the Summit on Peace in Ukraine on 15-16 June at the Bürgenstock (Canton of Nidwalden), presented by the Deputy head of Switzerland Mission to the EU. The aim of the meeting, which will be at heads of state and government level, will be to develop a common understanding on how to achieve a just and lasting peace in Ukraine. What came out very clearly was the intention to involve as much as possible the global south, to make sure they come onboard as opposed to an evident pro-Russia position. Members of G20 will be invited with the exception of Russia,
The discussion was very much politically oriented and about defence issues, also around "what if Trump wins"?
Even though I had gotten great inputs from Mykhailo, I was not able to take the floor (only 1h30 hrs time!) but UNDP Nick Hartmann, Deputy Regional Director of the Regional Bureau for Europe and CIS took the floor to explain what UNDP and the other UN agencies do in Ukraine in terms of energy supply, mine action etc. He even mentioned the EB members upcoming visit to Ukraine. He actually said that UNDP shares the same board with a few other UN agencies but he did not dare mention which ones (and the rep of UNFPA in Brussels and myself were there :). We spoke a bit after the end of the dinner (can tell you more).
I will have some follow-up meetings with some of the participants at the dinner in the coming days and will keep you informed.
Best regards,Carmen

On Fri, Feb 16, 2024 at 4:44 PM Emilie POTVIN <emiliep@unops.org> wrote:
Dear Daniel, Hodan, Maria, Akhtar, Colleagues,
I hope this finds you well. 
I would like to extend our sincere thanks to everyone engaged for your time and active participation in the discussions we held over the past week.
Teams covered a wide range of topics, highlighting the strong potential for a formal UNOPS-UN Women partnership. We believe these discussions have laid a strong foundation for further enhancing our global collaboration - and paved the way for the possibility of establishing a global MoU. 
We have taken note of specific concrete areas of collaboration discussed over the series of meetings, including, for instance, joint project implementation (e.g. on infrastructure or cash-based intervention projects) as well as the various possibilities for exchange of knowledge and expertise in the format of events, campaigns, training, etc. 
As agreed, we have attached the presentation from yesterday’s meeting, as well as collated the potential areas of collaboration into this working document, to which we warmly invite your and colleagues’ further comments and input.

Subject: Notes from ED and DED meeting with Denmark's DPR Mr. Erik Laursen on June 3
Body:
Dear colleagues, 
On June 3rd the ED and DED met with Denmark's Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN (DPR) Mr. Erik Laursen. 
The ED informed about the status of UNOPS' reforms, work in Gaza and Ukraine. 
The DPR highly appreciated the extremely good collaboration with UNOPS in Copenhagen, Ukraine, Gaza and other areas - while underlining the need for full transparency and accountability following the S3i revelations. The DPR agreed that the requests should be directed towards the right and responsible UN entities - and national jurisdictions. 
The DPR informed that the Danish Minister for Foreign Affairs would meet with the Secretary General on June 6th, where he would push for a decision to make Copenhagen host the CEB in 2025.
The DPR finally informed about a group of Member States named "Friends of Sustainable Energy" to which a number of relevant EDs might be invited to discuss anchoring energy topics at a relevant UN agency. 

***The ED thanked the DPR for Denmark's support during UNOPS's crisis and the ongoing reform process. The ED then informed about the status of completing the Comprehensive Response Plan, the initiatives to go beyond with new transformation initiatives and that practically all the senior leadership had been replaced since the S3i revelations. The ED underlined that UNOPS' staff on the ground had continued to deliver throughout the reform journey and that they were not to be blamed for the faults of a few individuals. 
The ED then explained UNOPS' role in Gaza operationalising the coordination mechanism together with Sigrid Kaag. The ED also explained the issues with getting goods into Gaza as observed during his own mission to Gaza. The ED hoped that with the UNOPS one-stop shop many of these issues could be minimised. 
The DPR conveyed a strong appreciation of the close, informal and constructive collaboration between UNOPS and the Danish MFA in Copenhagen. The MFA had experienced a significantly stronger voice from UNOPS in Copenhagen in the past year - and was eager to help increase the awareness of UNOPS even more. 
The DPR also highly appreciated UNOPS' work on the ground on behalf of Denmark in conflict affected places such as Ukraine and Gaza. 
The DPR pointed to the need for full transparency and accountability to ensure the re-establishment of trust in UNOPS. Denmark fully trusted UNOPS again - but to get other Member States and the broader public onboard - these were two crucial elements. The Danish MFA would focus on ensuring that UNOPS implemented better risk management procedures, instilled cultural change and established a robust whistleblower procedure. 
The ED agreed with the need for full transparency and accountability, and urged the Member States to be precise in their request for accountability, as it was not possible for UNOPS to push on this topic, which was the responsibility of other UN agencies - and national jurisdictions. The DPR agreed with the need to direct the requests for accountability towards the right entities. 
The DPR informed about a group of Member States called "Friends of Sustainable Energy" to which the ED suggested to invite a number of relevant EDs to discuss how to properly anchor the energy issue at UN level.

Subject: Notes from ED and DED meeting with Sweden's ECOSOC Ambassador, Ms. Charlotta Schlyter,
Body:
Dear colleagues, 
On June 4, the ED and DED met with Sweden's ECOSOC ambassador, Ms. Charlotta Schlyter.
The ED updated the ambassador on the implementation of UNOPS reforms, the whistleblower procedure, accountability, recovery of funds and UNOPS' work in Gaza and Afghanistan.  
The ambassador was satisfied with UNOPS' reform progress, and understood that the responsibilities for holding individuals accountable for the S3i and retrieving the missing funds was with the OIOS and OLA - not UNOPS. It was important the UNOPS continued to show progress - no matter how small. 
In general the ambassador was more positive than ever before in her attitude towards  UNOPS.  
***
The ED initially informed about the status of UNOPS's reforms, underlining that the journey would continue with the transformational initiatives. The ED also informed the ambassador about the status of the ongoing procedures regarding holding former UNOPS employees accountable and recovering the missing funds. 
Upon a question from the ambassador, the ED estimated that the process for recovering funds would likely go beyond 2024 while the ED had no timeframe for the legal procedures. 
The ambassador was satisfied with UNOPS' efforts so far, recognising that UNOPS was stuck between a rock and a hard place as the responsibilities for retrieving missing funds and holding individuals accountable was the responsibility of OLA and OIOS. The ambassador was pleased that UNOPS had pushed to get the other UN entities to provide updates to the EB - no matter how small progress was made, it was important to continuously demonstrate that things were actually moving forward. 
The ED informed about UNOPS' work in fragile and conflict affected areas - especially in Gaza and Afghanistan, underlining UNOPS' efforts in helping women in Afghanistan. 
Upon questioned by the ambassador, the ED updated on the implementation of new and stronger whistleblower procedures, the digitalisation strategy and risk management at UNOPS. 
The ED also informed the ambassador about the fact that UNOPS had rejected projects worth about 250 million USD in 2023, which indicated that UNOPS would not just accept any projects - and that staff at UNOPS considered carefully if any project was within the mandate. 
Finally the ambassador complimented UNOPS for the major progress in reforms that had taken place in the past two years - encouraging the ED not to lift the foot on the pedal - and repeating the need for UNOPS to stick to its mandate. 
Best,Asbjørn
