Subject: Notes from ED and DED meeting with UK ECOSOC Ambassador Tom Woodroffe, June 5
Body:
Dear colleagues, 
On June 5 the ED and DED met with the UK ECOSOC Ambassador. Tom Woodroffee. 
The ambassador expressed great satisfaction with the UNOPS reforms and hoped that eventually this would be the gold standard for reforming UN agencies after crises. The UK had fully restored trust in UNOPS and were working towards influencing other WEOG Member States in this direction. 
Upon explanations of the ED about the status of holding responsible individuals accountable for the S3i and recovering the missing funds, the ambassador found it clear that any requests should be directed towards the OLA and OIOS rather than UNOPS who could not influence these processes. The UK would not be part of statements or support EB decision language that made requests on this matter towards UNOPS. 
To the ambassador it would be important to get UNOPS out of the shadows of the past to enable UNOPS' unique ability to operate in difficult places where the FCDO or the private sector could not. The ambassador saw an increasing demand for UNOPS within the FCDO. 
Finally the ambassador assured the ED that the civil service would recommend a strategic dialogue with UNOPS to the new UK government. A strategic dialogue would likely take place in the first half of 2025, and would be a testimony to the UK's increased desire to work with UNOPS - especially in fragile and conflict affected places.  
***
The ED initially informed about the status of UNOPS' reforms, the increased demand for UNOPS' services in especially fragile and conflict affected areas and thanked the UK for the constructive support during UNOPS' reform process. The ED also reported on his recent visit to and UNOPS' work in Gaza, Afghanistan, Ukraine, Myanmar and Yemen. 
The ambassador noted that the FCDO was very pleased with the very comprehensive reforms of UNOPS. The S3i revelations had been very challenging in the donor community - and had also led to self-reflections. But the way that the crisis had been handled at UNOPS would contribute to restoring the confidence in the UN. The ambassador hoped that eventually the UNOPS reform process could be recognised as the gold standard in the donor community for how crises should be handled in UN agencies. 
The ambassador assured the ED that once a new UK government was in place, the recommendation from the civil service would be to host a full strategic dialogue with UNOPS in London - likely in the first half of 2025. Strategic dialogues were normally only held with agencies to which the UK provided core funding. But the increased dialogue between FCDO HQ and UNOPS HQ as well as increased demand from FCDO local representations to work with UNOPS on the ground - had shown the senior leadership in FCDO that there was a strong need for UNOPS. A strategic dialogue between UNOPS and the FCDO was therefore a testimony to the UK's desire to work more with UNOPS. 
Upon questions from the ambassador, the ED elaborated on the status of UNOPS' reformed whistleblower procedure, the remaining action points in the Comprehensive Response Plan as well as the Culture Roadmap. The ambassador stressed that the revised whistleblower procedure was of particular interest and importance to the UK. 
The ambassador assured the ED that the UK would continue to be a strong advocate of UNOPS and that trust in UNOPS had been fully restored. Unfortunately this was not the case for all donors due to the lack of accountability of responsible individuals and slow recovery of missing funds. The ED then explained the process for holding individuals responsible and retrieving the missing funds - which was being handled by OLA and OIOS respectively. 

The ambassador fully agreed that the right interlocutors would be OLA and OIOS - and he instructed his staff to help explain this to other members of the WEOG. The ambassador also made it clear that in his view the UK should not support any statement or EB decision language that made requests to UNOPS to ensure accountability and recovery of funds, when the responsible UN entities were OLA and OIOS.  
The ambassador finally expressed a need for UNOPS to return to being a strong and robust UN agency capable of delivering in fragile places where the FCDO could not - and there the private sector were unable to. The UK would be there to support UNOPS - and help UNOPS get out of the shadow of the past. 
Best,Asbjørn

Subject: Notes from ED and DED meeting with Norway's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ms. Merete Fjeld Brattested, June 5
Body:
Dear colleagues, 
On June 5 the ED and DED met with the Permanent Representative of Norway to the UN (PR), Ms. Merete Fjeld Brattested. 
The PR expressed admiration for the UNOPS reform process and assured the ED that Norway was working to get the progress reflected in a statement at the EB by a large group of cross-regional Member States.   
Norway agreed on the need to direct requests for progress in accountability issues and retrieval of missing funds towards the correct UN entities which were the OLA and OIOS. 
The ED briefed the PR about the work done by UNOPS in Afghanistan, Gaza, Myanmar and Ukraine which the PR found interesting and relevant to Norway's development aid priorities. 

***
The ED initially updated the PR about the status of UNOPS reforms, the culture roadmap, ongoing process of holding responsible individuals accountable for S3i and recovery of missing funds. The ED argued that UNOPS was stuck between a rock and a hard place as the ongoing proceedings for holding responsible individuals accountable and retrieving the missing funds were outside the control of UNOPS as OIOS and OLA were in charge of the processes. 
The PR agreed with the ED's considerations and would touch base with those Member States that continued to push for UNOPS to provide updates and progress on accountability. However due to the Norwegian nationality of the former ED, this was a particularly delicate matter for Norway - as some Member States now also questioned investigations into the former ED. Norway had no interest in protecting the former ED even if she was a Norwegian national. They would therefore "go with the flow" of the EB in terms of the accountability issues at hand. 
The PR stressed that Norway had great admiration for the very comprehensive reforms that had taken place in UNOPS over the past two years. A statement by a large group of Member States that crossed the usual regional groups was being prepared that clearly recognised the progress made. Norway was pushing internally among the Member States to ensure that this would be clearly recognised - against some, few Member States (Switzerland, The Netherlands and Canada) that still had a clear focus on accountability issues outside the control of UNOPS. Norway - together with Denmark and the UK - was actively trying to counter these in the WEOG internal discussions and tried to be very precise in the draft decision language on which UN entities accountability requests should be directed towards. 
The ED then briefed the PR about the work done by UNOPS in Afghanistan, Gaza, Myanmar and Ukraine which the PR found interesting and relevant to Norway's development aid priorities. 
Finally the PR informed that Norway together with Portugal and other Member States were preparing next year's high level conference on financing for sustainable development in Spain - where Norway tried to push for recognition that this was about more than assembling more funds - but also instilling a greater focus on eg. implementation. The ED stressed the need to address the implementation gap which the PR agreed on. 

Best,Asbjørn

Subject: Notes from DED meeting with Dr. Helge Zeitler, Director Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, June 5
Body:
Dear colleagues,
On June 5 the DED (Kirstine Damkjær) met with the Director Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, Dr. Helge Zeitler and Senior Policy Officer, Mr. Clemens Kapler.
Germany fully acknowledged the comprehensive reforms done at UNOPS at an impressive speed. The Director assured the DED that they were internally working hard to influence their peers at political level to return to business as usual with UNOPS. There was nothing UNOPS could do at the moment to speed up the process. 
The German State Secretary would be in Copenhagen on June 25 and would likely appreciate meeting UNOPS senior management (ED/DED). Relevant personnel would reach out to the Bruxelles Liaison Office to arrange. 
*** 
The DED informed about her new role at UNOPS and how the two new DEDs would effectively ensure separation of powers. The Director complimented UNOPS for the speed in which the very comprehensive reforms had been implemented.  
Upon a question from the DED on what would be needed for Germany to return to business as usual with UNOPS, the Director assured that they were working internally with their peers to turn the ship around and get back to business as usual. The Director asked for patience as it would take time to fully get things back to normal. It was the impression of the Director that the current case-by-case approach effectively did not block engagements with UNOPS. 
The main challenges in Germany to go back to business as usual were matters that were beyond UNOPS' control. It related to 1) former UNOPS personnel involved in S3i getting employment at other UN agencies, 2) holding responsible individuals accountable and 3) recovery of missing funds. The Director assured the DED that Germany was fully aware that these matters were in the hands of the OLA and OIOS. 
The DED offered full transparency on all matters related to UNOPS - as well as willingness to meet at all levels to exchange any info required from a Germany perspective to return to business as usual. 
According to the Director, the S3i case had led to self-reflection among many EB-members about their ability to actually oversee the work of UN agencies. For example a MOPAN assessment of UNOPS done 6 months before the S3i revelations had completely cleared UNOPS. 
The Director mentioned that the German State Secretary would be in Copenhagen on June 25 - and that it would be recommended to the State Secretary to meet with UNOPS ED / DED. 
Best,Asbjørn

Oggetto: R: Evento Codeway con banche multilaterali sviluppo
 
Carissimi,
 
grazie per il vostro interessamento ad una rassegna interessante e importante come Codeway. E grazie per la pazienza – ma questo paio di giorni è stato molto utile per fare dei
 passi avanti.
 
In primo luogo, posso intanto dirvi che è piuttosto certo che la data sarà il
15 di maggio e che l’evento si terrà la mattina. Infatti il Vice Ministro, che è stato coinvolto in questa edizione di Codeway sin dall’inizio, ha già inserito l’impegno in agenda (per ora) per tutta quella la giornata. Aggiungo che l’evento
procurement è - per dimensioni, partecipazione e potenziale in termini di opportunità per le imprese - probabilmente il più importante di tutta la Fiera e che pertanto, in attesa che sia comunque prodotto e approvato un appunto – su cui stiamo lavorando
 e per cui anticipo ai colleghi DGSP che chiederemmo l’intesa – l’ipotesi più solida è che il nostro sia
l’evento di apertura.
 
Con riguardo agli attori coinvolti, come sapete, nelle scorse settimane eravamo partiti con il procurement e il sistema di LTEs onusiano, con UNOPS che teneva le fila (in quanto
 si tratta di un settore che è oggetto specifico della propria mission). La reazione di UNOPS all’aggiunta della componente MDBs è stata estremamente positiva, perché le banche di sviluppo sono per loro partner strategici. Tra tutti, sicuramente per
 UNOPS è strategica la WB - e segnalo che mi hanno passato (se non lo avete già) il contatto di tal Enzo De Laurentis, italiano che fino al 30 novembre è stato Chief Procurement Officer di WB e ora è in pensione, segnalando che a loro avviso sarebbe un ottimo
 facilitatore. 
 
Ciò premesso, come anticipato telefonicamente ad Alessandra, l’evento era stato pensato in due parti:
una prima parte divulgativa e di natura generale (i tricks of the trade, che consentano alle imprese italiane di massimizzare le possibilità di successo nelle loro partecipazioni), che seguiva UNOPS e che adesso vedrebbe direi una regia congiunta
 UNOPS-ICE. A tale evento sarebbero seguite presentazioni individuali
delle OOII/MDBs in merito alle loro effettive e concrete esigenze di procurement. Questo momento ci sembra particolarmente importante, in quanto consentirà alle OOII coinvolte di segnalare con anticipo e precisione i settori per loro di particolare
 interesse (FAO ad esempio ha segnalato di volere incrementare la concorrenza nel proprio procurement relativo ai semi e alle macchine agricole), massimizzando l’efficacia e la concretezza dell’evento. Segnalo peraltro che tra le onusiane abbiamo finora raccolto
 il positivo interesse di UNICEF, UNHCR, UNDP, UNIDO, FAO, IFAD, WFP (ed è probabile che si aggiunga anche l’OIM). Per come l’abbiamo pensata, queste presentazioni individuali si terrebbero in stanze diverse e divise in raggruppamenti tematici, al fine di differenziare
 il programma in base alle esigenze delle imprese.  Il programma quindi sarebbe:
 
MAIN EVENT 9:30-11:00 – saluto di benvenuto del VM, interventi di Direttori Generali DGCS e DGSP, UNOPS e ICE
 
PANELS (11:00-13:15)
§ 
Room 1
(humanitarian): UNHCR pitch 11:00-11:45; UNICEF pitch 11:45-12:30; WFP pitch 12:30-13:15
§ 
Room 2
(food security and agriculture): WFP pitch 11:00-11:45; FAO pitch 11:45-12:30; IFAD pitch 12:30-13:15;

§ 
Room 3
(development agencies): UNDP pitch 11:00-11:45; UNIDO pitch 11:45-12:30; OIM pitch 12:30-13:15
§ 
Room 4
(MDBs):
Diteci se questa proposta è compatibile rispetto alle vostre aspettative, o se avete suggerimenti. Con riguardo alle banche da invitare, concordiamo senz’altro con WB, ADB, BEI,
 BERS e IDB – magari Carlo ne ha in mente altre?
 
Propongo in ogni caso una VTC tra noi (DGCS, DGSP, ICE –
se potete datemi magari le vostre disponibilità), Codeway e UNOPS a metà della prossima settimana, per chiudere sulle componenti chiave dell’evento (in primis il programma) e avviare i follow-up - il più importante dei quali secondo me, come segnalava
 Alessandra, è segnalare a Codeway le imprese potenzialmente interessate, magari tramite una tabellina di matching tra l’impresa e la banca/l’OI che maggiormente le interessa.

 
Grazie davvero per un feedback. Un caro saluto a tutti (e scusate la mail lunga!)
 
Filippo

Kære Asbjørn,
 
Tak for din mail. Jeg har allerede forinden mødet i dag med UNOPS været i dialog med MULTI-kollega Anine Hagemann, i Rikkes fravær.
 
Så jeg er allerede informeret om den responsplan, der er iværksat for UNOPS. Jeg er dog samtidig bekendt med, at andre donorer har overvejet om UNOPS
 eller UNDRR var den kanal de ønskede at kanalisere midler igennem til Santiago Netværket, idet der er en valgmulighed her. Jeg spurgte derfor ind hertil på mødet med UNOPS i dag. Jeg forstår dog, at uanset om midlerne kanaliseres via UNOPS eller UNPS, så vil
 det være UNOPS der bliver manager for midlerne.
 
Tak for tilbuddet om at række ud til dig hvis spørgsmål. Vi går i gang med forberedelse af et dansk bidrag til Santiago Netværket for tab og skader
 i efteråret 2023, med henblik på udmøntning af dansk pledge (givet ved COP26) i de første måneder af 2024. I den forbindelse er det meget muligt, at vi får brug for yderligere oplysninger om UNOPS, så jeg vil sætte pris på at kunne kontakte dig herom.
 
Bh. Jette

Dear colleagues
Today, on World Refugee Day, let's take a moment to acknowledge the incredible strength and resilience of millions of refugees and host communities whose lives have been impacted by displacement.World Refugee Day serves as a reminder of the ongoing displacement crisis. We are deeply committed to supporting displacement-affected communities. We believe that everyone deserves an opportunity to build a life of their own, choosing and contributing to the societies in which they live. In particular, I want to highlight the great work of three of our engagements that contribute to supporting refugees around the world:The Lives in Dignity Grant Facility funded by the EU, which provides refugees, host communities, and other displacement-affected people with the resources and agency to design and implement solutions that foster self-reliance. Since 2021, LiD has allocated $27 million to a diverse group of implementing partners, half of which are local. The facility's geographic scope includes 14 projects across 15 countries in Asia, Latin America, and Sub-Saharan Africa.Cities Alliance has just launched the Supporting Urban Integration of Displacement-Affected Communities (SUIDAC) programme in Sub-Saharan Africa, supported by a €30 million grant from the EU. This four-year initiative targets cities in DRC, Ethiopia, Somalia, Sudan, and Uganda, aiming to enhance the integration of refugees and their host communities and improving self-reliance, social cohesion, and local governance through infrastructure and sustainable urban planning. The Platform on Disaster Displacement plays a crucial role in advocating for refugees and promoting solutions for governments to welcome and support them. Their work supports those fleeing the devastation of natural disasters, so that they receive the protection and assistance they deserve.On this World Refugee Day, I encourage you to:Watch these inspiring stories of resilience from the LiD-funded project in Uganda and South Sudan. Also this short video on the work of the LiD Grant FacilityBe an advocate: Share World Refugee Day information and resources with your networks using #WithRefugees, #WorldRefugeeDay and #UNOPS.Consider volunteering your time or donating to organizations supporting people affected by displacementAll the best,Andrew

Subject: INTERNAL - Switzerland - update
Body:
Dear all
Summary: This is to update you on my regular informal call with the UNOPS focal point at SDC, the Swiss Agency for Development Cooperation (SDC/Martin Borgeaud, MB) on 19 June. The tone remains tepid but Switzerland continue to sign agreements for existing & related projects (Palestine, Cities Alliance, North Macedonia...) Jorge scheduled to speak with Patricia Danzi and team on 6 August.
On the June EB / closed session: SDC feels true dialogue (beyond "communications exercise") is still missing and that "SDC questions are still not answered". I urged MB/SDC to submit their questions in writing, for us to respond more effectively and help us to move forward. MB will follow up to see if that is desirable. I also reminded that perm rep did not respond, and SDC Head of Agency only recently agreed, to speak bilaterally with JMdS. MB shared they felt "different bilateral conversations with different EB members / countries are not always useful and cannot replace effective and transparent conversations through existing governance structures" Recovery of S3i funds
MB questioned whether paying USD 1 million to OLA for an investigation on the recovery of S3i funds is money well spent and asked what is the realistic chance of recovering any of the misused funds.Partnership / Agreements 
MB repeated "UNOPS is not a priority organisation for Switzerland"; they are still not comfortable with "tone from the top" (perception  of policy over operations; too quick to turn the page; impunity)  MB is following ongoing negotiations regarding the transfer of Swiss funds to the Santiago Network (GPO) and the Platform on Disaster Displacement (GPO) and others, confirming with the additional step of a PRA (partner risk assessment) Agreements are likely to be approved - though all must be signed off by Head of Agency.SDC/MB welcome the engagement with IAIG, seen as "very important and always helpful"MB and I will speak again in July, before Jorge and Patricia's scheduled call (6 August). Following which, we will plan for 2024 dialogue.
Happy to answer any specific / further questions.Best wishes
Louise

I am writing in my capacity as the coordinator for the University of Copenhagen initiative,
HUM:Global / Global Humanities and organizer of our forthcoming launch event.
For the launch entitled Narrating Global Conflict, we are planning a one-day conference with a slightly non-conventional program and would like to invite
UNOPS chief Mr. Jorge Da Silva as a speaker. My contact at the UN,
Najam UI Assar advised me to contact you in this regard.
 
According to the (working) preliminary program, we would like to invite Mr Da Silva to be in conversation with one of the senior researchers at HUM:Global (see
People – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk)) at 14:00 for 45-60 minutes. We are open to the suggestion of a different time in the bracket 12:00 – 16:00.
 
Please find a description of the theme below. We very much hope that Mr Da Silva will be enthusiastic about participating – the work of UNOPS is important to bring to this event, not least because of the global nature
 of the organization and the different perspectives it will bring to the discussion.
 
Narrating Global Conflict
 
At a time when the world is ablaze with perilous conflagration, entrenched geopolitical struggles, and atrocious warfare – scholars, journalists, artists, activists, and civilians – whether up
 close or from afar – are trying to make sense of the senseless. 
 
Scholars might try to uncover the roots or dynamics of a conflict, while journalists cover the events on the ground and the human experiences of the same. Artists articulate the conflicted emotions
 or utter hopelessness of warfare, while activists may mobilize to shine a light on the oppressed, the suffering or the persecuted, or to instill moral indignation and hope amidst carnage. And civilians, citizens, human beings – we absorb, we consume, we engage,
 we share, we debate, we reject, we ignore, we act. 
All of us partake in globally interwoven narrations of conflict.
 
This public conference seeks to explore and connect how different professions narrate conflicts across time and space. It takes artistic expressions, personal accounts, and academic and professional
 analysis equally seriously. We do this both to unpack the innate qualities they possess as practices of sensemaking, and how they blend across a digitized, globalized interactive space to create sustained tropes of conflict and resolution in our time. Our
 aim, therefore, is sustain a dialogue between perspectives on global conflict at a historical moment when professional compartmentalization, ideological schisms and political naming and shaming risk tearing the critical, free, frank and interrogative exchange
 that universities are meant to lift up apart.
 
Narrating global conflict is directed towards scholars and students at the University of Copenhagen and the wider interested audience. As such, all our activities are open to the public.
 
I look forward to hearing from you at your earliest convenience.
 
Warm regards
Nicol Marie Foulkes Savinetti

Hi SeynabouThanks for the call the other day, always lovely to catch up as always, and thanks for the clarifications on the Cote d'Ivoire project.  So I spoke with WHO HQ energy expert after we chatted, and he's keen to have a chat with us - can you suggest me a couple of days and times next week that work for you? Solarisation of health care facilities is one piece of the broader puzzle :) Looking forward to hearing from youBest wishes Louise 
I completely agree on the critical importance of training. This is indeed a fundamental aspect.In some cases, however, training covers particularly the preventive maintenance, while a budget allocation is still needed in case of future need for spare parts or to pay the curative maintenance interventions from specialized technicians. Often the health facilities do not have the budget to cover these curative maintenance costs, and in many cases project funds do not consider this long-term budget allocation. In some cases this happens because all the grant needs to be spent by a certain date, and this is not compatible with long term and future disbursements. Do you know by any chance if such curative maintenance budget and relevant long-term disbursements have been considered by the donors in the below cases, and what the disbursement arrangements are? I look forward to continuing these conversations with you, and to talking with your colleagues in charge of the health-care facilities solarization project in Cote D´Ivoire at your/their earliest convenience, if helpful.

Since many of you have expressed interest in the SDC Partner Risk Assessment, I am providing all the information about the process as well as links to specific files which you can also find in the corporate drive folder for SDC Partner Risk Assessment:SDC ToR for selecting a firm to carry out the PRA: in Serbia, the PRA was conducted by the audit firm DFK during October-November 2022, before signing the contract with SDC for the PRO programme in December 2022.A questionnaire with 48 questions divided into following areas: legal, governance, accounting and reporting, cash management, budgeting, audit, procurement, HR, PM, Asset, ICT. The next update is planned for the end of June 2024. 
Also, I am copying colleagues from RSMCO who participated in the process in North Macedonia (SDC used the PRA from Serbia) and are equally informed about the PRA process.

Jeg håber alt er godt i Oslo - og at sommeren også langsomt er ved at komme til jer med varmere vejr og sol. 


 


Jeg rækker ud til dig mhp. at drøfte et projekt som muligvis kunne være i norsk interesse i Moldova. Jeg vedlægger en kort konceptnote om projektet, som handler om migrationsbygningen i Chișinău,
 som er i meget dårlig stand. Bygningen er modtagecenter for de over 115.000 ukrainske flygtninge som indtil videre er flygtet til Moldova, hvoraf langt de fleste er udsatte borgere. 


 


Myndighederne i Moldova har meget vanskeligt ved at håndtere den store strøm af flygtninge og har ad flere omgange anmodet om hjælp til genopbygning af infrastruktur til håndteringen.
 Det vedlagte projekt er en særlig stor prioritet fra Moldova, som omhandler en første fase som vil skulle kortlægge behovene og udarbejde et konkret forslag til udbygningen af faciliteterne.

 af andre eller flere donorer). Dvs. en analyse af hob, et concept design, en projekt plan samt budgetestimater for en fuld genopbygning. 


 


Jeg håber at I finder projektet interessant, der som bekendt er meget efterspurgt i Moldova til håndtering af de mange ukrainske flygtninge. 


 


Hvis I har interesse for projektet, vil vi naturligvis meget gerne mødes med henblik på at drøfte nærmere om videre vej frem. 


 


Mvh

Subject: UN-SPBF & UNOPS collaboration - support scenarios and additional information
Body:
Dear Shereen, Rehana and Youssif,  
Many thanks again for the discussion with our Geneva team. We are keen to find solutions to support you, so with thanks to the Geneva team, below are (1) some considerations for the potential scenarios, and (2) additional information related to hosting.

1. Potential scenarios of support

A. UNOPS provides regular support to UN SPBF: In this scenario, UNEP would keep the fiduciary role while UNOPS is in charge of procurement, HR, organising workshops etc. There is no guarantee that this would be cheaper than what UNEP is already charging you - managing multi-donor agreements is costly; we may even be more expensive. (UNOPS delivers services on a full cost recovery basis, and each engagement agreement between UNOPS and partner shall cover direct and indirect costs incurred by UNOPS in relation to the execution of the activities. Direct costs are determined using activity-based costing principles, while indirect costs are incurred by the management and administration of UNOPS activities and policies and charged as a fee percentage.)

B. Joint hosting between UNOPS and UNEP: Given the size of the annual budget of Transformers, this solution is likely too costly, as UNEP and UNOPS would both charge you their costs.

C. UNOPS hosting Transformers: In this scenario, your annual budget is not an issue, but UNOPS would need to obtain high level guarantees that there is full support for this solution on UNEP's side. Should this be identified as the suitable option, I stand ready to facilitate this, for example in the form of a high level exchange between our EDs on this matter. At this stage, without seeing your detailed budget, we cannot guarantee that we would be cheaper than UNEP - in fact, part of the process to assess the eligibility of a prospective hosted engagement is the review of the multi year work plan and budget. However, our management fees would be topped at 7%. In terms of connections with your broader work at UN-SPBF, we could explore options that would allow UNEP to maintain its normative function in Transformers' work, and where coordination between Transformers and UN-SPBF could continue.
2. Additional information related to hosting

A. Documentation: Please see attached a general overview of what being hosted by UNOPS means, which could be used for your board. In addition, our comprehensive guidelines on welcoming new hosted engagements are also attached. The key steps to join as a hosted entity are detailed on page 13. The Geneva team can walk you through the key steps during a call.

B. Overview of the next steps:

1. Supporting documents: To assess the eligibility and kick start the due diligence with our HQ, we would need the following from you: information related to any multi-year funding you have (donors, start and end date), your engagement workplan and budget, your board composition and the proposed way forward on the legal personality of Transformers (i.e. a paragraph describing your current legal status, how you are envisioning the process of your legal transformation and the role of the board). 

2. Board approval: We would need the official decision of your board to move towards UNOPS as a hosted entity to be able to start the proposal.

3. Hosting Proposal and internal reviews: We need some more key documents such as your organigramme for the business analysis and the proposal. After the review of your key supporting documents (see a), we can start putting together the first version of the proposal. To give you an idea of what is required, please see here. We will need UN-SPBF and UNOPS to work on this jointly. In parallel, we will also work on internal reviews.
4. Hosting agreement and other agreements: Development of Joint Hosting Agreement (JHA) and the Bilateral Legal Agreements.

We stand available should you have any questions, and are happy to organize a follow-up call at your convenience. Wishing you a lovely weekend in the meantime!

All the best, 
Jean-François, Argita, Aurélie and Kajsa

--

Subject: Mulighed for at briefe relevante medarbejdere i migrations- samt fred- og stabiliseringsafdelingerne om Cities Alliance
Body:
Kære Khadije, 
Det var super godt at møde dig i dag. 

Som jeg kort nævnte er Cities Alliance en FN-multi-donor fond, der opererer under UNOPS' paraply, med det mål at bekæmpe fattigdom i byområder og fremme bæredygtig udvikling. Fonden opererer i 88 lande med støtte fra civilsamfundet, lokale myndigheder og multilaterale organisationer.  Medlemslandene inkluderer bl.a Sverige, Tyskland, Frankrig, Storbritannien og USA.
Vi ser gode strategiske synergier mellem Cities Alliance og Danmarks udviklingsprioriteter; migration, klimaforandringer, ligestilling og fattigdom.
I sidste måned har vi sammen med kollegaer fra Cities Alliance været forbi Asiatisk Plads til et møde med Winnie Estrup Petersen, leder i klimaafdelingen, for at give en kort orientering om de kapaciteter Cities Alliance har - og hvordan de kan bidrage til at indfri danske udviklingspolitiske prioriteter. Vi blev henvist til jer i Migration, fred og stabiliseringsafdelingen. 
Det er naturligvis meget oplagt, da Cities Alliance i øjeblikket arbejder på større migrationsprojekter, herunder et projekt finansieret af EU om tvungen fordrivelse grundet klima og konflikter i 12 byer fordelt over 5 lande i Østafrika. Når folk fordrives, flytter de generelt til sekundære byer, ofte i nabolande. Den vedvarende nød og mangel på muligheder i disse nye byer får dem ofte til at migrere videre med et ønske om at nå destinationer uden for Afrika.
Jeg vedlægger til din orientering en præsentation af Cities Alliance. 
Hvis det har interesse, kommer Asbjørn og jeg meget gerne forbi jer sammen med vores kollega fra Cities Alliance for at give en briefing. 
På forhånd mange tak og rigtig god weekend. 
De bedste hilsenerNaimo

Subject: Meeting with UK FCDO’s Director for Multilateral Affairs and Human Rights.
Body:
Dear Asbjorn, I hope you had a nice weekend! The UN Director in Brussels organised a meeting last Friday between the Brussels Head of Agencies and Freya Jackson, UK FCDO’s Director for Multilateral Affairs and Human Rights. Sharing the meeting notes, in case of interest. Some points relate to the SoF: Director Freya Jackson’s visit to Brussels on 19 July, the first in over a year and one taking place within two weeks of the start of the new mandate of the Labour-led British government, is meant to signal the importance for the new UK government of the relationship with the EU.  An importance highlighted on the other side of the partnership by the reelected President of the European Commission in her political guidelines. Another signal that the new government is trying to send, as its manifesto also underlined, is a commitment to multilateralism, which is seen as indispensable to tackling global challenges, and to the rule of law. Freya’s team will focus on managing the expectations of the new government with relation to the SOF. There’s a feeling that the SOF and UNGA might be two good opportunities for the new government to set out their views and speak to the world. On Rev 2 of the Pact. UK are still processing the text but overall feel very positive. However, they flagged some concerns on language around disarmament and the development of a binding agreement on lethal autonomous weapons. On IFA reform -an expected new priority for the new Foreign Secretary-, UK are looking at the new language IFI’s reform and they consider themselves forward leaning on many aspects. There’s an appetite to go forward.  One of his first calls upon arriving in his function was to PM of Barbados Mia Mottley. On participation at the Summit of the Future, they are quite confident that the UK will be come at the highest levels, PM, Foreign Secretary and Development Minister -may be a sequencing rather than all coming at once, with PM participating at the SOF, but to be confirmed and FCDO at UNGA, given the clash of both high-level meetings with the yearly Labour party conference.
 The meeting also covered other issues i.e. recommendations to put forward to the new Foreign Secretary besides the importance of engagement and follow up to the SOF, such as the use of confiscated and frozen assets and their return to address human rights and high-priority development needs. The UK government was praised by participants for its announced commitment to the human rights economy and for resuming the funding of UNRWA. Participants also expressed that the 'return of UK' in the development sphere (first through the new strategy, now with a new government) was considered positive, not least given the important role the UK played in the past by promoting effectiveness, results orientation etc. in the system, combined with significant financial muscle to help push these reforms. While noting that the fiscal space remains limited, signals from the new government are positive and the UN looks forward to strengthening its partnership with the UK.
Kind regardsLaetitia

First of all I want to thank you very much for your excellent work on finding a workable model for a partnership with the Olena Zelenska Foundation to construct the 10 foster family homes in Ukraine! I am so impressed by your pragmatic, fast and solution oriented approach to rapidly come up with workable options that would get the job done! 
Unfortunately the donor AP Møller Foundation and the Ministry of Business found our added costs to be too high. Even though our management fee is only 6.0%, the model would entail increased costs from the donor side of 1,4M USD equal to a 30% budget increase. They found this too high and will therefore instead do a public tender to find someone to supervise the implementation of the project. 
Even though we did not win the project this time around, we can be very proud to be considered the first ones to be called upon when a complex matter has to be solved in a pragmatic way. We clearly demonstrated our ability to do precisely this - and we have a good reputation in the donor community in Denmark that we can continue to build upon to grow our portfolio in Ukraine and beyond. 
We will now engage more directly with the AP Møller Foundation to explore opportunities for other projects. 
Once again - a huge thanks to you for your hard work on this!

Subject: Re: Donationer til Olena Zelenska Fonden
Body:
Kære Simon
Beklager langsommeligt svar herfra - der skyldes sommerferie. 
Jeg er naturligvis ærgerlig over, at I ikke ønsker at gå videre med UNOPS som implementeringspartner pga. prisen. Det er dog samtidig helt forståeligt - og vi ville under alle omstændigheder finde det problematisk at indgå et samarbejde, som Olena Zelenska Fonden grundlæggende ikke ønsker. 
I forhold til omkostningsniveauet skal vores oplæg bl.a. ses i lyset af, at vi ikke har haft indblik i de af Olena Zelenska Fonden skønnede momkostninger - som muligvis dækker over nogle af de opgaver, som I, UM og EIFO oprindeligt anmodede om vores hjælp til at udføre. 
Jeg synes det lyder fornuftigt med et offentligt udbud på monitorering af de to projekter, og håber at I ad den vej kan finde en farbar vej. 
Endelig håber jeg at vores input har bidraget til at skabe lidt mere klarhed over opgaverne i projektet, potentielle udfordringer og mulige løsninger. 
Jeg glæder mig til at følge med i projektets udførelse og håber at I snarest får mulighed for at igangsætte. I må endelig række ud igen hvis behov for input herfra. 
Såfremt der fremadrettet opstår ønske fra danske fonde eller virksomheder om at udføre infrastrukturprojekter eller indkøb af varer til fx Ukraine, står vi naturligvis til rådighed. En tidlig inddragelse af UNOPS kan også sikre, at vi sammen får skruet et mere realistisk og rimeligt budget sammen. 
Fortsat rigtig god sommer!
MvhAsbjørn

Kære Asbjørn
 
Jeg har forsøgt at ringe et par gange for at give dig en update på arbejdet med donationerne til Olena Zelenska Fonden, så nu får du en mail i stedet.

 
Vi har som bekendt arbejdet med modellen, hvor UNOPS står for implementeringen. Olena Zelenska Fonden og førstedamen har imidlertid udtrykt, at de finder den yderligere omkostning

Vi arbejder nu med en model, hvor Erhvervsstyrelsen laver et udbud med en lavere makspris om at monitorere de to projekter og følge Olena Zelenska Fondens implementering. Det

Subject: Invitation: Breakfast Briefing with UN Under-Secretary-General and UNOPS Executive Director, Jorge Moreira da Silva - September 10
Body:
Dear,
We are very pleased to invite you to a breakfast briefing with the UN Under-Secretary-General, Executive Director for UNOPS, and head of the UN City in Copenhagen, Mr. Jorge Moreira da Silva on September 10, at 8:30 AM in the UN City in Nordhavn. 
This breakfast session will be an opportunity to gain insights into UNOPS (the only UN agency headquartered in Denmark) and the role as the UN system’s implementer that provides the practical solutions on behalf of donors such as Denmark - especially in fragile and conflict affected areas. It is one of the major UN agencies with +5.500 staff that only does implementation on the ground in 80+ countries throughout the globe. 
The Under-Secretary-General would also like to informally brief you and your colleagues about the current situations in some of the most conflict affected areas such as Ukraine and Gaza where UNOPS operates and delivers aid on behalf of eg. Denmark.
Finally the breakfast session could be an opportunity to touch upon Danish companies position as the second largest suppliers to the UN in 2023, where the UN system purchased goods and services from Danish companies for a bit more than 1 billion USD - only surpassed by the USA.
The Under-Secretary-General would be happy to answer your questions during the breakfast.    
We would greatly appreciate it if you could let us know if you or a colleague of yours would be able to attend the breakfast background briefing by sending an email to naimoh@unops.org.  
Looking very much to seeing you and your colleagues. 
Best regards,Asbjørn

Subject: Questions regarding budget for Domanivka project
Body:
Dear Anne and Vasyl, 
Thank you for your email and inquiries regarding the budget for the Domanivka project. Apologies for my late response which is entirely my fault as I was away on holiday, 
I understand that your question related to the fact that the project itself costs about 950,000 USD but that the additional overhead costs amounted to a total of about 600,000 USD, which seemed excessive. While the estimated 14 month duration for the Domanivka project is in itself a rather complex project (see timeline here), the main reason for the costs is that most of it actually relates to the 3 months extension of the current infrastructure project. Thus, the lion's share of the 600K is attributable to the upcoming Arkas High School restoration project. Due to Domanivka's remoteness from Mykolaiv city, it necessitates addition of a driver for the duration of the project and an additional car, which upon completion will be handed over to the beneficiary, in agreement with you.The personnel structure includes addition of a dedicated WASH engineer for the duration of the project;Most importantly - as mentioned above, the duration of the project adds 3 extra months to the current duration of our common infrastructure project. This means that pending the extension of the Arkas project early next year, this amendment will already ensure the extension of the entire project team structure for extra 3 months. That project structure will of course be serving both Domanivka and Arkas functions, but we can not extend the project in only one part. Hence, this extension will also cover 3 extra months for the Arkas project.Finally, our Finance Team by mistake incurred an increased cost for the use of local and shared UNOPS services (from USD 6,500 to USD 6,681 per month) on the entire duration of the infrastructure project, while this should of course only be on the extended months. This reduces the overall costs with about 30K. To give an indication of the distribution of costs between the Arkas and Domanivka project, please find here a spreadsheet where Elene has kindly provided a detailed breakdown - and tried to make a split between the two projects. In the last column we showed the distribution of personnel costs 50%-50% between Domanivka and Arkas, which was the easiest way to make a split. But in fact, it could be assume that the real costs attributed to Arkas and Domanivka will be 60%-40% in favour of Arkas.
With a 50-50 split it means the the costs for the work attributable to Domanivka will be closer to 341,719 USD - rather than 600K. 
I hope this clarifies and we remain as always available for a meeting to discuss upon your convenience.

Dear Shirley, 
 
Thank you very much for your time last week, it was a great pleasure to meet you and Patricia in person and discuss topics of mutual interest. Based on our conversation,
 we’d like to move forward with the possibility of avoiding a capped fee in our framework agreement, since this is something that UNOPS doesn’t normally do to ensure consonance with our cost-recovery policy. We hereby share more information on our approach
 to fee setting here.
 This is an external document that we share with our stakeholders so they have a clear understanding of the procedures we follow in terms of fee setting, and ensure transparency. In this sense, we can work on a paragraph that details this information in our
 agreement. 
 
Likewise, we are
sharing here
 the latest version of our MoU with updated revisions from our team. 
 
We consider that the framework agreement should reflect that the IDB has no objection to financing the UNOPS fee and eligible expenses within the project, provided
 these are included in the loan account at the borrower's request. In this sense and in alignment with our collaborative goals, we would like to propose that it be stated that the IDB is amenable to covering the UNOPS fee and any eligible expenses related to
 the project. These costs can be incorporated into the loan account upon the borrower's formal request to ensure clarity and mutual understanding.
 
Please let us know of any updates on your side in regards to the fee setting. We are happy to work on the aforementioned paragraph so UNOPS’ cost-recovery policies
 and net zero revenue approach are properly showcased in the agreement, to ensure transparency in our operations and with stakeholders. 
 
Warm regards,

Subject: Executive Board, Second Regular Session, August 26-29
Body:
Dear Agnes, 
I hope this email finds you well - somewhere warm and sunny!  
As usual, I wanted to provide you with a brief and informal overview of the UNOPS relevant topics to be discussed at the upcoming Executive Board session on August 26-29. 
You might already have noticed that all the relevant documents as well as the draft agenda have been uploaded to the UNOPS website and can be found here. 
On substance the topics relevant specifically to UNOPS relates to the following: A draft terms of reference for the review of UNOPS implementation of the Comprehensive Response PlanAn information note on UNOPS strategy for the implementation of the Process Innovation and Digitalisation ProgrammeInformation note on the estimated amount remaining of undisbursed excess reserve fundsThe annual report on the procurement activities of the UN system in 2023 + annexAd 1) - ToR for review of implementation of the Comprehensive Response PlanAn informal session about this topic is scheduled for 19 August. 
Upon request from the EB, UNOPS' Internal Audit and Investigation Group (IAIG) has prepared a draft ToR for the upcoming second review of UNOPS' implementation of the Comprehensive Response Plan (CPR). This document was also presented to the EB at the June EB session. 
This second review will seek to validate/dismiss that UNOPS has in fact implemented the remaining action points in the CPR and thereby adhered to the recommendations by KPMG following the S3i independent review. The review is meant to start in 2025 when all but one recommendation will have been concluded (the digitisation programme (PID) - which runs until 2025). 
Ad 2) Implementation of the Process Innovation and Digitalisation ProgrammeAn informal session about this topic is scheduled for 19 August. 

Upon request from the EB, UNOPS has provided an extensive information note with a roadmap for the PID's scope, progress, milestones, budget, governance and risk management, KPIs and stakeholder engagement. 
The progress in implementation - as well as challenges - will be reported in the monthly briefings to the EB until the first EB session in January / February 2025. 
Ad 3) Estimated remaining excessive reserve fundsAn informal session about this topic is scheduled for 19 August. 
UNOPS estimates that out of the 123.8M USD, only 1.5M will be undisbursed by the end of 2024, which is the deadline provided by the EB. As per June 2024, only 8.5M USD remains in the reserve, which is focused on 10 government partners - of which one is the UK. 
The EB will decide on the use of the remaining funds at the first session in 2025. 
Ad 4) Estimated remaining excessive reserve fundsAn informal session about this topic is scheduled for 23 August. 
The annual procurement report shows that the UN procured goods and services worth almost 25B in 2023 - a decrease by 15.7%. 5B was procured from least developed countries. 
Scheduled Informal Sessions19 August, 10 am - 1 pm: ToR for review on UNOPS implementation of the CRPRoadmap for the PID programmeRemaining funds in excess reserve23 August 10 am - 12 pmProcurement report 
I hope this gives you a somewhat overview of the topics to be discussed at the August EB session. 
I also hope that you might be available during next week for an informal chat. where we could go through the topics, clarify potential questions bilaterally and get your initial take on the topics. 
If so - please do let me know when it might suit you to meet online next week. 
Looking forward to hearing back from you. 
Best regards,Asbjørn

Directors, RRs and colleagues,



We are currently engaging closely with UNOPS to enhance our collaboration
mainly on programmatic matters. One key expected outcome is a UN-Habitat and UNOPS Action Plan, which we aim to finalize and sign during WUF12.


To facilitate this process, I would appreciate your kind support to
assign a focal point from your respective division and regional office to coordinate
on this. Given the time constraints, kindly assign your focal points by COB
Tuesday, 30th July.


Workplan:



Stocktake (1st week of August):
 We plan to conduct a stocktake on the current engagement of your divisions and regional offices with UNOPS, focusing on normative and operational work. This will involve a systematic approach to mapping ongoing and planned activities to identify potential
 thematic areas and synergies.



Consultations (second half
 of August): To gain a clearer understanding of the inputs,
we will conduct consultations to discuss the scope and gather ideas, thoughts, comments, and suggestions.

MOH has expressed a desire to source these through the UNOPS Bangladesh Country office if the commercial terms remain the same or are more advantageous to the GoB. The Ministry is preparing the business case, and the process for internal approvals to request this change is already in progress. The main advantages cited by MOH are the ease of follow-up and interaction with a local UNOPS office in the local language. GF clarified that the CCM would have to approve the request before the GF considers it, and then the CCM will again need to approve the changed implementation arrangements should the GF approve this. Both GF and UNOPS will keenly follow progress and keep each other praised on progress. GF cannot comment further on this until a formal request reaches them from the CCM.Medical Waste Management: The investment committee of the GF has yellow-lighted a potential medical waste management project for Bangladesh from the remaining Covid 19 response funds. GF will informally share the proposal which was sent to the IC. The condition placed by the IC is that a more detailed technical proposal be developed and greenlighted by the IC. GF expects the detailed proposal to be developed in August- September to go back to the IC in September for full greenlighting. The implementation end date cannot cross Dec 31, 2025, as things stand. The IC yellow light assumes implementation by UNOPS, and this will be clarified with ADG Flora next week to understand the Government's preference. The next steps should take final shape during the GF mission to Bangladesh in September. UNOPS mentioned that because of the short implementation timeline and UNOPS due diligence in infrastructure projects, it may be good for UNOPS to be involved closely in the next steps. Oxygen Guidelines- DGHS has developed draft oxygen management guidelines for Bangladesh with support from UNICEF. The oxygen guidelines ownership within the DGHS rests with NEMEW & TC. NEMEW & TC has expressed reservations about the guidelines and has informally requested UNOPS to review them to address their concerns. Dear James and Kevin,
 
I hope this email finds you well.
 
I apologize for the delay in providing project updates. I was finally able to connect after returning to Sri Lanka this morning. As you're
 aware, the situation in Bangladesh has been extremely challenging, and the lack of internet connectivity, curfew, etc. disrupted our day-to-day work and even internal team communications.
 
While I will be sending the detailed monthly highlight report early next week, I wanted to provide some key updates that I know you are eager
 to hear about.
 
Handed Over Sites
As discussed in our last coordination meeting, we conducted retesting at NIDCH and Manikganj with NMEP operators and engineers present. The
 plants were operational for approximately 6 hours per day over three days, and the purity levels were consistently above 93%. Unfortunately, the planned training sessions requested by NMEP had to be postponed due to ongoing issues. The operators are now more
 confident in running the plants, and we stressed the importance of daily operations to maintain performance.

 
Completed Sites (With Power)
Following advice from the Line Director - CDC, the NMEP team will take over the three sites where the PSA plant is already connected to the
 existing substation. Our goal was to complete these handovers by July 2024, but this timeline will need to be adjusted.
 
Completed Sites (Without Power)
NMEP's recent decision not to take over sites without power has significant implications for project handovers, site security, the DNP period,
 and our operational expenditure. While we understand the necessity of fully completed sites, we are concerned about the critical impacts of this decision on our plans. I will provide a detailed explanation in a separate email.
 
The good news is that there has been no damage to the sites from the ongoing demonstration activities, and our team is working diligently
 to ensure their security as some site locations are really sensitive.
 
Ongoing sites (Ishwardi & Bandarban)
The construction activities are underway but slow progress due to the absence of workers due to the movement restrictions in place.
 
Transformers
On behalf of NMEP, I want to update you on the meeting held on 15th July 2024 by LD-CDC with the relevant hospital directors. The roles and
 responsibilities concerning transformers were clearly outlined. Our colleagues Mr.Maruf, Mr.Hashan, and Mr.Fahad attended the meeting, and I will provide a detailed update in the coordination meeting on 25th July 2024. We are hopeful that things will proceed
 smoothly.
 
Upcoming Meeting
Given the current situation in Bangladesh, NMEP's participation in the 25th July 2024 meeting is uncertain. However, I suggest we proceed
 with the meeting so I can provide further updates on the project status.
 
Thank you for your understanding and patience. 
 
We all pray for the safety of our team and for the situation to be resolved in Bangladesh soon and bring the team together.
 





Thank You!


Best Regards!

 made to fight the climate emergency, and the ability to make change happen. UNOPS - with our focus on operations - helps bridge the implementation gap - and Denmark has a clear political convening power on this topic.

OFFICIAL






Hi Asbjorn,
 
You so kindly share reading with me, that I thought I’d return the favour for once! Not at all required reading but attaching in case of interest some
 of Minister Dodds’s academic papers on her specialism, public administration reform.
 
Dodds, A., Obradovic-Wochnik, J., & Badran, A. (2014). The new institutionalism in the context of Kosovo's transition: regulatory institutions
 in contested states. East European Politics, 30(4), 436-457.
 
This article explores the new institutionalist literature in political economy in the context of Kosovo's contested statehood, focusing on institutional
 arbitrage and legitimacy. This article considers both the consequences of institutions for actors' behaviour and the norms that shape this, as well as the factors determining the legitimacy of institutions. In doing so, it combines the new institutionalist
 theory with documentary and interview material collected during research on energy regulation in one contested state, Kosovo. Rather than singling out one particular variety of “new institutionalism”, the article attempts to blend insights from historical
 (or “political”), rational choice, and sociological institutionalism.
 
Dodds, A., & Paskins, D. (2011). Top-down or bottom-up: The real choice for public services?. Journal of Poverty and Social Justice, 19(1),
 51-61.
 
This article considers two contrasting approaches to reforming public services in order to meet the needs of people living in poverty.
 The first approach is top-down, involves categorising individuals (as ‘hard to help’, ‘at risk’, etc) and invokes scientific backing for justification. The second approach is bottom-up, emancipatory, relates to people as individuals and treats people who have
 experience of poverty and social exclusion as experts. The article examines each approach through providing brief examples in the fields of unemployment and parenting policy – two fields that have been central to theories of ‘cycles of deprivation’. It is
 suggested here that the two approaches differ in terms of their scale, type of user involvement and type of evidence that is used for their legitimation. While the article suggests that direct comparison between the two approaches is difficult, it highlights
 the prevalence of top-down approaches towards services for people living in poverty, despite increasing support for bottom-up approaches in other policy areas.
 
Kelly, J., & Dodds, A. (2012). Public administration in an age of austerity: The future of the discipline. Public Policy and Administration, 27(3),
 199-211.
 
Reflecting changes in the nature of governance, some have questioned whether Public Administration is now an historical anachronism. While
 a legitimate debate exists between sceptics and optimists, this special issue demonstrates grounds for optimism by indicating the continuing diversity and adaptability of the field of Public Administration. In this introduction, we first sketch the variety
 of intellectual traditions which comprise the field of modern Public Administration. We then consider institutional challenges facing the subject given considerable pressures towards disciplinary fragmentation, and ideological challenges arising from a new
 distrust of public provision in the UK. Despite these challenges, Public Administration continues to provide a framework to analyse the practice of government and governance, governing institutions and traditions, and their wider sociological context. It can
 also directly inform policy reform – even if this endeavour can have its own pitfalls and pratfalls for the ‘engaged’ academic. We further suggest that, rather than lacking theoretical rigour, new approaches are developing that recognise the structural and
 political nature of the determinants of public administration. Finally, we highlight the richness of modern comparative work in Public Administration. Researchers can usefully look beyond the Atlantic relationship for theoretical enhancement and also consider
 more seriously the recursive and complex nature of international pressures on public administration.
 
 
LIBERALIZATION AND THE PUBLIC SECTOR: THE PRE‐EMINENT
 ROLE OF GOVERNMENTS IN THE ‘SALE’ OF HIGHER EDUCATION ABROAD - DODDS - 2009 - Public Administration - Wiley Online Library

 
Much recent scholarship concerning liberalization has emphasized the role of regulatees, rather than governments, in promoting liberalization.
 This article examines such scholarship in the light of an important development in the British and French public sectors—the creation of new agencies (the Education Counselling Service and EduFrance) to ‘sell’ British and French higher education to potential
 international students. The new agencies attempted to induce two things: competition amongst higher education institutions for the recruitment of international students from developed and emerging economy countries, and the commodification of these students.
 This article shows that, contrary to existing theories of liberalization, governments were pre-eminent in pushing forward this liberalization, while higher education institutions attempted to hold it back.
 
Agnes

Subject: Re: Call for Japanese Supplementary Budget concept notes
Body:
Dear Mr. Moustapha TAHIROU,
 
Thank you for your request regarding Japanese Supplementary Fund (JSF).
 
This is Harushi Sakashita as Attache en politique et economie from Embassy of Japan in Benin. I am writing you in terms of JFS on behalf of Mr. KATO.
 
As for the priorities and deadline of a concept note, please kindly follow the guidance below.
[Main contents of a concept note]
               Suggested items to be included in a concept note and a project proposal
- A summary table of the concept note or the proposal
- Background: Include information on emergencies such as sudden natural disasters (floods, droughts, etc.), epidemics of infectious diseases, and significant humanitarian crises
- Four important elements of the project rationale:
1. Urgency: Provide reasons why it cannot wait until the next fiscal year that starts in April in Japan. Discuss the impact of the global food crisis and other unique reasons
 specific to each country.
2. Obligation: Provide reasons why Japan must contribute to address the issue(s) a country office is referring to.
3. Unpredictability: Provide a compelling rationale for why assistance must be increased or strengthened the soonest that was not predictable before March. Additionally, include
 other unique reasons specific to each country.
4. Irreplaceability: Provide reasons why there were no alternative opportunities or irreplaceable options, necessitating a request through the supplementary budget.
- Geography and targeting areas: Provide information on the geographical areas or regions targeted by the project.
- Beneficiaries: Aim to address a range of humanitarian needs, primarily focusing on vulnerable populations significantly impacted by recent events or exacerbated conditions
 since last April.
- Expected results and indicators: Specify expected outcomes of the project and the relevant indicators for measuring progress.
- Programme implementation and coordination: Include details about strategic partnerships, especially if the country office is engaging Japanese entities for project implementation.
- Involvement of Japanese staff: If any Japanese staff member will work in the project, specify their names, positions and roles in the project.
- Gender aspects: Address gender-related considerations within the project.
- Contribution towards Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): Explain how the project contributes to specific SDGs.
- Visibility: Include a plan for public relations and donor visibility during project implementation.
 
- Focus and priority areas;
1. The Women, Peace and Security (WPS) (https://www.mofa.go.jp/press/release/pressite_000001_00123.html).
2. Cross-cutting perspectives for African countries: Regional integration and connectivity, youth engagement, public-private partnerships and adherence to rule of law. This
 priority leads up to the ninth Tokyo International Conference on African Development (TICAD) scheduled for August 2025.
3. Coherence with Governmental Action Plan (PAG 2021-2026)
4. Security cooperation against extremists from Sahel
5. Development cooperation in the northern region of Benin affected by crisis
 
We would very appreciate if you could submit your concept note
by Tuesday 13, August.
 
Let us know if you have any questions.
 
Sincerely yours,
Sakashita

Ambassade du Japon au Bénin

Body:
Buenas tardes colegas, 
 
Como saben, el Fondo ODS ha revisado su estrategia y enfoque con el fin de asegurar apoyo estratégico y catalítico a los equipos de país para acelerar la implementación de los ODS. Esta nueva visión se enmarca en la ambición
 de acelerar la implementación de la Agenda 2030 a través de las 6 transiciones, e invita a los equipos de país a explorar soluciones que sean catalíticas y capaces de tener un impacto real.

 
En esta ocasión tenemos la oportunidad de presentar una propuesta de “seed funding” (un máximo de 250,000 euros y 12 meses de implementación – encontrarán toda la información en la guía adjunta), y tras varias conversaciones
 y reuniones con las y los colegas del equipo del SDG Fund, la sugerencia para nuestro UNCT es que nos enfoquemos en explorar oportunidades y/o mecanismos de financiación innovadores en temas clave que puedan impulsar transformaciones y catalizar acciones y
 fondos de diferentes fuentes y actores. 
 
La 4ª Conferencia de países SIDS, en la que como saben República Dominicana participará con una delegación de alto nivel, va a ser una excelente oportunidad para explorar algunas de estas oportunidades y mecanismos de financiación,
 y de identificar buenas prácticas en otros países SIDS. Así, estaremos muy atent@s a los resultados de la conferencia y a las ideas y sugerencias que puedan surgir de la delegación dominicana en la materia.

 
Les proponemos por tanto retomar la reflexión y discusión después de la Conferencia para decidir el enfoque de nuestra propuesta a este fondo semilla.
 
Gracias a todas y todos, y feliz noche, 

 
Pilar

Subject: Joint SDG Fund – Update on Funding Rounds with Guidance on the Integrated Policy and Capacity Building seed funding track


 
Dear Resident Coordinators, dear colleagues,
 
I am pleased to share this update of Joint SDG Fund developments since we met on 5 March at the Global RC/UNCT clinic on the Fund 2.0.  Attached
 please find:  
 


The current list of potential fund allocations by pathfinder country and the criteria established by inter-agency processes for country selection of the four funding rounds launched to date, namely
 the Global Accelerator on Jobs and Social Protection, Digital Transformation, Food Systems Transformation, and SDG Localization. These processes reflect both the political momentum surrounding many of these priority areas as well as an enormous effort
 by the wider UN development system, including RCs, your UNCTs and colleagues across the agencies, funds and programs at HQ and regional levels, who have not only developed the criteria but undertaken the painstaking process of country selection. 

 

As you recall, this list is preliminary and, in many ways, meant to foster pipeline development for the expansion of each of the Fund’s thematic tracks as the Fund is replenished. 

 

Guidance for the seed funding track on Integrated Policy and Capacity Building. This track seeks to provide seed
 funding of up to $250,000 to UN country teams, aimed at facilitating integrated policy services and scaled capacity building to incubate transformative solutions for key SDG transitions.
In alignment with the
Joint SDG Fund’s 2023-2026 transitional strategy,
 joint programmes are intended to leverage the comparative advantages and capacities of the UN development system to propel key SDG transitions. Seed funding via the UNCT should support the sourcing, identifying and incubating of solutions and pulling together
 of expertise required to deliver them, be it from the government, private sector or civil society – or from a partner country that has undertaken a similar transition.
 

These seed funding proposals will have a maximum implementation duration of 12 months with the participation of two UN Organisations recommended. The
 joint programmes will be considered for review and approval on a rolling basis. While all UNCTs are invited to submit proposals for the Fund’s pipeline, countries ineligible in current funding tracks/rounds will be prioritised.

 


Seed funding track ProDoc template and annexes to be submitted through the online form:
https://forms.office.com/e/VVEY0FTZpz.
 The original webinar
 recording
 and  presentation
 are also here, for your reference.
 
Your humble Joint SDG Fund Secretariat is standing by to support, whether a brainstorm call or to add further clarity on this or other funding tracks.
 Do reach out to me or via email to the Dream team at 
jointsdgfund@un.org, sebastien.fahrni@un.org
and
heewoong.kim@un.org. 
 
With best regards, 
Lisa

Dear SDC colleagues,
Thank you very much for the productive call this week. It was a pleasure to see you all (virtually at least) and have the opportunity for a frank exchange. Please find attached draft notes and follow ups for your review and approval. Should we not hear from you by Thursday 15 August ‘close of business’, we will take these as a final record of our conversation. 
Regarding the question of risk assessment, as part of the CRP implementation, the Risk and Compliance Group of UNOPS has carried out a global project portfolio risk overview across its service lines. This covered key risks within Infrastructure, Procurement, Financial Management, Project Management and HR services, as well as associated lessons learned. The internal work was complemented by an external advisory engagement for extended risk data modelling and analysis. Please note that the report itself contains confidential information on individual partnerships and projects, and for that reason cannot be shared as a whole. However, we will prepare a short note that summarises the approach taken, the key observations and lessons learned as well as our overall framework for managing risks within the project portfolio. We will share this summary note with you and the Executive Board Members along with the next monthly update on implementation of the Comprehensive Response Plan that will be issued on 5 September 2024.   
We look forward to hearing from you in due course and continuing to strengthen our collaboration going forward. 
Wishing you a restful weekend. On behalf of the team,Louise

Kære Stein Erik og Constantin

Jeg håber, at alt er vel hos jer i Oslo.

Jeg skriver til jer på vegne af en af vores såkaldte "hosted entities", Sanitation og Hygiene Fund (SHF), der opererer under UNOPS' paraply.

SHF er en af FN’s globale fonde, der har fokus på at fremme sanitet, hygiejne og menstruationshygiejne (SDG-mål 6.2) i lav- og mellemindkomstlande gennem markedsbaserede tilgange. SHF’s mål er at forbedre sundheds- og uddannelsesresultater, skabe jobmuligheder og økonomisk vækst, tilbyde en lysere fremtid for kvinder og piger samt mindske klimaforandringer.

Vi tænker umiddelbart, at der kan være gode synergier og muligheder for samarbejde på områder som klima, global sundhed og ligestilling. 

Hvis det har jeres interesse, ville vi meget gerne tilbyde en kort online briefing af relevante medarbejdere i Utenriksdepartementet og NORAD, hvor kollegerne fra SHF kunne præsentere deres arbejde, kapaciteter og kompetencer med henblik på at identificere områder, hvor de kan understøtte norsk udviklingspolitik.  

Vi forestiller os, at det kunne være relevant for kolleger i Avdeling for bærekraftig utvikling, herunder Sektion for energi, klima og miljø samt Helse. I og med at de fleste mennesker uden adgang til hygiejne og sanitation er i Afrika syd for Sahara, tænker vi at Afrikaseksjonen i Utenriksdepartementet også kunne være relevant. Hos NORAD tænker vi umiddelbart, at medarbejdere i departementet for partnerskaber og innovation måske kunne være relevante. Men det er naturligvis helt op til jer, hvad I finder mest relevant 

Til orientering vedlægger jeg et slidedeck om SHF. 

Vi ser meget frem til at høre fra jer. 

På forhånd mange tak!

De bedste hilsener 
Naimo

Dear Mr. Moustapha TAHIROU,
 
Thank you for your request regarding Japanese Supplementary Fund (JSF).
 
This is Harushi Sakashita as Attache en politique et economie from Embassy of Japan in Benin. I am writing you in terms of JFS on behalf of Mr. KATO.
 
As for the priorities and deadline of a concept note, please kindly follow the guidance below.
[Main contents of a concept note]
               Suggested items to be included in a concept note and a project proposal
- A summary table of the concept note or the proposal
- Background: Include information on emergencies such as sudden natural disasters (floods, droughts, etc.), epidemics of infectious diseases, and significant humanitarian crises
- Four important elements of the project rationale:
1. Urgency: Provide reasons why it cannot wait until the next fiscal year that starts in April in Japan. Discuss the impact of the global food crisis and other unique reasons
 specific to each country.
2. Obligation: Provide reasons why Japan must contribute to address the issue(s) a country office is referring to.
3. Unpredictability: Provide a compelling rationale for why assistance must be increased or strengthened the soonest that was not predictable before March. Additionally, include
 other unique reasons specific to each country.
4. Irreplaceability: Provide reasons why there were no alternative opportunities or irreplaceable options, necessitating a request through the supplementary budget.
- Geography and targeting areas: Provide information on the geographical areas or regions targeted by the project.
- Beneficiaries: Aim to address a range of humanitarian needs, primarily focusing on vulnerable populations significantly impacted by recent events or exacerbated conditions
 since last April.
- Expected results and indicators: Specify expected outcomes of the project and the relevant indicators for measuring progress.
- Programme implementation and coordination: Include details about strategic partnerships, especially if the country office is engaging Japanese entities for project implementation.
- Involvement of Japanese staff: If any Japanese staff member will work in the project, specify their names, positions and roles in the project.
- Gender aspects: Address gender-related considerations within the project.
- Contribution towards Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): Explain how the project contributes to specific SDGs.
- Visibility: Include a plan for public relations and donor visibility during project implementation.
 
- Focus and priority areas;
1. The Women, Peace and Security (WPS) (https://www.mofa.go.jp/press/release/pressite_000001_00123.html).
2. Cross-cutting perspectives for African countries: Regional integration and connectivity, youth engagement, public-private partnerships and adherence to rule of law. This
 priority leads up to the ninth Tokyo International Conference on African Development (TICAD) scheduled for August 2025.
3. Coherence with Governmental Action Plan (PAG 2021-2026)
4. Security cooperation against extremists from Sahel
5. Development cooperation in the northern region of Benin affected by crisis
 
We would very appreciate if you could submit your concept note
by Tuesday 13, August.
 
Let us know if you have any questions.
 
Sincerely yours,
Sakashita

Dear Charles and team, 
Thank you for the call yesterday morning - we are happy to make ourselves available at short notice to get this project over the line.
Please find attached a 2-pager to explain UNOPS cost-recovery/fee setting methodology. Our average management fee is 5.1%. However, as I explained, we are working with Global Fund in over 60 countries, with different agreements and associated project budgets, with direct and indirect costs calculated based on expected deliverables - reflecting the size of the project. This is why we differ from other UN agencies in this regard.I hope this helps clarify. FYI since 2018, we have delivered over USD 1 billion in activities for the Global Fund. 
Regarding the Mali project, please note the following:

1. We are all aware of the Sahel environment this project is being conducted in. As discussed, the security situation in Segou has recently changed, with additional security measures to be applied for UN entities. This situation is in constant evolution. In addition, new procedures are frequently introduced by the Government ; which might lead to additional costs for management and unforeseen measures.
2. As mentioned during the call, the indirect costs and contingency costs have been calculated using UNOPS standardised fee calculation methodology, given the operating environment and the potential need to respond rapidly to a changing environment. We will not be able to call meetings each time additional funding might be needed as the project evolves and potential emergencies arise. Certain issues cannot be foreseen, and therefore risks have to be anticipated with adequate mitigation measures planned for. As emphasized, any unused funds will be returned.
We are looking forward to hearing back from you, and will wait for a follow up meeting to conclude the discussions.
Thanks and best wishes,
Louise, Michael and Abdoul Aziz

Le taux moyen de nos coûts indirects est de 5,1%. Cependant, comme je l'ai expliqué, nous travaillons avec le Fonds mondial dans plus de 60 pays, avec différents accords et budgets de projet associés, et des coûts directs et indirects calculés sur la base des résultats attendus - reflétant la taille du projet. Nous différons donc des autres agences des Nations Unies à cet égard.Pour information, depuis 2018, nous avons exécuté plus d'un milliard de dollars d'activités pour le Fonds mondial.
En ce qui concerne le projet au Mali, prière de prendre en considération les éléments ci-dessous :

Nous ne pourrons pas convoquer des réunions à chaque fois qu'un financement additionnel serait nécessaire, au fur et à mesure que le projet évolue et que des urgences pourraient survenir. Certains problèmes sont imprévisibles et les risques doivent donc être anticipés, avec les mesures de contingence adéquates planifiées.
