Subject: Progress with USAID on Sunsetting July 2022 Clauses.
Body:
Dear Emilie,I wanted to update you on our (Sven, Irakli, and myself) productive meeting yesterday with the USAID Office of Development Cooperation (ODC), in the Planning, Learning, and Resource Management Bureau (PLR), the Comptroller’s Office, and the General Counsel.Sven and Irakli delivered a comprehensive briefing on our net-zero budgeting, reserve calculations, and the process for refunding excess reserves. USAID appreciated the discussion and the insight into the significant changes we've made to our financial rules and regulations over the past two years  
Charles Kiame, the head of ODC, monopolized most of the subsequent discussion. He asked several questions about our approach to managing reserves, cost recovery, and applying indirect costs. We assured him that our costing methodology is fully transparent, with project budgets negotiated openly, reserve levels set by the Executive Board (EB), and excess reserves returned to partners every two years, following the same process as the initial $5.6M refund. He appeared satisfied with the discussion  
We also discussed our collaboration with INL to develop standardized language that addresses the Bureau's concerns. I shared the INL language and proposed using a similar approach to sunset the July 2022 clauses. ODC said they will consult internally and follow up with us on the next st  
Charles also asked about our progress on digitization, organizational culture, and whistleblower protection policies. We outlined the significant changes we've implemented in these areas and offered to provide additional briefings or information. We also noted that these topics are likely to be discussed at the upcoming EB session.  
Overall, it was a productive meeting. I will talk with my USAID counterparts early next week to develop a plan for sunsetting these clauses this fall. 

Your meeting with ODC's Liz Buckingham on the sidelines of the EB will be another opportunity to support this effort, 
Please let me know if you have any questions or need further information.Best regards,
Patrick

Subject: Re: Thanks and hope to see you soon!
Body:
Dear Karl, 
Thank you very much for briefly but properly taking good care of UNOPS during the summer time. It was a pleasure working with you and I wish you all the best for the future! 
Dear Roger,Welcome onboard and I look very much forward to continuing the constructive and excellent collaboration between the Swedish MFA and UNOPS in your capable hands. 
I do not assume that you will attend the Executive Board in New York next week - but if you do, I would be very happy to invite you for a coffee to get introduced. In case you are not in NYC next week, perhaps we could schedule an introduction call for the first week of September at your convenience? Please let me know when you might be available. 
Jumping right into substance, please find attached to this email - for your convenience - the statement that the ASG and Executive Director for UNOPS will give to the Executive Board next week.  
Secondly, as I have previously discussed with your predecessors, it can be difficult to keep track of / on top of the ongoing UN tribunal involving the former UNOPS DED, Mr. Vanshelboim. 
For your convenience and ease of reference I wanted to informally let you know that the UN tribunal case is ongoing in Geneva with regular hearings, submissions of requested documentation, etc. The latest hearing took place in Geneva on August 14. Please see here for your info a summary of the latest hearing. 
While it is unknown when the case will be finalised, a qualified guess is that the tribunal could present their ruling by the end of september. However, this ruling can be appealed by both parties. 
In short, the ongoing case relates to Vanshelboim contesting the UN disciplinary measures of: DismissalA fine of 12 months’ salaryRecovering from him 63,626,806 USD - and to withhold his UN pension fund until the 63M USD has been fully recovered  
In case you're interested in following developments in the case, you can find all updates here. As you will see, the documents contain very detailed updates on each new document submitted, statements by the contestant, etc. 
I hope this brief overview and status of the tribunal case helps. To be clear, all of these matters are naturally handled by the OLA. The above is merely a way for you to be better capable of keeping track and being up to date. 
Once again - looking very much forward to meeting you and continuing the excellent collaboration! 
Until then - I hope you will have an excellent weekend!
Best regards,Asbjørn

Subject: Crown Agents
Body:
Dear Agnes and Sally, 
We noticed with great sadness the unfortunate demise of the esteemed Crown Agents. With 191 years of operations it was quite an institution that did some really good and important work. 
Having been one of the FCDO's most important implementing contractors, I imagine that some of your local embassies are now looking for alternative implementing partners. Looking at Crown Agents' core capacities in delivering in some of the most fragile and conflict affected areas, complex and high impact projects, health systems, project managements, procurements, logistics, capacity building etc. - I am thinking that this aligns very well with the core capacities of UNOPS. 
I was therefore wondering if it might be useful for you to engage in a conversation on where the FCDO is looking for alternative implementing partners - to see if UNOPS could rapidly help carry forward the important work? If so, it might also be worthwhile to explore if we could develop some sort of MOU or similar at HQ level to make it easy for our colleagues in the field to carry forward the important projects smoothessly. 
I would be very keen on hearing your thoughts on how together we could best help our colleagues in the field - and avoid too much interruption in the important work for the benefit of vulnerable people. 
Looking forward to hearing your initial thoughts on this. 
Best regards,Asbjørn

Subject: Opfølgning på Danmarks nye Afrika-strategi
Body:
Kære Ketil
Mange gange tillykke med Danmarks nye, flotte Afrikastrategi! Det er et imponerende arbejde - men gode ambitioner for det fremtidige samarbejde mellem Danmark og de afrikanske lande. 
Her i UNOPS har vi allerede med meget stor interesse læst jeres nye strategi - og vil meget gerne indgå i dialog om, hvordan vi kan hjælpe med at føre strategien ud i livet på jorden i tæt samarbejde med de lokale samarbejdspartnere. Det gælder ikke mindst når det kommer til klimavenlig infrastruktur, bæredygtige indkøbsprocesser og effektiv projektledelse - som er vores kernekompetencer. 
Vores Regionale Direktør for Afrika regionen, Dalila Goncalves, hendes nærmeste medarbejdere samt jeg selv vil meget gerne mødes med dig og øvrige relevante medarbejdere mhp. at drøfte hvilke kapaciteter i UNOPS som evt. kunne understøtte den nye danske Afrika-strategi. 
Dalila er i København den første uge i oktober (dvs. i perioden d. 30 september til d. 4. oktober). Ville det evt. være muligt at finde et tidspunkt i løbet af den uge, hvor vi kunne kigge forbi Asiatisk Plads?
Jeg står naturligvis helt til jeres rådighed for evt. opfølgende spørgsmål og behov for afklaringer. 
På forhånd mange tak!

Subject: Opfølgning på Norges nye Afrikastrategi - besøg fra UNOPS i Oslo?
Body:
Kære Stein Erik og Constantin, 
Jeg håber at i hvert fald Constantin er kommet godt tilbage til Oslo - uden alt for meget jetlag.
Som kort drøftet over en kop kaffe i New York, vil vi meget gerne følge op på Norges nye Afrikastrategi. Vi ser en hel del muligheder for, at nogle af UNOPS' kernekompetencer i forhold til for eksempel klimavenlig infrastruktur, bæredygtige indkøbsprocesser og effektiv projektledelse kan bidrage til at føre de nye norske mål for bistanden til Afrika ud i livet.
Vores Regionale Direktør for Afrika, Dalila Goncalves, et par af hendes nærmeste medarbejdere samt jeg selv vil derfor meget gerne besøge jer og jeres kolleger i Oslo med henblik på at drøfte nærmere, hvordan samarbejdet mellem Norge og UNOPS evt. kan udbygges i Afrika. 
Dalia, hendes nærmeste medarbejdere og jeg selv og min medarbejder Naimo (cc) har mulighed for at rejse en dag til Oslo i den første uge af oktober (dvs. 30. september - 4. oktober). 
Kunne I være behjælpelig med at identificere hvilken dag der ville være mest hensigtsmæssig for et besøg i Oslo? Samt hvem der vil være mest relevante for Dalila at mødes med fra hhv. NORAD og Utenrigsdepartementet - som arbejder med det norske engagement i Afrika? 
På forhånd mange tak!

Subject: Coordination and Next Steps for PFA and Template Review/ Sign off 


 


 


Dear Shirley,


 



I hope this message finds you well. I want to inform you that internally, we are in the final stage of clearance, just waiting for the Finance Group to approve topics of their competence. Hopefully, we will be able to send it tomorrow morning.
 Regarding the template, we are still in the process of internal review. We hope to share a version with our comments soon, especially since it is a binding document to the PFA and one of the added values we see in the PFA. As you mentioned, this PFA will be
 signed during the IDB General Assembly in September (SoF/ UNGA). On behalf of the IDB, would it be the President's signing? Do you recommend it be the Executive Director of UNOPS to maintain reciprocity? What would be the approximate dates and location? I
 ask because the UNOPS Executive Director's office is already coordinating and scheduling bilateral meetings. I need to share this with colleagues from the OED in Copenhagen HQ to ensure the space within the UNGA framework.  


 


Additionally, I would like to inquire who you recommend from UNOPS to accompany our Executive Director on this crucial milestone occasion of the signing. Since this agreement is promoted by the LAC region of UNOPS to maintain coherence
 with the benefits to the member countries of IDB and where UNOPS has a presence, it is essential to maintain proportion and reciprocity in the protocol to follow in this process. We can delve into these details further, but it is crucial to start coordinating
 with the respective IDB unit in a timely manner. 


 


I would appreciate it if you could provide us with the IDB contacts we should eventually coordinate with. Could you please send the contacts from the Office of the IDB President, and the Partnerships Office to whom we can contact to arrange
 accordingly? This will allow our OED to include this in the ED agenda within the framework of the UNGA, where this PFA/template would be signed. 


 


Special thanks to you for the progress, leadership, communication, the IDB & UNOPS team's support and commitment to these negotiations for the benefit of the LAC region and its citizens.


 


Looking forward to hearing from you soon. 


 


Warm regards,

Subject: Notes from ED meeting with Ireland's Permanent Representative to the UN
Body:
Dear colleagues, 
On August 28 the ED met with the Permanent Representative (PR) of Ireland to the UN at the Irish Mission in NYC. 
The PR was pleased with UNOPS' reform and looked forward to turning the page with the review of the implementation of the Comprehensive Response Plan (CRP). As Ireland was focusing on delivering tangible results on the ground, UNOPS was an important stakeholder in the wider UN ecosystem. 
The ED informed about UNOPS' work in conflict-affected places - highlighting how UNOPS' non-programmatic mandate made this possible. 
Finally the ED encouraged Ireland to engage in upcoming discussions on UNOPS' next strategic plan - especially to ensure better collaboration between UN agencies and which SDGs UNOPS should cover.  
***
The PR initially complemented UNOPS' reform process, hoping that with the review of the CRP it would be possible to move out of the crisis mode. The Irish Mission had followed the process closely, but was not among the countries most engaged in the EB discussions. Ireland was a strong supporter of the wider UN ecosystem - with a focus on making a tangible difference on the ground. To this aim - UNOPS was a crucial stakeholder. 
Ireland had advocated on allocating the remaining excess reserves from UNOPS to the RC system - as it was clear that there was a need there and a big added value.  
The PR explained that there was a broad consensus in Ireland to maintain a high level of development aid - which had even been maintained during the financial crisis. 
The ED presented UNOPS' business model and work in highly conflict-affected countries such as Afghanistan, Myanmar, Mozambique, Gaza, and Ukraine. The ED pointed out that UNOPS' services were in demand as we did not bring any political agenda to the table - but only focused on deliveries for the benefit of vulnerable people. This also made it possible for UNOPS to operate in politically difficult and conflict-affected places such as Myanmar and Afghanistan. 
Upon request from the PR, the ED elaborated on UNOPS' work in Gaza together with Sigrid Kaag - making a comparison to the work UNOPS did in Yemen. The ED also gave his views on the effectiveness of the corridors into Gaza as well as the problems with distributing the aid within Gaza. 
Finally the ED reminded the PR that work on UNOPS' next strategic plan would soon commence and he hoped that Ireland would engage actively in the discussions - for example on which SDGs UNOPS should cover and how collaboration between UN agencies could be increased - for example on energy.

The Africa-Europe Foundation (AEF) will convene its cross-continental network of experts on the sidelines of the 79th Session of the UN General Assembly and this year's

 the Future via an Africa-Europe lens.

 

Key AEF sessions in New York:

 

1. Future, Now!


Saturday,
21 September, 11:00am-12:30pm EST

 role of multilateral trust and finance to reach global goals. Members will discuss actionable recommendations for advancing a holistic approach to climate and health at the UN Climate Change Conference 2024 (COP29) in November and look ahead to key milestones
 in the 2025 multilateral agenda, from Financing for Development to COP30.

Subject: Invitation for Lotte Machon to speak at panel discussion on "How Sustainable Development Can Foster Lasting Peace"
Body:
Hi Marie-LouiseFollowing up to our brief exchange yesterday regarding the upcoming event that UNOPS is organizing at Goals House in Central Park on Thursday, 26th September. 
The event will focus on the connection between sustainable development and lasting peace, a topic that I think could resonate deeply with current global priorities - not least Danish.
Given Denmark’s leadership in these areas, our close collaboration and common aim of increasing awareness of the UN agency headquartered in Copenhagen, we would be honored to have State Secretary Lotte Machon speak at our panel discussion and share her insights. Do you think that it might be possible to fit into her calendar? 
The panel will be moderated by Mr. Simon Mundy of the Financial Times, and hosted by Jorge alongside other prominent figures. 
Please find additional details about the event below. Should we have the honor of welcoming Lotte, our excellent events team (cc) will ensure a comprehensive briefing and preparatory call are arranged ahead of the event.
Thank you very much for considering this!
Best,Asbjørn

Title: Missing Peace: How Sustainable Development Can Foster Lasting PeaceDate: Thursday 26th September
Time: 10.30am – 12.00pmVenue: Tavern on the Green in Central Park, New York From Ukraine to Gaza and Sudan to Mozambique, violent conflict is rife and having far-reaching impacts across the world. Beyond the immense human suffering caused by conflict, war reverses progress on human development and creates challenges often felt most by already vulnerable populations. From food insecurity and disease, to environmental damage and inequality, conflict undermines the foundations of a just and prosperous society. Join UN Under-Secretary-General and UNOPS Executive Director, Jorge Moreira da Silva, and partners for a panel discussion on the necessary foundations for lasting peace. The panel will share ideas and experiences on how to respond, recover, and rebuild from conflict and develop long-term sustainable solutions for communities around the world. Moderated by Simon Mundy, Moral Money Editor, Financial Times. 
Background & context In 2022, more people lost their lives as a result of conflicts than at any time over the preceding 28 years. In the same year, military expenditures globally reached a new record of $2.24tn.
Peace is needed across the globe, from Gaza, Ukraine, the Sahel, Sudan, Libya, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Yemen, Myanmar, and Haiti. When emergencies happen, we must respond, recover and rebuild., from dispatching first responders to coordinating reconstruction. At the same time, we must forge long-term solutions that enable access to essential services, build resilience against future shocks, and contribute to a more sustainable future.
“In a world facing rising conflict and complex crises, UNOPS works to respond to immediate needs, while laying the foundations for a more sustainable and resilient future. Agility, preparedness and resilience are the heart of our humanitarian, development and peace efforts.”  Jorge Moreira da Silva - UNOPS Executive Director

Subject: Re: Opfølgning på Norges nye Afrikastrategi - besøg fra UNOPS i Oslo?
Body:
Hej Stein Erik
Mange tak for din tilbagemelding. 
God pointe at NORAD jo ikke er organiseret i geografiske områder. Med tanke på UNOPS' portefølje i Afrika, vores kapaciteter og med særligt blik på den nye norske afrikastrategi, tænker jeg at det kunne være relevant at mødes med direktør / medarbejdere fra jeres afdeling for:Klima, Natur og Den Private Sektor, herunder særligt:FødevarerEnergiSkovNatur og KlimaMenneskelig UdviklingGlobal sundhedUddannelse og forskningGender balanceGovernanceHensigten med Dalilas mission til Oslo vil være at afdække muligheder for at styrke det konkrete samarbejde mellem NORAD og UNOPS i Afrika - som opfølgning på lanceringen af Afrika-strategien. Dalila vil meget gerne benytte lejligheden til at drøfte de norske prioriteter for det humanitære og udviklingsmæssige arbejde i Afrika - samt præsentere UNOPS' kapaciteter til at understøtte implementeringen. 
Jeg håber meget på, at I vil være behjælpelig med at sætte møder op med relevante afdelinger. 
Jeg ser frem til at høre fra jer. 
På forhånd mange tak! 
MvhAsbjørn
On Fri, 6 Sept 2024 at 13:12, Horjen, Stein Erik <Stein.Erik.Horjen@norad.no> wrote:








Hei Asbjørn
 
Takk for dette. Norad er ikke organisert geografisk så derfor er det ikke en avdeling eller seksjon som jobber med Afrika.

Jeg tenker derfor det viktigste er å møte Afrikaseksjonen i UD, men dette overlater jeg til Constantin å bedømme.

Dialogen mellom Norad og UNOPS på strategisk nivå foregår mye mellom våre direktører. Om det i dette tilfelle er Bård Vegar eller andre som kunne ha truffet Dalila
 får vi ta stilling til når vi vet litt mer om tematikken for møtet. Vi har en partnerskapsseksjon i kunnskapsavdelingen, men de jobber mer med innovasjon og utvikling av nye partnere.

 
Beklager et litt vanskelig svar, Asbjørn.

 
God helg,

Stein Erik

Subject: Opfølgning på Norges nye Afrikastrategi - besøg fra UNOPS i Oslo?

 

Kære Stein Erik og Constantin, 

 


Jeg håber at i hvert fald Constantin er kommet godt tilbage til Oslo - uden alt for meget jetlag.


 


Som kort drøftet over en kop kaffe i New York, vil vi meget gerne følge op på Norges nye Afrikastrategi. Vi ser en hel del muligheder for, at nogle af UNOPS' kernekompetencer i forhold til for eksempel klimavenlig infrastruktur, bæredygtige
 indkøbsprocesser og effektiv projektledelse kan bidrage til at føre de nye norske mål for bistanden til Afrika ud i livet.


 


Vores Regionale Direktør for Afrika, Dalila Goncalves, et par af hendes nærmeste medarbejdere samt jeg selv vil derfor meget gerne besøge jer og jeres kolleger i Oslo med henblik på at drøfte nærmere, hvordan samarbejdet mellem Norge og
 UNOPS evt. kan udbygges i Afrika. 


 


Dalia, hendes nærmeste medarbejdere og jeg selv og min medarbejder Naimo (cc) har mulighed for at rejse en dag til Oslo i den første uge af oktober (dvs. 30. september - 4. oktober). 


 


Kunne I være behjælpelig med at identificere hvilken dag der ville være mest hensigtsmæssig for et besøg i Oslo? Samt hvem der vil være mest relevante for Dalila at mødes med fra hhv. NORAD og Utenrigsdepartementet - som arbejder med det
 norske engagement i Afrika? 


 


På forhånd mange tak!


 


Mvh

Kære Niklas og Amalie, 
Jeg kontakter jer på vegne af FN Byen i København samt UNOPS, med henblik på at indlede dialog om mulighed for foretræde for Udvalget.  
Formålet med dialogen vil være at afsøge muligheden for, at FN Byens øverste chef, FN-Under-Generalsekretær og Executive Director for UNOPS, Jorge Moreira da Silva kan få foretræde for Udvalget. 
FN Under-Generalsekretæren ønsker bl.a. at orientere Udvalget om situationen i Gaza og Ukraine samt at informere Udvalget om FN's arbejde i de mest konfliktramte områder - herunder også FN's vurdering af situationen. 
Herudover ønsker FN Under-Generalsekretæren at informere Udvalget om det konkrete arbejde som udføres af FN agenturerne i København, herunder særligt UNOPS, der som det eneste FN-agentur har hovedkvarter i København.

Subject: Gaza
Body:
Dear Cristina (cc your colleagues from the MFA), 
Thank you for the good catch-up meeting earlier this week. 
As agreed, I am following up with a bit of information on UNOPS' work in Gaza to facilitate an online briefing session by relevant colleagues in SIDA and the MFA on this. I have cc'ed Beatrice with whom we tried to find a workable time slot for an in-depth briefing before the summer holidays (following a conversation between Carl and Jorge). Unfortunately this did not materialise due to calendar conflicts. 
I hope we could find a workable time slot to facilitate such a briefing in the coming weeks. Our Regional Director for the Middle East and her team stands ready to brief you and your colleagues. 
As you may be aware, UNOPS is working with Sigrid Kaag to operationalise the Gaza Mechanism. The aim of this is to ensure that more humanitarian assistance gets into Gaza. The Mechanism has been activated for the Cyprus and Jordan corridors. We are currently engaged  with the Egyptian Red Crescent to enable data sharing, which would activate the Egypt corridor. Full return to operation would obviously depend on the political level discussions. 
The financial need for the Mechanism is approx. $61M. So far it has received $21M. The donors are: Netherlands ($7.2M), United Arab Emirates ($5M), Australia ($1.3M), Denmark ($2M), Estonia ($30,000), New Zealand ($1.2M), and Minderoo Foundation (4M). We received additional pledges, for $7M million, from Canada ($3.7M) and Germany ($6.6M).
Furthermore, the US has provided a stand-alone contribution of $70M in support of the Jordan Corridor. This contribution provides additionality to the overall budget and secures the majority of the needs for functioning of the Jordan Corridor.  
UNOPS also supports delivery of critical humanitarian assistance and we stand ready to procure urgently needed aid on behalf of partners. Eg. fuel, medicine etc. For example we deliver the fuel to power plants in Gaza. The project has increased electricity supply to the people in Gaza from 5-6h/day to approx. 12h/day.

Looking towards reconstruction, UNOPS has significant experience in the region which we would hope to leverage. For example from our work in Yemen.
I look forward to hearing back from you with a view of setting up an in-depth online briefing about our work in Gaza. 
Until then I wish you and your colleagues a wonderful weekend!
Best regards,Asbjørn

Kære Niklas, 
Tak for den opfølgende samtale i fredags vedrørende nedenstående anmodning om at mødes med Udenrigsudvalget. 
Jeg har haft lejlighed til at drøfte format og temaer for mødet med Jorge, som meget gerne vil imødekomme de efterspurgte emner vi drøftede (se yderligere herom nedenfor). 
Fsva. datoer for mødet vil vi foreslå:D. 2. oktober kl. 15.00D. 17. oktober kl. 15.00Kunne en af ovenstående tidspunkter fungere for Udvalget?
Som aftalt pr telefon, vil Jorge meget gerne mødes med udvalget med henblik på at orientere om: Den sikkerhedspolitiske og humanitære situation i nogle af de mest skrøbelige og konfliktramte steder i verden, hvor UNOPS især opererer (bl.a. finansieret af Danmark). Det gælder bl.a. Afghanistan, Ukraine, Yemen, Sudan, Gaza, mv. Særligt fokus på koordinationsmekanismen for humanitær nødhjælp til Gaza, som medfinansieres af Danmark og drives af UNOPS.  Jorge orienterede g.d. FN's Sikkerhedsråd om status på Gaza Mekanismen (se her) - hvilket han på mødet med Udenrigsudvalget vil kunne uddybe - herunder særligt status på, hvad der fungerer i de enkelte korridorer og hvad der ikke virker. Jorge's indlæg suppleres meget gerne med en direkte videoforbindelse til vores Direktør for Mellemøsten, Fru Bana Kaloti, som kan give en uddybende og live status på situationen i Mellemøsten. Som omtalt pr. telefon vil Jorge også gerne benytte lejligheden til at orientere Udvalget om det konkrete arbejde som udføres af FN agenturerne i København, herunder særligt UNOPS, der som det eneste FN-agentur har hovedkvarter i København.Jorge deltager i mødet som UNOPS' Executive Director samt som øverste chef for FN-Byen i København. Han vil derfor også komme ind på FN-Byens generelle rolle og arbejdet i de 10 agenturer. Fokus i Jorge's indlæg vil dog være på UNOPS' arbejde i de mest konfliktramte områder i verden (hvor de meste af UNOPS' arbejde foregår), vores rolle som et efterspørgselsdrevet, implementerende FN-agentur uden kernefinansiering - specialiseret i at finde praktiske løsninger indenfor især infrastruktur og indkøb. Som drøftet pr. telefon taler Jorge indledningsvist i ca. 10 minutter efterfulgt af spørgsmål fra Udvalgets medlemmer. Herefter gives ordet til Bana via videolink, som taler i 5-7. minutter efterfulgt af spørgsmål fra Udvalgets medlemmer. I alt afsættes 1 time til mødet. 
Jeg håber ovenstående vækker Udvalgets interesse. Såfremt der er andre ønsker til emner som ønskes drøftet, er vi naturligvis meget lydhør og vil efterkomme Udvalgets ønsker. 
Jeg ser meget frem til at høre fra dig - i første omgang især mhp. at få mødet i kalenderen. 
På forhånd mange tak!
MvhAsbjørn

Body:
Dear Colleagues:
Good morning from Washington. I wanted to update you all of my meeting yesterday (Sept 17) with USAID regarding the sunsetting of the special clauses. While making it clear that this was unofficial and very preliminary, I shared with them the feedback from the meeting I had with FG on Monday (Sept 16). USAID said they would like to wrap this up quickly and sought to replicate the August 2024 INL language in their proposal. 
Below are USAID's responses to the points discussed in the Sept 16  meeting. 
1) Do we need this under the special provisions or can this be in any other form, e.g. agreed templates or MoU?

USAID said that these clauses would be part of their ADS directives website and that they would be public.  USAID noted that they "have to do this" and that the agency does not rely on MOUs for projects.  I mentioned that UNOPS wanted to ensure that these provisions would not be presented in a way that makes it seem like the S3i crisis is recent or ongoing. USAID said they understood this. As such, they said they would recommend the agency's General Council put in a provision that requires a review after two years. 
2) Suggest to find one focal point for the excess reserve communication rather than every agreement officer.? 
USAID said this was intended to be a focal point and not require a separate notification for each project or agreement.  My counterpart said he would talk to their lawyers and clarify this so that it was clear on where to send the required information. 
3) UNOPS will further provide a detailed explanation of the basis for the management fee rate[s] as per the approval of its Executive Board on a biennial basis.  
USAID seemed amenable to this and said they would consult with their finance team and lawyers. 
As a path forward, USAID suggested I send them an official response with proposed revisions to the text. Once done, my main counterpart believed we could easily conclude this via email exchanges as he believed USAID would concur with our suggestions. I am losing my amazing counterpart on October 15 so I'd like to push this as fast as possible to see if we can leverage him to get this over the finish line. 
@Eli and Vinesh, I will wait to respond until LG has had a chance to review the proposed changes we discussed with FG. I have opened a ticket and will add this email to it. 
Thanks again for all of your help and support in restoring a normal business relationship with the US. I can't wait to finish the final piece of the puzzle. In the meantime, please let me know if you have any questions or need additional information. 
Best regards, Patrick

Subject: New U.S. Global Development Strategy
Body:
Dear Colleagues: I am writing to share some key insights from my attendance at the U.S. government’s new Global Development Strategy launch at the White House on September 18. President Biden’s National Security Advisor (NSA) Jake Sullivan and USAID Administrator Samantha Power introduced this update, the first since the Obama-Biden Administration's strategy in 2010. They both outlined the strategy's main priorities and how it addresses the ever-increasing global challenges we face today. (The White House Press Release on Global Development Strategy provides an excellent strategy summary. The complete strategy can be found here.)NSA Sullivan opened the event by highlighting the pressing global challenges, including wars, conflicts, pandemics, and climate issues. He emphasized that the new strategy demonstrates the vital role of development, alongside defense and diplomacy, in securing U.S. national interests and addressing global crises.He emphasized the importance of partnering with like-minded nations and international organizations to address global challenges. Although the U.S. is the largest bilateral donor, Sullivan noted that the required resources far exceed current funding levels, and there is a need to "shift from billions to trillions." To achieve this, he highlighted the necessity of reforming international financial institutions (IFIs) to streamline their operations, leverage their balance sheets to expand funding, and seek capital increases from Congress when needed. He stressed the importance of mobilizing private sector capital to meet global development needs.Sullivan expressed pride in the G-7’s Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment, highlighting its transformative potential for countries and regions. He used the Lobito rail corridor in Africa as an example, a $1 billion U.S.-backed project poised to boost the economies of Angola, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and neighboring nations. Sullivan emphasized the importance of continuing such large-scale investments to drive sustainable development and regional growth through "transparent initiatives," contrasting them with China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI).Administrator Power echoed many of National Security Advisor Sullivan's points, highlighting USAID's efforts to enhance development diplomacy by strengthening partnerships with donors, the UN, international financial institutions, and recipient countries. She noted that USAID has created an Office of the Chief Economist to evaluate programs, measure outcomes, and prioritize investments. Like Sullivan, Power emphasized the critical role of diplomacy, defense, and development in the U.S. national security strategy. She added that the administration must demonstrate how development spending delivers tangible value to U.S. taxpayers and companies.In addition, she emphasized USAID's commitment to engaging the private sector. She highlighted USAID’s $50 million EDGE Fund, which aims to incentivize private sector initiatives contributing to development outcomes.  (Edge Fund Press Release). Power noted that USAID is preparing another round of EDGE funding. She also emphasized the USAID’s need to streamline its bureaucratic policies and encourage innovation. She also highlighted the importance of increasing USAID's spending with local suppliers, aiming to improve localization efforts beyond the current "very low level" of 10-11%.Following the remarks, a roundtable discussion took place featuring MCC Chair Alice Albright, DFC Deputy Director Nisha Biswal, Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for International Affairs Alexia Latortue, and Deputy Secretary of State for Management Richard Verma. The panelists shared insights on how their respective agencies are advancing key aspects of the Global Development Strategy. They expressed confidence in bipartisan support for development as a crucial national security tool for the U.S. In closing, they emphasized the importance of creativity and innovation among development professionals in tackling the world's most pressing challenges.The release of the new U.S. Global Development Strategy is an important resource for UNOPS as it consolidates the current administration's global development approach and priorities. It also demonstrates a strong White House commitment to elevating development alongside diplomacy and defense as a critical component of U.S. national security. The strategy’s relevance for UNOPS could be short-lived depending on the outcome of November’s election. If Vice President Harris wins, many current priorities and initiatives will likely continue. However, if former President Trump is elected, his administration would likely discard much of the plan, shift resources toward domestic priorities, and redirect remaining assistance away from efforts like combating climate change. I will continue monitoring the potential priorities of both Democratic and Republican candidates as we approach November’s election and will provide periodic updates this fall. In the meantime, please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any questions, need further information, or if there’s anything I can do to support your engagement with U.S. partners.Have a great weekend! Best regards, Patrick --

On Wed, 2 Oct 2024 at 13:04, Rikke Enggaard Olsen <rikoln@um.dk> wrote:








Kære Noa og Asbjørn,

 
Den 4. dec. afholder Udenrigsministeriet et udviklingsfagligt FN-seminar for nordiske udviklingspartnere (statslige styrelser) i København. Jeg vil i den forbindelse
 høre om det vil være muligt at afholde hele eller dele af programmet (der finder sted i tidsrummet 9.00-16.30) i FN-byen. Rent logistisk vil det indebære afvikling af et seminarprogram med digital understøttelse (PPT, skærm, A/V-udstyr) for ca. 30 deltagere
 med forplejning (kaffe/te/vand hele dagen, samt frokost). Budgetline til afviklingsudgifter foreligger.
 
Afholdelse af seminaret i FN-byen er dels en mulighed for at vise nordiske udviklingspartnere (statslige styrelser) FN-byen som et attraktivt og relevant hub til
 den nordiske region, samt for at der i programmet kan indgå en mulighed for interaktion imellem FN-landeteamet og nordiske donor-repræsentanter. En konkret mulighed for førstnævnte kunne f.eks. være en velkomst ved Jorge (som UNCT chair) eller Henrik (som
 ansvarlig for samarbejdsaftalen vedr. administration af FN-byen), der kan fortælle om den samlede FN-tilstedeværelse, herunder hvilke nordisk-orienterede funktioner, der har til huse i FN-byen. Mulighed for interaktion imellem FN-landeteamet/relevante tilstedeværende
 FN-partnere kunne f.eks. bestå i en tematisk paneldiskussion eller rundbordsdrøftelse (f.eks. vedrørende ”remaining engaged”-princippet og FNs udviklingssystem som implementerende i kontekster hvor diplomatisk samarbejde har svære vilkår).
 
Ser frem til at høre jeres tanker om denne mulighed.
 
Bedste hilsner,
Rikke

Dear Anne and colleagues at the Danish MFA, 
I am writing to you to kindly inquire if you would have had a chance to review the attached proposal on Strengthening Health Systems in Mykolaiv, Ukraine - that Elene transmitted for your review in August?
As you may recall, this project would run alongside another Health project funded by Novo Nordisk. While the Danish MFA funded project is intended to fund the reconstruction of 6 health facilities, repairs of 4 hospitals and installation og ambulatorities, the Novo Nordisk Funded project is intended to equip the same facilities with various medical equipment, machinery, etc. 
The Novo Nordisk funded project (50M DKK) is currently being reviewed by the senior management and we would expect a signature on an agreement during October. 
As the procurement of the medical equipment (funded by Novo Nordisk) is dependent on the prior repair of the identified health facilities (funded by MFA), it would be important not to delay the initiation of the repair project further. If the repair project is delayed, we will jeopardise the time frame for procuring and delivering the medical equipment funded by Novo Nordisk. 
I therefore hope that you would soon have time to take a look at the attached proposal in order for us to together move ahead and ensure the timely delivery of medical equipment funded by Novo Nordisk. 
We remain as always at your entire disposal for any follow-up inquiries.

4 October 2024 
 
Information Session on Global Fund Support to African Continental Mpox Response Plan
 
Dear colleagues, 
 
The Global Fund, together with Africa CDC and WHO, would like to invite you to an information session on coordination and support for the mpox
 emergency response. The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda will present case studies. 
 
Presentations include: the latest epidemiologic information, guidelines and operational tools to ensure effective mpox preparedness and response.
 It will also include voices from ministries of health at the center of the epidemic and from Global Fund Country Teams who are collaborating to ensure that immediate response needs are met.


Thursday, 10 October 10:30 – 12:00 (CEST) –

link to join the session 

Meeting ID: 957 2216 8413 | Passcode: 163230 

 
This session will be held in English with live interpretation in French and Portuguese and it's targeted to:


Country Coordinating Mechanisms (CCMs).
Principal Recipients (PRs) and sub-recipients (SRs).
Country stakeholders involved with early warning surveillance and response to epidemic-prone diseases.  
Mpox preparedness and response coordination bodies. 
Epidemiologic Surveillance and Laboratory Directorates. 
Public Health Emergency Operations Centers. 
Workforce Directorates and Field Epidemiology Training Programs. 
National Public Health Institutes.
Other partners supporting mpox response at country level. 
 
Please contact
info-sessions@theglobalfund.org if you have any questions. 
 
Best regards, 
The Global Fund 
















 
















Resources from previous sessions are available on this

Global Fund web page.

Les présentations incluent: les plus récentes informations sur l’épidémiologie de la mpox, ainsi que des directives et des outils opérationnels

Subject: Re: Updated proposal for the full restoration of the Arkas High School
Body:
Dear Anne and colleagues, 
With regards to our conversation on when the children would be able to return physically to the Arkas High School, our estimate for a best-case-.scenario is September 2026 - whilst the worst-case scenario is December 2026. Due to the ongoing construction work it would not be responsible with a phased return for the children, as it would be a proper construction area with risks of accidents. 
With regards to our conversation on what would be the potential delays if the agreement on the full restoration of the Arkas High School is not signed before January 2025, we estimate that there would be no substantive delays in the reconstruction work. However, if the agreement will only be signed by mid/end February, it would lead to delays in the construction works. We would therefore suggest to finalise the conversation on proposal, agreement amendment, budget etc. before the end of 2024 - so that we are able to sign it as soon as possible in January 2025. 
Elaborating about the timelineThe long-term stabilization is estimated to last 10 months. We should have started, but we are struggling with the local authorities to get the permits, which are more challenging than expected. Teresa and colleagues in Kyiv will reach out to the Danish embassy to get assistance if today's meeting is not productive. 
We can begin the restoration work approximately 6 months after starting the stabilization (during the last 4 months of the stabilization). The full restoration, which includes finishing the bomb shelters, is estimated to take 21 months. We will try to reduce it to 18 months, but we cannot promise this for now. Naturally we will continue to keep you in the loop throughout the process. 
We look very much forward to hearing back from you - and remain at your entire disposal for follow-up inquiries, comments, etc. 
Best regards,Asbjørn

Subject: Follow-up on meeting with UNOPS
Body:
Dear Ketil, 
It was an absolute pleasure meeting you and Emma on Friday 4 October. 
As mentioned by Dalila (cc) many of our operations are in some of the most challenging environments in Africa, including the Sahel and the Horn of Africa. UNOPS is the largest implementer of World Bank-financed projects in fragile, conflict, and violence-affected environments. This includes situations where the World Bank is unable or unwilling to fund governments directly due to political or financial constraints. In such cases, the World Bank channels funds through UNOPS to implement on behalf of donors, as seen in Afghanistan, Yemen, South Sudan, and Zimbabwe. We do similar setups for government donors. 
I am attaching a few factsheets for your information about our capacities and experience with projects on support to national governments and education that showcases our work supporting skills development and vocational training, UNOPS in the Sahel as well as one-pager about the two Danish funded projects in Somalia. 
As agreed, please find below a few short stories about some of the projects carried out by UNOPS in Africa. 
We look very much forward to continuing the dialogue. 

Best,Asbjørn 
Powering peace and sustainable development in West AfricaOn behalf of Sweden, UNOPS is bringing reliable and sustainable access to clean energy in rural areas of the Liptako-Gourma region of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger.The project is providing access to clean and sustainable energy for over 300,000 people, and is implemented in collaboration with UNDP and the Liptako-Gourma Authority. UNOPS is responsible for the installation of 6 mini-grids – two in each country – and we are leading the development of local capacity that will ensure that the new systems can be effectively operated and maintained in the longer term. This is a three year pilot project. 
Zimbabwe Idai recovery projectThe Zimbabwe Idai recovery was a four-year project, where UNOPS managed a $72 million World Bank fund and worked together with UNICEF, FAO, WHO, WFP, IOM, UNFPA and UNESCO. The project aimed to build the foundations for regional recovery after Cyclone Idai hit Zimbabwe. 
Around 50,000 households were destroyed and more than 60,000 people were displaced. Nine districts faced up to $622 million in damages. The approach of this project was to help the community not just to recover what was lost - but be able to mitigate future shocks. 
The results of the projects include: rehabilitation of health facilities, water systems and sanitation facilities, schools, irrigation schemes, micro-watersheds and roads that connected people to services – all infrastructure that's vital to the more than 346,000 people in the impacted communities.integrated health services and gender-based violence response for more than 672,000 people, including more than 3,600 internally displaced people.local jobs, thus helping build community capacity and resilience by providing infrastructure development skills. Labor-intensive, community-focused infrastructure projects created job opportunities for more than 5,200 community members, nearly half of them women.training for local authorities on the operation and maintenance of the infrastructure that was built, ensuring it remains in good working order for communities.partners involved worked closely with Zimbabwe’s national and local government, to build stronger disaster risk governance and preparedness. This involved developing early warning and risk information systems to inform disaster risk preparedness and contingency planning.to ensure that the project laid the foundation for resilience to future shock and stresses, it involved a comprehensive climate hazard and risk assessment. It made sure to engage the local community’s views via a participatory design process. This approach informed the climate resilient and inclusive design and construction of community schools, roads, health facilities, irrigations and markets.
Reconstruction of social services in YemenFunded by the World Bank, this project restored access to critical services and strengthened resilience to shocks in selected urban cities in Yemen. The project follows an area-based approach for investment in tertiary municipal services, solid waste management, water, sanitation, roads, and electricity. The project targeted approximately 3 million beneficiaries.  UNOPS has designed and rehabilitated critical urban infrastructure damaged by the ongoing conflict, incorporating resilience against identified risks. This includes water, sanitation and solid waste systems, roads and electricity supply. UNOPS has rehabilitated more than 230 kilometers of roads in 8 cities and restored access to critical services for more than 3 million people. A key component of the project aims to boost the local economy and strengthen capacity by partnering with local Yemeni.
The results of the projects include: rehabilitation of over 450 km of urban roads.the enhanced road infrastructure improves road safety, while efficient water drainage systems and newly built retaining walls are designed to protect the road from structural damage and to mitigate the effects of climate change.the upgraded road plays a crucial role in connecting Amran city to Sadah and Hajjah, serving a population of over 200,000 people.to help improve sanitation and avoid health hazards for more than half a million people, UNOPS constructed more than 6 km of new sewage line in Yemen’s historic city of Sana’a
4. Support to Tunisia’s border control and management of migration flowsFunded by the Italian government, this project aims at supporting Tunisian authorities in the continued and improved control of maritime borders by enhancing operational capacities of the fast patrol fleet of the maritime National Guard.
With €15 million funding from the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, UNOPS is implementing this project to provide maintenance services for 6 of the Tunisian Maritime National Guard’s fast patrol boats, as well as the procurement of various equipment for the Tunisian Authorities.
UNOPS has continuously provided maintenance of 6 patrol boats over a period of two years. This includes: Ordinary maintenance (predictive)Extraordinary maintenance (corrective)Spare parts for six vesselsThe Tunisian authorities’ needs for equipment and supplies were fulfilled; UNOPS has procured and supplied equipment needed by the Tunisian Authorities to a maximum value of €31 million. I hope that some of these project examples give a good indication of some of the tangible value add of the projects we implement in Africa.

Subject: Notes from DED (D&P) meeting with Danish State Secretary for Development Aid, Ms. Lotte Machon
Body:
Dear colleagues, 
On October 11 the DED (D&P) met with the State Secretary for Development Aid, Ms. Lotte Machon, at the Danish MFA. 
The State Secretary complemented the collaboration with UNOPS being very solution oriented, fast and agile - especially in Ukraine where UNOPS were implementing a significant part of the Danish aid. 
During the meeting it was agreed to gather 4-5 of the major Danish philanthropic foundations to discuss potential partnerships that could complement some of the Danish government's funded projects in Ukraine - following the format of the recent engagement with Novo Nordisk. 
The DED informed about the reform process and the upcoming dialogue about UNOPS' future vision and mission. The need to be better at measuring the impact of the work carried out by UNOPS was also discussed in relation to this.  
***
The DED initially informed the State Secretary about the discussions at UNOPS' GLN - where focus had been on the culture shift, partnerships and the future vision and mission for UNOPS. The State Secretary looked forward to an inclusive consultation process on the future vision and mission of UNOPS - and asked about the DED's first impression of UNOPS. 
The DED explained that the employees at UNOPS were extremely dedicated and very solution oriented. Unlike many other UN entities it was her impression that UNOPS employees were entirely focused on finding practical solutions to the problems at hand. There was however room for improvement in terms of measuring and communicating the quite significant impact of the work done by UNOPS throughout the world. The State Secretary agreed on the need to be better at measuring impact - but also pointed out that the most important part was the actual work on the ground. 
The State Secretary complemented the collaboration between Denmark and UNOPS - especially in Ukraine where she looked forward to the next 3 year programming period and hoped that UNOPS would continue to play a major role in the implementation of the Danish aid to Ukraine. The Danish Government was also very satisfied with UNOPS' rapid implementation of the Comprehensive Response Plan and looked forward to the independent review so that this chapter could be closed early 2025. 
The DED informed about the planning of the upcoming CEB in Copenhagen in 2025 and the ongoing reform process - pointing out that the digitalisation reform would take years as more investments had to be done over a number of years. 
The State Secretary emphasised the Danish Government's policy on more sustainable procurement practices - and desire to make the UN procurement more sustainable. The DED repeated the offer for a dedicated session with the PG on sustainable procurement - and how this could be improved further. The DED also asked the State Secretary to recall the sustainable procurement requirements when asking UNOPS to procure equipment on behalf of Denmark - not only focusing on time and speed. 
Upon a question from the State Secretary it was agreed that the DED and the State Secretary would soon gather 4-5 of the major Danish philanthropic foundations to suggest partnerships that would enhance the effects of some of the Dansh funded projects in especially Ukraine. The approach would build upon the recent experiences with Novo Nordisk, where the government funded the reconstruction of 6 hospitals and Novo Nordisk provided funding for the medical equipment, ambulances, machinery, etc. A similar approach could be done for the schools, where eg. Carlsberg  and LEGO might be interested in funding the school books, IT, furniture etc. NELO and the MFA Ukraine Division would provide a list with suggested projects by week 43 to initiate such a dialogue. 
Best,Asbjørn

Dear
 Seynabou,


I
 hope you are well. I represent UNOPS in Washington, and am writing to follow up on what I understand was a very successful visit to Cabo Delgado, where you met with the UNOPS team implementing the
Northern
 Crisis Recovery Project
 (NCRP) on behalf of the Government of Mozambique.  


As
 the Annual Meetings approach, I wanted to highlight some of the key results from the project, particularly the timely delivery of key outputs to improve access to basic services and economic opportunities in a challenging FCV context: 





NCRP is reaching
 680,000 beneficiaries across 13 districts overall, including displaced people, host communities, and returnees. 


Two health centers
 have been completed, with eight more under construction. 


35 local peacebuilding
 committees have organized more than 500 peacebuilding activities.


3,282 local jobs
 have been created in NCRP construction sites.  


65,000 households
 have received agriculture kits. 


5,000 people have
 received self-employment kits to enhance their livelihood and income, through carpentry, tailoring, poultry farming, fisheries and agriculture.  



On
 capacity building, the project is delivering a number of subcomponents to enhance local institutions’ ability to deliver basic services, including: 





Training for health
 workers (maternal and neonatal nurses, doctors, midwives) on prevention of gender-based violence (GBV) and sexual exploitation and abuse. The program includes support for case management and liaison with the justice system.


Training for teachers
 as health focal points within schools, with a focus on GBV, and mentorship for counselors and psychologists on GBV case management. 


In addition, 10,000
 youth have received technical skills training. 



Note
 that our partnership in Northern Mozambique will be featured at the upcoming UN-WB Knowledge Management Workshop “Operational Partnerships for Strategic Impact in Complex Settings,” taking place in Nairobi on 21-22 November and organized by the WBG FCV Group
 and the UN Peacebuilding Support Office.


Looking
 ahead to 2025, UNOPS is planning to hold a knowledge-sharing workshop to dive deeper into our approach to capacity building on this and other Bank-financed projects, and we would strongly welcome collaboration with and participation from your team and others
 at the Bank on this effort. 
If
 you have any questions or suggestions related to the World Bank partnership with UNOPS, I will be more than happy to assist. In the meantime, wishing you a productive and successful Annual Meetings next week.


Best
 regards,


Christine

On Tue, 15 Oct 2024 at 13:05, Julia Winding <julwin@um.dk<mailto:julwin@um.dk>> wrote:



Kære Asbjørn



Som drøftet kommer her kort skitsering af forløbet omkring vores sekundering til EOSG/Climate Action Team (CAT).



Jeg sætter Lars og Tina på, der har haft kontakten til UNOPS og CAT, og som gerne giver mere baggrund.



Super nyttigt, hvis du har mulighed for at bistå. Vi har som sagt behov for, at den pågældende ansættes af FN, som det også normalt er tilfældet, herunder i lignende stilling tidligere.



Mange tak.



Bh Julia









I marts måned slog UM stillingen i EOSG/Climate Action Team (CAT) op som en FN-stilling, og FN oplyste i april direkte til Emma Siemens Lorenzen (på tidspunktet lokalansat på den danske FN-mission), at hun var udvalgt til stillingen. UM fik dog først oplysning herom i august til trods for, at vi op til flere gange, forsøgte at få en tilbagemelding fra FN.







FN havde derpå ifølge Emma Siemens Lorenzen løbende opfordret hende til at opsige sin stilling på missionen, så hun kunne starte hos CAT. Hun opsagde sin stilling med effekt fra 1.10. Ifølge Emma havde CAT stillet hende en kontrakt pr 1. oktober i udsigt. Samtidigt i september drøftede UM med FN formaliteterne, om hvordan Emma Siemens Lorenzen skulle ansættes. Stillingen har hele tiden været lagt op til en FN-ansættelse ligesom det var tilfældet ved en tidligere sekundering EOSG/CAT, men UNOPS ønskede formelt en dansk ansættelse. Relationen mellem UNOPS og CAT i sagen er ikke helt klar.







Dialogen om sekunderingsaftalen startede med Heba Najjar fra UNOPS (heban@unops.org<mailto:heban@unops.org>), hvorefter Marsha Cheddi (marsha.cheddi@un.org<mailto:marsha.cheddi@un.org>) fra CAT overtog dialogen pga spørgsmålet om, hvem der skulle ansætte. Den danske FN-mission ved DPR Erik Laursen gik i dialog med Cheddi om sagen, hvor det pr mail den 3. oktober (vedlagt) blev godkendt af CAT, at de ville ansætte Emma Siemens Lorenzen, således som ønsket fra dansk side.







Tirsdag den 8. oktober havde UM en samtale med Cheddi, der bekræftede, at CAT ville ansætte Emma under en multilateral sekundering, og i den forbindelse gav UM præcise oplysninger om Emmas anciennitet, civilstand og aktuelle bolig med henblik på, at de kunne beregne det præcise løntilbud til Emma. Det blev utvetydigt sagt, at Emma ville blive ansat af CAT på en kontrakt, der kan forlænges. Sideløbende med det meddelte UNOPS Emma, at hun ikke kunne ansættes af FN.







Torsdag vendte CAT tilbage efter samtalen tirsdag og nævnte, at stillingen skulle slås op igen kun for et år, og at Emma i stedet for kunne få en konsulentkontrakt indtil videre, da Emma nu ikke var ansat på missionen længere. Fra UM’s side gjorde man på ny opmærksom på, at det ikke var det, der var aftalt, og CAT undskyldte misforståelsen, men fastholdt at stillingen skal genopslås.







I fredags oplyste UM, at vi fastholdt, at CAT skulle ansætte Emma Siemens Lorenzen. Hertil har CAT oplyst, at de vil eskalere sagen, hvorved vi forstår, at de vil lade nogle højere i systemet afgøre det.







Vi forstår, at UNOPS kun kan modtage ’staff on loan’ som ’expert on mission’, og at det tilsyneladende er udfordringen med den konkrete konstruktion.

Subject: ATACH membership
Body:
Dear Elena and team
Thanks for organising the well chaired and interesting ATACH call this morning - and congratulations on the "revitalisation" of the structure and ways of working! 
Having contributed to the various working groups, meetings and joint events at WHA, COP etc over the last couple of years, can you please kindly confirm whether UNOPS is already an "official" Partner in ATACH (I don't see us listed here). If not, please advise what the process is for becoming an official partner (fyi a WHO/UNOPS MoU was signed in 2015).
Advancing Climate Action is a priority at UNOPS and we continue to support WHO and member states with implementation capacity, to scale up Climate and Health initiatives, across solarisation for health care (Côte d'Ivoire, Somalia, Yemen, Haiti etc), climate resilient infrastructure, sustainable procurement, and more,  particularly in fragile and conflict affected settings. 
ATACH is a well recognised platform to share the increasing body of evidence and data, experience and lessons learned which UNOPS is keen to contribute to, e.g. as was requested in today's call, guidance for engaging with private sector for energy / mini grid solutions; we have taken lessons from our rural renewable energy project in Sierra  Leone with FCDO and other partners - which are now being replicated in the Sahel  
Beyond project implementation, we are also co-hosting the Santiago Network agreed at COP28, hosting SE for All and most recently working with the US to expand the Global Climate Action Partnership - ATACH is a great way to share this information, lessons and technical support, enabling more member states to benefit, and helping improve coordination. Please help us share! 
Looking forward to hearing from you on this issue, and continuing our collaboration with Maria, Marina and Alex on our upcoming COP29 panel on the WHO Pavilion.
With thanks and best wishes, Louise

Subject: Notes from ED meeting with Permanent Under-Secretary of State at the Danish Prime Minister's Office, Mr. Anders Tang Friborg
Body:
Dear colleagues,
On 21 October the ED met with the Permanent Under-Secretary of State at the Danish Prime Minister's Office, Mr. Anders Tang Friborg and Head of Foreign Affairs Department at the Prime Minister's Office, Mr. Henrik Winther. 
The ED initially informed about the situation in the Middle East, presenting the Gaza and UNVIM mechanisms as confidence building tools that could be useful to get the facts straight about the aid being delivered. 
Upon information from the ED, the Permanent Under-Secretary of State was positive towards the presented ideas on increased visibility about the tangible work done by the UN and the increased focus on implementation in connection with the CEB in Copenhagen in May 2025 - which would coincide with the Danish membership of the UN Security Council. The Permanent Under-Secretary of State would discuss the idea of a dialogue / fireside chat between the PM and the SG at the UN City in connection with the CEB. The Danish Government would try to utilise their membership of the Security Council to showcase what the UN could do - as the UN's reputation had diminished in recent years. It was therefore important to better show to the taxpayers what the UN could deliver. UNOPS was uniquely situated at this as the implementer of the UN system - headquartered in Denmark.  
It was agreed to resume the conversation once a full draft program for the CEB and the potential Helsingør Dialogue had been agreed upon between UNOPS and the Danish MFA. 
***
The situation in Gaza and YemenThe ED initially informed about the situation in Gaza and Yemen - explaining the Gaza Mechanism and the Yemen UNVIM as confidence building mechanisms that would enable better decision making based on factual data from the aid entering the conflict areas.  
The Permanent Under-Secretary of State afsked if it would be possible to scale the mechanisms for when the reconstruction efforts would start - which the ED confirmed although pointing to the fact that UNOPS could not guarantee the end use of the the products entering Gaza. 
The Permanent Under-Secretary of State mentioned that he had first encountered UNOPS during his time in Afghanistan. He had therefore followed UNOPS for a number of years. Initially it had been difficult to understand what UNOPS did, the business model, etc. But once he understood it, he had been impressed with UNOPS' ability to deliver tangible results on the ground - especially in difficult places such as Gaza and Afghanistan. 

S3iUpon a question from the Permanent Under-Secretary of State, the ED provided information about UNOPS' reform process since the S3i revelations. The Permanent Under-Secretary of State complemented UNOPS for the reform process - which could be a model for other UN agencies hit by crisis. 
UNOPS' mandateThe ED explained UNOPS non-programmatic mandate, focusing on the practical solutions and how the mandate was an enabler to work in special conflict areas such as Afghanistan, Sahel, etc. The Permanent Under-Secretary of State found this approach to be very much in line with Danish priorities and ways of working. 
CEB in Copenhagen and Helsingør DialogueThe ED committed to make the strong UN presence in Copenhagen more known to the broader public as the UN premises were funded by the Danish tax payers. A clear opportunity for this would be the upcoming CEB in Copenhagen in May 2025. The ED would try to maximise visibility which could for example be ensured by a dialogue or fireside chat between the Danish Prime Minister and the UN SG at the UN City back-to-back with the CEB. Such a dialogue could be open to the public/youth as well as the UN personnel based in Copenhagen - potentially also broadcasted publictly. 
The ED also presented the idea of a Helsingør Dialogue in connection with the CEB focusing on the implementation gap and the need to find practical solutions. Such a focus on the implementation would align well with the Danish pragmatic and solution focused approach. The ED mentioned that he had presented the idea to the Danish MFA State Secretary - offering to invite Denmark as the co-host. 
The Permanent Under-Secretary of State found the ideas of increased visibility interesting and the scope of focusing on the implementation gap to be fully in line with the Danish approach of making sure that big promises are translated into reality on the ground - finding pragmatic solutions. He committed to discuss the ideas with the PM and flagged that it could also be an opportunity for the PM to point towards the added value of the UN, some of the very tangible results and work done by the UN. This would be a topic for the Danish Membership of the UN Security Council - which would coincide with the CEB in Copenhagen. It might be worthwhile exploiting this. 
The Permanent Under-Secretary of State pointed out that although the Nordics had always been - and would remain - staunch supporters of the UN, it was clear that the reputation of the UN was diminishing. There was a clear need to showcase to the population what the UN could actually do. This was also a topic that the Danish Prime Minister had discussed with the UN Secretary General during UNGA a few weeks ago. 

The Permanent Under-Secretary of State would await for a draft program for the CEB coordinated between UNOPS and the MFA. Based on this, he would discuss with the Prime Minister. 
Finally the ED offered UNOPS' services and ability to provide objective data on eg. the situation in Gaza and Yemen to the Security Council during the Danish Membership. 

/Asbjørn

Subject: Draft concept note for "Helsingør Dialogue" - translating commitment into solutions on the ground
Body:
Dear Lotte, Marie-Louise and colleagues 
Thank you for the pleasant meeting on Monday regarding the upcoming CEB as well as our idea of a "Helsingør Dialogue" focusing on the implementation bottlenecks. 
As promised please find attached a digital version of our draft concept note for the Helsingør Dialogue for your review. 
While we will continue with the planning of the event in conversations with the SG, DSG and other relevant UN stakeholders, I hope that you would consider Jorge's offer to co-host the event. We believe that the focus on translating big promises into reality on the ground is very much in line with the solution oriented Danish approach and political agenda. 
A joint event could further help increase awareness of the strong UN presence in Copenhagen - and the focus in this specific event would underpin the Danish priorities of showcasing more clearly what the UN can deliver in terms of tangible results. 
My colleagues Emilie and Rahul (both cc) are leading the taskforce that are planning the Helsingør Dialogue. We are all at your disposal for any comments, questions, clarifications, etc. 
I look very much forward to hearing back from you.

Subject: Suggested way forward for Danish Funded Secondment to UNSG's Climate Action Taskforce
Body:
Dear Marie-Louise and Lars,

First of all on behalf of UNOPS I wish to repeat my sincere apologies for the unsatisfactory process for the secondment of Ms. Lorentzen to the Climate Action Taskforce. I fully recognise your frustration for the situation that Ms. Lorentzen has been put in due to miscommunications between us, the Climate Action Taskforce and the Danish MFA. 

As discussed yesterday we now need to find the best option to remedy the situation as fast as possible and with the best possible conditions for Ms. Lorentzen. 

As the initially discussed secondment option means that Ms. Lorentzen would be liable for taxes, insurance and social security we propose two alternative options for the contract modalities:  
Fixed-Term Appointment: This option would take approximately 6 to 8 weeks, as it requires going through a competitive process, including a technical test. We will do our utmost to fast-forward the process as much as possible. This option provides more security in terms of taxes, insurance, and contract renewability.

Start with a Consultancy Contract (a fast tracked desk review): This option would cover an initial period of 6 to 9 months. The expected salary ranges from $8,500 to $9,400, depending on her years of experience. However, she would be responsible to pay for medical insurance and tax filings (which could be up to approx. 30%). Following this period, she could apply for the FTA position once it’s advertised.For the second approach, the Climate Action Taskforce would need to submit two substantially different Terms of Reference for the two positions. 

We await your decision on which option to proceed with - and remain at your entire disposal for any further clarifications.

Best regards,

Dear all: 
Thank you for your assistance over the past week in updating WLO on urgent SFA cases. 
No long-term agreement has yet been reached with the World Bank on the SFAs. We learned this afternoon (31 October) in a meeting with the Bank lawyers that the 31 October/1 November deadline will not be enforced. This is because the World Bank's leadership has not signed off internally on all the various provisions, nor have UN agencies seen the full text of the proposed framework agreement. To that end, we will continue on a case-by-case basis under the interim solution for urgent cases and work across LG, PLG and other relevant units to reach a final template. 
In the meantime, please continue to update the Google Sheet and to reach out to Christine and me with any urgent questions. 
We will keep you posted as discussions with the World Bank continue. 
Best wishes,
Alistair

More broadly, we do not expect to have a finalised new standard template by the end of October. Thank you for your cooperation and we look forward to supporting you in the coming weeks.

Subject: Re: Updates from the World Bank Group Annual Meetings
Body:
Dear Jorge, 
I hope you enjoyed your weekend. Now that the Annual Meetings are over, I am sharing an updated list of all our write-ups (plus audio podcast wrap-up) from the past week. 
Day 1: Key themesDay 2: Focus on energy and climateDay 3: Spotlight on IDA and WBG reformsDay 4: IFI/MDB cooperationDay 5: Podcast wrap-upGiven the significance of the initiative, I'm also sharing below some further information on Mission 300. WLO will be sure to follow up with relevant teams in HQ and the regions to raise awareness around Mission 300 and to support UNOPS' positioning.
Mission 300Alongside the African Development Bank, the WBG announced a new target at the 2024 Spring Meetings to connect 300 million people in Africa to electricity by 2030: now branded as Mission 300. The WBG has pledged $25bn in financing so far; AfDB $5bn. 
The Rockefeller Foundation, Sustainable Energy for All and the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet are also partners. These partners are leading a technical assistance facility to support governments.Energy Compacts are the primary vehicle to realise Mission 300. Fifteen pilot countries (including Nigeria, Senegal, DRC, and Côte d’Ivoire) are engaged in the Compact planning process, and will present their finalised plans to MDBs and donors in Tanzania in January 2025. At the summit, a second cohort of countries will be announced. (That the Compacts are country-level initiatives demonstrates the ongoing relevance of the country-driven model for the WBG). Compacts consist of five pillars. (Highlights indicate areas where UNOPS may add most value):Expand generation and invest in infrastructure at competitive costsLeverage benefits of increased regional integrationEmbrace distributed renewables (DRE) and clean cooking solutions to increase affordable last mile access.Incentivize private sector participation to unlock additional resources.Work towards financial viable utilities that provide reliable service.Affordability is a critical issue to ensure communities that are connected to energy can sustain their access. WB Regional Director for Infrastructure for Eastern and Southern Africa Wendy Hughes highlighted the role of competitive procurement tenders as one of the key ways to ensure competitive pricing. She also mentioned mini-grid/off-grid solutions, stating that these were normally driven by the private sector. 
Full write-upWLO would be happy to answer any further questions you may have about the Annual Meetings and next steps.
Best wishes,
Alistair

Dear Jorge,
I hope you are well. Emilie asked me to send you the internal updates I have been preparing each day during this week's World Bank Group-International Monetary Fund Annual Meetings in Washington. 

We are pleased to see that procurement has been front and centre in several high-level panels, including one with President Banga. Procurement is clearly emerging as an important area as the WBG seeks to simplify its processes and ensure greater coherence of approaches across MDBs and other donors. This is part of the broader "Better Bank" agenda to increase the speed and efficiency of WBG operations. This week we are also tracking discussions around the new WBG Corporate Scorecard, the "Mission 300" effort to connect 300M Africans to electricity by 2030, and the IDA replenishment. The Scorecard is a particularly important development for UNOPS, given our organisation's efforts to focus on people-centred results measurement. 

You can view all the updates here: 
Day 1: Key themesDay 2: Focus energy and climateDay 3: Spotlight on IDA and WBG reformsWe are also grateful to Kirstine for recording a short video on IDA, released today, which complements your own video message from earlier this year at the Spring Meetings.

I will share a second batch of updates with you after the Meetings wrap up this weekend. 
Please let Christine and me know if you have any questions and/or if there are any specific topics you would like us to cover in more detail in our write-ups.

Body:
Dear Jakob
Thank you for your response and valuable considerations on the way forward. 
We are consulting a wider group of our legal experts and will provide additional written elaborated explanations in Ukrainian on the 4 remaining disagreements in the draft legal agreement with CCD (as an agreement with the contractor has been reached). Based on that, Teressa and Svitlana will meet with the CCD again on Tuesday next week to make another attempt to reach an agreement. Following this meeting we will consult with you again on the way forward. 
We are very conscious of the fact that the CCD by the end of the day will be the formal recipient of the final reconstructed Arkas High School - and therefore has to be closely involved in the entire process, taking into account all of their input, technical advice, requests, etc. It is therefore crucial for the success of the reconstruction project that all parties (Denmark as the donor, UNOPS as the project manager, the contractor(s) and the CCD as the final recipient) are aligned. To ensure this we have for example incorporated legally binding requirements of monthly CCD inspections of the work. 
We are flagging the issues on contractual disagreements to you now, as the negotiations with the contractor and the CCD have been ongoing for a long time with more than 20 iterations at working level with the CCD alone. If Teressa and Svitlana are not able to reach a workable solution with the CCD next week at their level, I believe that we need to escalate the matter. Otherwise I fear that too much time will be lost without substantive progress. 
We may therefore need to call upon your help to escalate the matter with the local Ukrainian authorities to ensure that an amicable solution is reached with an agreement without potential conflicts of interests and a minimized risk assessment. 
As outlined in Teressa's document (attached here for ease of reference), the contractor was selected after a public tender process approved by CCD. The contractor has requested that all communication between the contractor and CCD happens via UNOPS as the project manager - which would ensure arms length and avoid potential conflicts of interests, etc. 
To specify the outstanding points, I have reiterated them below: CCD requests that UNOPS can only pay the contractor upon approval from CCDwould be a violation of UN financial rules and regulationsUNOPS would in practice lose control over the projectwould severely increase financial risk assessment

CCF requests the right to terminate the agreement with the contractor unilaterally with a notice period of 30 daysunacceptable to contractorcould create unfortunate conflicts of interests between contractor and CCDin violation with UN financial rules and regulations as UNOPS is the entity contracting UNOPS would in practice lose control over the project

CCD is to be the technical author and supervisorwhile CCD certainly should provide technical advice, requests, input, observations and must be consulted regularly (see agreement on monthly basis), the technical supervision of the reconstruction project has to be done by UNOPS as the project manager and as the responsible entity for ensuring the quality of the final product

Contractor has to eliminate defects after the first 12 months of finalising the projectthe defects notification period that can be accepted by UNOPS is 12 months which is standard for these types of infrastructure reconstruction projectsduring the first 12 months after finalising the reconstruction, flaws, etc. can be notified to UNOPS and we will make sure that it is dealt with within the 12 months period. Body:
Dear Dorothy Owegi,
My name is Asbjorn Brink, and I am heading UNOPS' Northern Europe Liaison Office based at our HQ in Copenhagen - which includes our partnership with Novo Nordisk. 
I am reaching out to you following close dialogue with your colleagues at the Novo Nordisk A/S HQ, where we have been partnering on projects to support the health sector in Ukraine - by rebuilding destroyed hospitals and procuring much needed medical equipment. 
I am writing to you to express our interest in exploring potential collaboration between UNOPS and Novo Nordisk in the area of health on the African continent. My colleague Naimo (cc) and I will be visiting our UNOPS colleagues based in Nairobi on December 2-5 and would greatly appreciate it if you would have time to meet with us to discuss how we can align our efforts to maximize impact. 
For your background information, more than half of UNOPS' operations are in the health sector and we are already actively engaged in strengthening health systems across the African continent, with a focus on delivering sustainable solutions in collaboration with partners. 
We believe that Novo Nordisk's commitment to improving global health, particularly in addressing non-communicable diseases and improving access to care in underserved regions aligns strongly with our work in Africa. 
Please let me know your availability or if there is someone on your team who could join the conversation. I am happy to adjust to a time that works best for you.
Looking forward to the opportunity to explore ways we can work together to make a meaningful difference.
Best regards,Asbjørn
