Dear Satu and colleagues in Helsinki, 



 



A late - but very happy new year to all of you! I hope you have had a chance to enjoy some offline time with your loved ones. 


 


As usual I wanted to provide you with a brief overview of the topics relevant for UNOPS at the upcoming EB session on January 27-31. I am sorry that I am a bit late with this overview, as we already have the first informal session this
 afternoon at 5 pm CET about the status of the Comprehensive Response Plan and UNOPS' digitalisation plan (the so-called PID). 


 


I am sure that you have already seen that all the relevant documents were uploaded to the website here -
 but I just wanted to share the link with you to gather all the pieces in one email. 


 


I was wondering if perhaps you would have time to briefly catch up in advance of the EB - to get your initial take on the topics and for me to perhaps clarify matters, point towards (for us) important aspects, etc. If so - please just let
 me know when it might suit you. 


 


Further to the topics to be discussed at the upcoming EB, I have provided you with a quick overview of the upcoming informal session below for your ease of reference. 




·      
13 January: The comprehensive response plan and the UNOPS report on the Process Innovation and Digitalization Programme implementation 

·      
14 January: Informal consultation with UNDP, UNFPA, UNOPS on the joint update on organization culture 

·      
17 January: Joint UNDP, UNFPA, UNOPS orientation for the Executive Board (our DED Sonja will give an introductory presentation on UNOPS to the EB members)

·      
20 January: Briefing on undisbursed excess reserves, with UNBOA 

·      
21 January: Joint consultation on enterprise risk management 

·      
22 January: Joint informal with JIU on JIU report on governance and oversight 



There will also be two closed session during the EB week:



·      
28 January: Closed briefing on S3i funds recovery, with OLA

·      
30 January: Closed briefing on portfolio risk assessment




  

Topics to be discussed at the EB relevant to UNOPS



1.    
UNOPS'
 response to the recommendations of the UN Board of Auditors for 2023 


o  
The UNBOA report for 2023 on UNOPS was unqualified (also known as "clean") - meaning that our financial statements are deemed to present a true and fair view of UNOPS' financial position and performance, comply with UN accounting
 standards and are free of material misstatements. 

o  
UNBOA issued 9 recommendations classified as high priority and 10 recommendations classified as medium priority.  The implementation of all recommendations is on track for completion within the timelines. Because the recommendations
 were issued in July 2024, and many of them require long-term attention, UNOPS will need to work beyond 2024 to implement them all successfully.

o  
In the implementation schedule UNOPS is targeting an implementation rate of 68% during the 2024 audit cycle, which will surpass that of 2023 (58%).

2.    
Governance and oversight functions of the Executive Board 


o  
At the last EB session the Bureau was tasked to develop a terms
 of reference for the operationalisation of a working group to review the 31 recommendations of the Joint Inspection Unit (JIU) and to develop actions
 for their implementation. 

o  
In advance of the last EB session in 2024, UNOPS developed this
 informal document outlining UNOPS' views on the JIU recommendations. The document also contains the views of the ethics offices of the involved agencies. 

3.    
Risk management 

o  
At the last EB session, UNDP, UNFPA and UNOPS were asked to provide updates on the agencies' efforts to improve the enterprise risk management system and inform the EB of any critical risks of strategic importance. 

o  
From a UNOPS perspective The
 joint information note points towards key risks associated with project delivery, financial management and stakeholder engagement. It also points to more concrete risks regarding UNOPS' operations in fragile and conflict affected places, shortage of talent,
 sexual abuse due to the geographical operations of UNOPS, regaining trust among partners since S3i failures, implementing the many reforms at UNOPS and increasing financial constraints.     

4.    
Organisational culture 

o  
The
 informal information note provides an update on the implementation of the work plan to transform the organisational culture. Status of each action point is in this
 annex.    

5.    
Implementation
 of the Comprehensive Response Plan 

o  
This is the last update to the EB on the implementation of the CRP. As the note was written in November, 3 of the outstanding recommendations were yet to be completed by the end of 2024. These related to 1) revising the management
 and organisational culture towards broader engagement and less top-down, 2) invest in outcome-reporting, and 3) revision of financial rules and regulations.  

o  
The EB is asked to release the third tranche (11.8M USD) for the implementation and to initiate the second independent review of the implementation of the CRP.  

6.    
Review
 of the whistleblower process 

o  
The informal information note provides an overview of the now completed overhaul of UNOPS' whistleblower mechanism. 

o  
The new system is set to launch in January 2025 and will introduce: 1) a central platform for reporting, 2) ressources to provide early informal guidance, 3) a workplace conduct team within PLG, 4) a new advisory group to address
 systemic issues. 

7.    
Portfolio risk assessment of UNOPS 

o  
As a response to the original KPMG recommendations a
 portfolio risk assessment is presented that outlines a number of risks in UNOPS' portfolio. These relate e.g. to 1) challenges in managing complex infrastructure projects, 2) large-scale procurement of health products, 3) capacity of supplivers and implementing
 partners. 

8.    
Calculation
 method for excess reserves 

o  
The note presents a suggestion for revising the calculation methodology for calculating UNOPS' excess reserves. The proposed changes are to ensure that only liquid assets are calculated as part of the potential excess reserves
 and that only if the excess reserve exceeds 20% of the minimum operational reserve, it should trigger the refund process. 

o  
By the end of 2023 UNOPS distributed 123.2M USD of the excess reserve back to partners and all other funds had been transferred to the RC system and the SDG fund. Only 0.6M USD is withheld as these relate to discussions with partners. 

9.    
Implementation
 of the PID 

o  
This is the annual status of implementation of the PID that points towards progress in seven programmes (country engagements, partnerships and project management, procurement, HR, finance, data, market research for the new ERP). 

o  
Notice that the selection of a new ERP system can only be done after a formal evaluation is presented to the EB (as requested by the EB). Therefore the timeline for the PID has been extended by one year to 2028.


I hope this brief overview helps - and I look very much forward to hearing your initial thinking about the topics. 



 


All the best,


Asbjørn

Kære Constantin og Stein Erik 
 
Et sent - men rigtig godt nytår til jer alle! Jeg håber, I har haft mulighed for at nyde noget offline tid med dine kære. 
 
Som vanlig ville jeg give jer et kort overblik over de emner, der er relevante for UNOPS på den kommende EB-session den 27.-31. januar. Jeg beklager at den kommer
 noget sent, da vi allerede i eftermiddag kl. 17 har den første uformelle session om status for Responsplanen og UNOPS’ digitalisering (den såkaldte PID). 
 
I har sikkert allerede bemærket, at alle de relevante dokumenter er uploadet til hjemmesiden
her

Jeg ville sætte stor pris på, om I havde tid til at mødes kort online, mhp. en uformel drøftelse om de vigtigste emner på dagsordenen. Lad mig meget gerne vide
 hvornår det kunne passe jer. 
 
Jeg vil ikke selv være tilstede under EB - da jeg er i Oslo til NORAD konferencen. Hvis I har tid til at mødes til en frokost, kaffe eller lignende, ville det være
 super. Jeg rækker ud særskilt herom. 
 
Ud over overblikket over de emner, der skal drøftes i bestyrelsen ultimo januar, har jeg nedenfor givet et hurtigt overblik over de kommende uformelle sessioner 

·        
13 januar: Status på Responsplanen og UNOPS’ digitaliseringsprogram
 (PID) 

·        
14 januar: Fælles møde med UNDP, UNFPA og UNOPS om organisationskultur 

·        
17 januar:
Fælles UNDP, UNFPA, UNOPS orientering for nye medlemmer (vores DED Sonja vil holde et oplæg om UNOPS)

·        
20 januar: Briefing om ikke-udbetalte overskydende reserver, med
 UNBOA 

·        
21 januar: Risikostyring, sammen med UNDP og UNFPA 

·        
22 januar:
Uformel, fælles dialog med JIU om JIU-rapport om styring og tilsyn 
Der vil også være to lukkede sessioner i løbet af EB-ugen:

·        
28 januar:
Lukket briefing om inddrivelse af S3i-midler med OLA

·        
30 januar: Lukket orientering om porteføljerisikovurdering
  
Emner, der skal diskuteres på EB, der er relevante for UNOPS

1.    
UNOPS'
 svar på anbefalingerne fra FN's Revisionsråd for 2023

o   
UNBOA-rapporten for 2023 om UNOPS var ukvalificeret (eller "ren") - hvilket betyder, at vores regnskaber anses for at give et retvisende billede af UNOPS'
 finansielle stilling og resultater, overholder FN's regnskabsstandarder og er fri for væsentlige fejl. 

o   
UNBOA udsendte 9 anbefalinger klassificeret som høj prioritet og 10 anbefalinger klassificeret som medium prioritet. 

o   
Implementeringen af alle anbefalinger er på sporet med forudset færdiggørelse inden for tidsfristerne. 

o   
I implementeringsplanen sigter vi efter en implementeringsgrad på 68% i løbet af 2024-revisionscyklussen, hvilket vil være lidt højere end i 2023 (58%).

2.    
Bestyrelsens ledelses- og tilsynsfunktioner 

o   
Ved den sidste EB-session fik Præsidiet til opgave at udvikle et

kommissorium for operationalisering af en arbejdsgruppe at gennemgå 31 anbefalinger fra Joint Inspection Unit (JIU) og at udarbejde konkrete handlingspunkter. 

o   
Forud for den sidste EB-session i 2024 udviklede UNOPS
 dette uformelle dokument, der skitserer UNOPS' synspunkter om JIU-anbefalingerne. Dokumentet indeholder også synspunkter fra de involverede agenturers etikkontorer.


3.    
Risikostyring

o   
Ved den sidste EB-session blev UNDP, UNFPA og UNOPS bedt om at give opdateringer om agenturernes bestræbelser på at forbedre risikostyring og informere
 EB om eventuelle kritiske risici af strategisk betydning. 

o   
Fra et UNOPS perspektiv peges i det
 fælles informationsnotat på bl.a. risici forbundet med projektlevering, økonomistyring og interessentengagement. Der peges også på mere konkrete risici vedrørende UNOPS' operationer i skrøbelige og konfliktramte steder, seksuelt misbrug på grund af UNOPS'
 geografiske operationer, genvinding af tillid blandt partnere siden S3i, implementering af de mange reformer hos UNOPS og tiltagende økonomiske begrænsninger.    


4.    
Organisationskultur

o   
Det
 uformelle informationsnotat giver en opdatering om implementeringen af arbejdsplanen for at transformere organisationskulturen. Status for hvert handlingspunkt findes i

dette bilag.    

5.    
Implementering
 af responsplanen

o   
Dette er den sidste opdatering om implementeringen af CRP. Da notatet blev udarbejdet i november, var 3 af de udestående anbefalinger endnu ikke afsluttet
 ved udgangen af 2024. Disse vedrørte 1) revision af ledelses- og organisationskulturen mod bredere engagement og mindre top-down, 2) investering i resultat- rapportering, og 3) revision af finansielle regler og forskrifter. Disse er nu implementeret. 

o   
EB anmodes om at godkende frigivelsen tredje tranche (11,8 mio. USD) til implementeringen og at indlede den anden uafhængige gennemgang af implementeringen
 af CRP.  

6.    
Gennemgang
 af whistleblower-processen

o   
Informationsnotatet giver et overblik over det nu afsluttede eftersyn af UNOPS' whistleblower-mekanisme. 

o   
Det nye system skal lanceres i januar 2025 og vil introducere: 1) en central platform til rapportering, 2) ressourcer til at give tidlig uformel vejledning,
 3) et team for adfærd på arbejdspladsen og 4) en ny rådgivende gruppe til at håndtere systemiske problemstillinger.


7.    
Porteføljerisikovurdering af UNOPS

o   
Som et svar på de oprindelige KPMG-anbefalinger er udarbejdet

en porteføljerisikovurdering der skitserer en række risici i UNOPS' portefølje. Disse vedrører f.eks. 1) udfordringer i styring af komplekse infrastrukturprojekter, 2) storstilet indkøb af sundhedsprodukter og 3) kapacitet hos leverandører og implementeringspartnere.
 Hertil kommer naturligvis det faktum, at hovedparten af UNOPS’ aktiviteter foregår i konfliktramte og volatile områder.


8.    
Beregningsmetode
 for overskudsreserver

o   
Noten præsenterer et forslag til revision af beregningsmetoden til beregning af UNOPS' overskydende reserver. De foreslåede ændringer skal sikre, at kun
 likvide aktiver beregnes som en del af de potentielle overskydende reserver, og at tilbagebetalingsprocessen kun udløses hvis den overskydende reserve overstiger 20 % af den minimale operationelle reserve. 

o   
Ved udgangen af 2023 distribuerede UNOPS 123,2 mio. USD af den overskydende reserve tilbage til partnere, og alle andre midler var blevet overført til
 RC-systemet og SDG-fonden. 0,6 mio. USD tilbageholdes, da disse vedrører igangværende drøftelser med partnere.


9.    
Implementering
 af digitaliseringsprogrammet - PID

o   
Dette er den årlige status for implementering af PID, der peger mod fremskridt i syv programmer (landeengagementer, partnerskaber og projektledelse, indkøb,
 HR, økonomi, data, markedsundersøgelser for den nye ERP). 

o   
Bemærk, at valget af et nyt ERP-system kun kan foretages, efter at en formel evaluering er præsenteret for EB (som anmodet af EB). Derfor er tidslinjen
 for PID blevet forlænget med et år til 2028.
Jeg håber, at denne korte oversigt hjælper - og jeg ser meget frem til at høre jeres indledende tanker om emnerne.

Dear Satu and colleagues in Helsinki, 



 



A late - but very happy new year to all of you! I hope you have had a chance to enjoy some offline time with your loved ones. 


 


As usual I wanted to provide you with a brief overview of the topics relevant for UNOPS at the upcoming EB session on January 27-31. I am sorry that I am a bit late with this overview,
 as we already have the first informal session this afternoon at 5 pm CET about the status of the Comprehensive Response Plan and UNOPS' digitalisation plan (the so-called PID). 


 


I am sure that you have already seen that all the relevant documents were uploaded to the website here -
 but I just wanted to share the link with you to gather all the pieces in one email. 


 


I was wondering if perhaps you would have time to briefly catch up in advance of the EB - to get your initial take on the topics and for me to perhaps clarify matters, point towards
 (for us) important aspects, etc. If so - please just let me know when it might suit you. 


 


Further to the topics to be discussed at the upcoming EB, I have provided you with a quick overview of the upcoming informal session below for your ease of reference. 




·      
13 January: The comprehensive response plan and the UNOPS report on the Process Innovation and Digitalization Programme implementation 

·      
14 January: Informal consultation with UNDP, UNFPA, UNOPS on the joint update on organization culture 

·      
17 January: Joint UNDP, UNFPA, UNOPS orientation for the Executive Board (our DED Sonja will give an introductory presentation on UNOPS to the EB members)

·      
20 January: Briefing on undisbursed excess reserves, with UNBOA 

·      
21 January: Joint consultation on enterprise risk management 

·      
22 January: Joint informal with JIU on JIU report on governance and oversight 



There will also be two closed session during the EB week:



·      
28 January: Closed briefing on S3i funds recovery, with OLA

·      
30 January: Closed briefing on portfolio risk assessment




  


Topics to be discussed at the EB relevant to UNOPS



1.     UNOPS'
 response to the recommendations of the UN Board of Auditors for 2023 


o  
The UNBOA report for 2023 on UNOPS was unqualified (also known as "clean") - meaning that our financial statements are deemed to present a true and fair view of UNOPS' financial position and performance, comply with UN accounting standards and are free
 of material misstatements. 

o  
UNBOA issued 9 recommendations classified as high priority and 10 recommendations classified as medium priority.  The implementation of all recommendations is on track for completion within the timelines. Because the recommendations were issued in July
 2024, and many of them require long-term attention, UNOPS will need to work beyond 2024 to implement them all successfully.

o  
In the implementation schedule UNOPS is targeting an implementation rate of 68% during the 2024 audit cycle, which will surpass that of 2023 (58%).

2.     Governance and oversight functions of the Executive Board 


o  
At the last EB session the Bureau was tasked to develop a terms
 of reference for the operationalisation of a working group to review the 31 recommendations of the Joint Inspection Unit (JIU) and to develop actions
 for their implementation. 

o  
In advance of the last EB session in 2024, UNOPS developed this
 informal document outlining UNOPS' views on the JIU recommendations. The document also contains the views of the ethics offices of the involved agencies. 

3.     Risk management 

o  
At the last EB session, UNDP, UNFPA and UNOPS were asked to provide updates on the agencies' efforts to improve the enterprise risk management system and inform the EB of any critical risks of strategic importance. 

o  
From a UNOPS perspective The
 joint information note points towards key risks associated with project delivery, financial management and stakeholder engagement. It also points to more concrete risks regarding UNOPS' operations in fragile and conflict affected places, shortage of talent,
 sexual abuse due to the geographical operations of UNOPS, regaining trust among partners since S3i failures, implementing the many reforms at UNOPS and increasing financial constraints.     

4.     Organisational culture 

o  
The informal information
 note provides an update on the implementation of the work plan to transform the organisational culture. Status of each action point is in this
 annex.    

5.     Implementation
 of the Comprehensive Response Plan 

o  
This is the last update to the EB on the implementation of the CRP. As the note was written in November, 3 of the outstanding recommendations were yet to be completed by the end of 2024. These related to 1) revising the management and organisational
 culture towards broader engagement and less top-down, 2) invest in outcome-reporting, and 3) revision of financial rules and regulations.  

o  
The EB is asked to release the third tranche (11.8M USD) for the implementation and to initiate the second independent review of the implementation of the CRP.  

6.     Review
 of the whistleblower process 

o  
The informal information note provides an overview of the now completed overhaul of UNOPS' whistleblower mechanism. 

o  
The new system is set to launch in January 2025 and will introduce: 1) a central platform for reporting, 2) ressources to provide early informal guidance, 3) a workplace conduct team within PLG, 4) a new advisory group to address systemic issues. 

7.     Portfolio risk assessment of UNOPS


o  
As a response to the original KPMG recommendations a
 portfolio risk assessment is presented that outlines a number of risks in UNOPS' portfolio. These relate e.g. to 1) challenges in managing complex infrastructure projects, 2) large-scale procurement of health products, 3) capacity of supplivers and implementing
 partners. 

8.     Calculation
 method for excess reserves 

o  
The note presents a suggestion for revising the calculation methodology for calculating UNOPS' excess reserves. The proposed changes are to ensure that only liquid assets are calculated as part of the potential excess reserves and that only if the excess
 reserve exceeds 20% of the minimum operational reserve, it should trigger the refund process. 

o  
By the end of 2023 UNOPS distributed 123.2M USD of the excess reserve back to partners and all other funds had been transferred to the RC system and the SDG fund. Only 0.6M USD is withheld as these relate to discussions with partners. 

9.     Implementation
 of the PID 

o  
This is the annual status of implementation of the PID that points towards progress in seven programmes (country engagements, partnerships and project management, procurement, HR, finance, data, market research for the new ERP). 

o  
Notice that the selection of a new ERP system can only be done after a formal evaluation is presented to the EB (as requested by the EB). Therefore the timeline for the PID has been extended by one year to 2028.


I hope this brief overview helps - and I look very much forward to hearing your initial thinking about the topics. 



 


All the best,


Asbjørn

Investments: Operating at pre-seed and seed, we're one of the most active investors in Europe and the winner of the Business Green Early Stage Investor or the Year.

Jeg skal beklage, at vi endnu ikke har fået sendt jer svar på spørgsmålet om MOMS’en. Det
 er klart, at I skal have svar, således at I regnskabsmæssigt kan få håndteret beløbene. Nedenfor refereres de oplysninger, vi har fået på forespørgslen om MOMS fra 2016-2017, hvor UNOPS angiveligt pga interne fejl har glemt at indsende anmodning om refusion
 på i alt 909.203,81 kr. inden for fristen på de 3 år.
 
Som tidligere nævnt, har vi talt med Skattestyrelsen, nærmere bestemt styrelsens afdeling
 for Jura, Skatteproces og Forvaltningsret. De oplyser, at i medfør af Skatteforvaltningslovens §31, stk. 2 har den momspligtige 3 års frist (efter angivelsesfristens udløb) til ordinær genoptagelse af afgiftstilsvar.
Den frist er overskredet. 
 
Det blev foreslået, at UNOPS gør sig bekendt med Skatteforvaltningslovens § 32, stk. 1, nr.
 4, som anfører mulighed for ekstraordinær genoptagelse hvis der foreligger særlige omstændigheder. Opmærksomheden blev henledt på, at det
ikke er særlige omstændigheder, hvis fejlen skyldes borgeren/virksomheden eller dennes repræsentant.

 
Styrelsen henviste i øvrigt UNOPS til den juridiske vejledning

A.A.8.3.2.2.2.4 Særlige omstændigheder - info.skat.dk. Der er ikke umiddelbart noget i den juridiske vejledning som antyder, at der skulle være mulighed for ekstraordinær genoptagelse. Styrelsen henviste imidlertid til, at såfremt UNOPS efter at have gjort
 sig bekendt med relevant lovgivning og den juridiske vejledning måtte være i tvivl om sine muligheder, kunne man overveje at få en jurist eller anden specialiseret rådgiver til at se på, om man kunne have en sag.

 
Skulle en sådan jurist/rådgiver vurdere, at der kunne være en sag, oplyste styrelsen, at
 en sådan anmodning skulle fremsættes til Protokollen (jf. MOMS-lovens § 45, stk. 7), og så skulle Protokollen oversende den til Skattestyrelsen til en udtalelse.
 
Vi ser frem til at høre fra jer vedrørende ovenstående, herunder om I ønsker at forfølge
 spørgsmålet om ekstraordinær genoptagelse gennem en jurist/rådgiver.
 

Med venlig hilsen

Søren

 UN Partner to “ensure that the Contractor and/or Implementing Partner has the capacity to comply with such E&S Obligations”.

PS - your colleagues in Kathmandu might also reach out to you / your colleagues in your legal team to initiate this dialogue on a new standard template. Just flagging this to avoid any confusion. 
Looking very much forward to hearing back from you.

Attachment: --none--

Subject: Under-claimed and over-claimed VAT/MOMS
Body:
Dear Asbjørn,
 
As previously mentioned in correspondence between us, we have been in contact with the Danish Tax Agency (Skattestyrelsen) and their Department for Legal Affairs, Tax Process
 and Administrative Law (Jura, Skatteproces og Forvaltningsret). They have informed us that pursuant to the Danish Law on Tax Administration (Skatteforvaltningsloven) §31 (2) the person/entity liable for MOMS/VAT has a period of 3 years (after the expiry of
 the declaration period) for ordinary resumption of VAT liability, i.e. to apply for reimbursement of MOMS.

 
In regards to your under-claimed MOMS from 2016-2017 (expenses amounting to DKK 909,203.81) the deadline for ordinary request for reimbursement of MOMS has been exceeded.

 
UNOPS has informed us that the expenses in question were not submitted to the Protocol Department within the 3 year period due to mistakes by one or more staff members. The
 Danish Tax Agency furthermore referred to §32 (1)(4) (i.e. § 32, stk. 1, nr. 4) of the Law on Tax Administration, which refers to a possibility for extraordinary resumption (after the 3 year period) if special circumstances exist. The Tax Agency mentioned
 that it would not be considered special circumstances if the error/mistake is caused by the business/entity or one of its representatives. UNOPS may also see the legal guide,
A.A.8.3.2.2.2.4
 Særlige omstændigheder - info.skat.dk, regarding special circumstances. There is nothing in the legal guide to suggest the presence of special circumstances and thereby justify
 extraordinary resumption of the reimbursement claims. The Protocol Department adheres to the information and guidance provided by the Tax Agency and cannot on the grounds mentioned extraordinarily receive and process the expenses in question for reimbursement.
 
However, the Tax Agency mentioned that if UNOPS, after familiarizing itself with the relevant legislation and the legal guidance mentioned above, were in doubt about its rights
 and/or options, it might consider acquiring the services of a lawyer or other specialized adviser to look into whether there are possibilities to pursue the matter within the framework of the Law on Tax Administration. Should UNOPS wish to pursue the matter
 regarding under-claimed VAT/MOMS, the Tax Agency advised that a request for a legally binding opinion should be submitted to the Protocol Department (cf. VAT Act/MOMS-loven § 45 (7)), and the Protocol Department should in turn forward the request to the Tax
 Agency for such an opinion.
 
In the matter of over-claimed VAT/MOMS, relating to four duplicated expense submissions from 2015, 2016 and 2018 respectively (amounting to DKK 42,308.75), the Protocol Department
 refers to information provided by the Tax Agency, according to which such a matter/request should also be assessed pursuant to the Danish Law on Tax Administration §31 (2). The expenses in question are from 2015, 2016 and 2018, and consequently the deadline
 for ordinary resumption has been exceeded. In dialogue with the Tax Agency the Protocol Department has assessed the request for repayment of duplicated VAT/MOMS reimbursement pursuant to the Law on Tax Administration §32 (1)(4) regarding special circumstances
 for resumption. On the basis of the information provided by UNOPS and scrutinization of the reimbursement process carried out by the Protocol Department (in regards to the four expenses in question), it is the assessment of the Protocol Department that no
 special circumstances exist in this matter. The abovementioned legal guide does not offer opinions to the contrary. The Protocol Department will not pursue the matter of over-claimed VAT/MOMS further.
 
Should UNOPS have any questions to the above, please do not hesitate to contact the Protocol Department.
 
Kind regards,
Søren

Body:
Kære Sune
Som efterspurgt er vedlagt et kort projektforslag for den fulde genopbygning af Arkas Gymnasium, inkl. budgetoverslag. 
Der skønnes med et budgetbehov på ca. 6,8M USD (knap 50M DKK) for genopbygningen af Arkas. Hertil kommer skønnet ca. 0,6 M USD (ca. 4,5M DKK) til møblering, IT, mv. for at sikre eleverne mulighed for at kunne vende tilbage til skolen. 
Selve genopbygningen af skolen skønnes at tage ca. 1,5 år at gennemføre, hvoraf en del af arbejdet kan udføres under de sidste faser af stabiliseringsarbejdet. Dvs. at hvis alt går som planlagt vil skolen være genopbygget i 2026/27. 
Mine kolleger og jeg står naturligvis til rådighed for videre drøftelser og vi vil meget gerne præsentere forslaget for den private aktør som I har været i dialog med.   
I løbet af den næste uges tid forventes vi også at modtage visualiseringer af designet, så en evt. donor bedre vil kunne få indblik i, hvordan den endelige færdige skole kommer til at se ud. Det fremsender vi naturligvis også  gerne hvis der er efterspørgsel. 
Jeg frem til at høre tilbage fra jer. 
MvhAsbjørn

Subject: Re: FCLP: Norway
Body:
Dear Julie, 
Thank you very much for reaching out. 
Super happy to hear about the interest from Norway in contributing to FCLP! Could I ask how much they are considering? 
It has indeed been difficult to sign new engagements with Norway for some time due to the fallout of the S3i and the fact that the former ED was of Norwegian nationality. For your background information, the Norwegian Court of Auditors published a report in December containing a rather severe criticism of the Norwegian MFA for their lack of critical scrutiny of UNOPS at the Executive Board. 
Last engagement with Norway was a 34K top-up for the implementation of the maputo accord in April 2024. The last new engagement with Norway was back in April 2021 to support EU accession process for Western Balkans. So quite some time ago... 
Norway does not have any formal restrictions on engagements with UNOPS. But due to the salience of the S3i fallout in Norway, some skepticism may remain among some personnel that are not in the loop on the global relationship between the Norwegian Government and UNOPS. We have a very good and constructive dialogue with the HQ based persons within NORAD and the Norwegian NFA that are responsible for Norway's relationship with UNOPS. They follow our reform process closely and have been complementing UNOPS on our progress, the transparency, etc. 
A way to ease the resistance of your counterpart might be to:I reach out to our Norwegian HQ focal points at NORAD / MFA to make them aware of your ongoing conversations regarding a potential Norwegian contribution to FCLP - and encourage them to explain to your counterpart that it is perfectly legitimate to engage with UNOPS since we have implemented the reforms. 

That you kindly refer your counterpart to the persons responsible for NORAD's / MFA's relationship with UNOPS - to get their take on Norwegian engagements with UNOPS. To initiate this, could I kindly ask for the name, email, position and division/unit of the person you're in contact with? I assume it is someone from NORAD? If so - you could refer your counterpart to Mr. Stein Erik Horjen (Stein.Erik.Horjen@norad.no). Stein Erik is following UNOPS' reform process very closely and knows that there is a great relationship between NORAD's Director General and our Executive Director. In fact, Jorge was invited to be a keynote speaker at the annual NORAD conference last week (unfortunately Jorge couldn't attend as he has to participate in the Executive Board). 
In case you're dealing with the Norwegian MFA, the relevant person to refer your counterpart to, would be Mr. Constantin Nicolaysen (Constantin.Nicolaysen.Karame@mfa.no) who is a Chief Advisor in their UN Division and responsible for the Norwegian Government's relationship with UNOPS. He is also the Norwegian member of our Executive Board. 
I hope this helps - and as mentioned I would be more than happy to jump on a call to discuss how to approach if you would find it useful. 
In any case, it would be super good if we could get the Norwegians to contribute to the FCLP - as it would be the first new engagement with them in years. 
All the best,Asbjørn

Kære Marie-Louise, Louise, Camilla og Adwan, 
Jeg rækker ud til jer som opfølgning på samtaler mellem UNOPS' Executive Director, Jorge Moreira da Silva og Erik Laursen i NYC for nylig om situationen i Gaza samt den seneste udvikling i Syrien. 
Ift. Gaza undersøger vi i øjeblikket flere projekter, som hurtigt og direkte kan adressere nogle af de mest akutte og presserende  behov, som muligvis kunne være i jeres interesse. Disse inkluderer bl.a.: 
Styrkelse af energiforsyningen: Dette projekt har til formål at forbedre levevilkårene og sikre stabil adgang til kritiske og essentielle tjenester for de mest berørte palæstinensere i Gaza ved at genopbygge og styrke elsystemet med vedvarende energi. 

Sikker fjernelse og genanvendelse af murbrokker: Dette projekt fokuserer på at rydde ødelagt infrastruktur, en forudsætning for genopbygningsindsatsen.

Humanitært brændstof til Gaza: Dette projekt sigter mod at anskaffe og levere brændstof til Gaza for at understøtte humanitære operationer og essentielle tjenester som fx drift af hospitaler mv.Jeg har vedhæftet en kort oversigt over disse potentielle projekter til jeres gennemgang. Alle projekterne er skalerbare i budgetniveau. 
Tilsvarende har jeg vedlagt en oversigt over en foreløbig behovsanalyse for Syrien samt mulige projekter af evt. dansk interesse. Disse vedrører bl.a. genopførelse af skoler, veje, broer, landbrugsområder, adgang til vand og indkøb og levering af medicinsk udstyr, Også fsva. de mulige projekter i Syrien er der tale om skalerbare indsatser.  

Vi vil sætte stor pris på muligheden for at drøfte disse projekter nærmere med jer, såfremt det skulle have jeres evt. interesse.  

Jeg ser meget frem til at høre fra jer. 
MvhAsbjørn

Subject: Updates from GLO
Body:
Dear all
Beyond the emotive language, quite an interesting read about Swiss cuts to foreign aid and the UN:

In a nutshell: 

Switzerland is cutting its foreign aid budget for 2025 by CHF 110 million, affecting several UN agencies and NGOs. Major cuts include CHF 3m from UNAids, CHF 7.31m from the Global Partnership for Education, and CHF 4m from UNESCO. Contributions to UNICEF, UNDP, and UN Women will also be reduced. Swiss NGOs will face an average 10% cut in core contributions, impacting organizations like Caritas and Médecins Sans Frontières. Dear Birgit, Thank you for your explanation of the changes and the rationale behind them. We’ve gone through the revisions and have a few adjustments we’d like to propose.
First, with respect to the definition of Non-Staff Personnel, we would like to account for the fact that a large number of our personnel are International Contractor Agreement (ICA) - a type of contract modality used to engage individuals as consultants or contractors for specific projects or assignments. Moving down to Article 15 and 19 - this is the most significant issue for us as it presents a challenge under Articles 100 and 101 of the UN Charter. These articles establish member states’ commitment to respecting the exclusivity of the international character of the UN, including an obligation not to seek to influence the UN in the discharge of its responsibilities, as well as the duty to recruit personnel based on the highest standards. Sharing CVs deviates from this commitment, as it exposes UNOPS to scrutiny over its recruitment processes and the individuals selected. Instead, we propose sharing the TORs of the selected individuals. This would allow us to demonstrate that we have recruited personnel to perform the requested work, without inviting interference in our independent recruitment processes. Additionally, we have confidentiality obligations toward our personnel and should not be sharing their CVs without consent. Finally at Article 20, we would like to add a reference to UNOPS applying its established regulations, rules, policies, and procedures to ensure a common understanding of the standard being applied by UNOPS in making its determinations.  We also propose to align Article 20 with the revision to Article 15, meaning that instead of sharing CVs, we would share terms of reference.I have attached the draft with track changes and comments for easy reference.  Let me know if you'd like to discuss further. Best regards, 
Elizabeth

 Personnel, Personal Data), which had been updated to clarify the scope of E&S obligations. To ensure consistency throughout the agreement, we changed the references to these definitions throughout. This does not entail any substantive changes of requirements.
   
As you indicated that the project for Papua New Guinea was approved under the Bank’s previous environmental and social safeguards, I would like to clarify whether you are referring to the safeguards that belong in the July template, now superseded by the
 November version. When referring to the Bank’s previous environmental and social safeguards, we are referring to the Bank’s E&S policies that were in force prior to the Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) being adopted
 and becoming effective for new projects in late 2018. The PNG Project, under which the Government is engaging UNOPS, was prepared under these “old” safeguard policies, which continue to be the applicable policy framework for this project.

What this means in practice for the SFA with UNOPS is that the E&S Covenant (article 21) will refer to the “Environmental and Social Safeguard Policies” instead of the ESSs, otherwise the E&S Covenant remains the same.
“Environmental and Social Risk Management. (a) The UN Partner shall provide the Technical Assistance in accordance with the
Bank’s Environmental and Social Safeguard Policies, and as outlined in Annex I, Section III
(the “E&S Obligations”).

(b) To this end, when the UN Partner engages Contractors and/or Implementing Partners in the provision of Technical Assistance under this Agreement, the UN Partner shall identify
 all parts of the E&S Obligations relevant to the provision of Technical Assistance to be carried out by the Contractors and/or Implementing Partners, which may include, inter alia, requirements for codes of conduct, security risk assessment and management,
 reporting on E&S implementation, and incident and accident notification and reporting. The UN Partner shall, in relation to each Contractor and/or Implementing Partner:


ensure that the Contractor and/or Implementing Partner is contractually bound to comply with such E&S Obligations;ensure that the Contractor and/or Implementing Partner has the capacity to comply with such E&S Obligations;
monitor the implementation of such E&S Obligations by the Contractor and/or Implementing Partner and require remedial action where necessary; andat the Bank’s request, share with the Bank[1]
 the contracts entered into with the Contractors and/or Implementing Partners engaged in the provision of Technical Assistance, redacted to remove Personal Data and confidential business information, provided that such redactions do not impair the Bank's ability
 to review the E&S Obligations included in those contracts.”

 to labor management procedures); they also did not require a Stakeholder Engagement Plan (so no reference to that either). Under the old safeguard policies there was also no Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) so the chapeau to the table will only
 be referring to the Financing Agreement, and not to an ESCP. 
Additionally, may I ask whether you anticipate any further changes to the TA template to be punished, beyond those already incorporated in the version you shared for Tonga?
Since the new TA template has not come out yet, we are adopting the retrofitting approach to the Tonga and PNG agreements, meaning that the old agency-specific TA templates are being used, and are only being retrofitted with the
 new E&S sections (Article 21, E&S Annex, and definitions). We are making the changes to retrofit the PNG agreement now and plan to share it with you shortly.

We’d be happy to discuss this further at a convenient time.


With best regards, 


Elizabeth

appreciated the conversation and look forward to continuing our engagement in
2025, with a view to establishing potential partnership opportunities in the
future.

interest and priority you highlighted in support of Finland's priorities in

·      
Rural economic development

·      
Sustainable land/resource management

·      
Digital transformation and system support

·      
Improving WASH services

·      
Strengthening conditions for inclusive basic
education

complementary support services we might offer to support your collaboration and

Subject: Summary from ED meeting with PR of Finland, 30 January 2025
Body:
Dear Rahul, Freya, Asbjorn and Naimo,
Please see below a summary from the recent meeting between Jorge and the PR of Finland in New York:
 Meeting with H.E. Ms. Elina Kalkku, Permanent Representative of Finland (30 January 2025 / Briefing)UNOPS participants: Jorge, Freya, OonaThe PR was accompanied by Mr. Ramses Malaty, Deputy Director General, Department for Development Policy, and Mr. Antti Virtanen, First Secretary, Permanent Mission of Finland.The ED briefed the PR on his upcoming mission to the Middle East. He shared updates on the UN2720 Mechanism, highlighting its success in promoting transparency and accountability. Additionally, he noted that UNOPS has scaled up its fuel operations in Gaza, now assuming responsibility for fuel distribution inside Gaza. The ED underscored the critical importance of the early recovery phase, particularly activities such as the removal of rubble and debris. As UNOPS celebrates its 30th anniversary in 2025, the ED reflected on this milestone as an opportunity for UNOPS and Member States to evaluate the progress of the reforms achieved through the Comprehensive Response Plan (CRP). He reported that the CRP has been successfully completed (with the exception of PID), and that recovery efforts of the funds related to S3i  led by OLA are advancing well. UNOPS is looking forward to the third party review on the CRP which will confirm its completion and be addressed at the 2025 Annual Session. The PR congratulated the ED on the reform agenda and expressed appreciation for the informative closed session on the recovery efforts held earlier in the week. The PR and ED discussed the letter sent by anonymous UNOPS personnel to the Board.Finally, the PR and ED reflected on the role of the Executive Board and agreed on the importance of strengthening collaboration and coherence among agencies sharing the Board. The ED and PR discussed initiatives such as organizing joint interactive dialogues and showcasing project stories from the country level to enrich the quality of the discussions at the Board. The Joint Meeting of the Boards in June 2024 (focused on the HDP Nexus) was highlighted as a successful example of these efforts. Additionally, the PR shared insights from her weekly meetings with EU and Nordic delegations, noting a shared concern that a communication gap appears to exist between the information available to delegates and PRs on Board-related topics.
Please let me know if you have any questions!
Kind regards,Oona

Subject: FA comments Feb 2025: UNFPA MOU Discussion
Body:
Dear Rebecca and colleagues, 
We are pleased to share with you attached further comments and feedback on the draft Framework Agreement, in response to the latest comments provided by the FCDO.
We also note the feedback from Louise at the time that, as FCDO is now a fully merged department, some policies relating to the framework have changed and in the absence of further context from us, it is difficult for you to agree to revert to historic positions when FCDO policy has moved on. There are, however, a couple of areas where extensive discussions resulted in agreement ( such as the audit discharge annex)  and where we would appreciate not reverting and re-negotiating, further delaying this process.
We have flagged some areas where further clarity is needed; though there may be others after UN agencies review; on the financial reporting (33),  procurement (para 76) and asset management (para 78). 
On communication and Branding -Para 90 and related annex, we would highly recommend keeping the detailed planning of communications efforts and assets to the programme document, rather than a legal agreement. 
Organization Payment Request Form - Annex 1, the form has a number of issues ( as discussed our financial rules stipulate that payment must be in advance, our operational currency is USD, for payments in full or a first tranche this information is not available). Can we revert to the simpler form of the payment request form agreed previously. 
Audit discharge certification - Annex 2 - this form has been discussed and removed. We do not  audit all projects automatically and we cannot implement a pre-arranged audit. 
Visibility statement - Annex 3 -  we would request keeping the detailed planning of communications efforts and assets to the programme document, rather than a legal agreement. 
One the Due Diligence assessment, Annex 4 a separate call was held on 7 November and the draft is attached. 
Please note, we are sharing these comments in order to move this process along. However, while our approach on most items are in line with that of other UN agencies based on the history of the negotiations,  we stress that considering the long lapse in time, other UN agencies still need to review the draft FA after we have feedback from FCDO and hopefully a cleaner document.All the best, 
Asa

Subject: Re: Feedback from meeting with Human Practice Foundation?
Body:
Dear Fumie, Elena and colleagues in Nairobi, 
I just met with the CEO of the Human Practice Foundation, Ms. Pernille Kruse Madsen to discuss how to proceed with the collaboration on building schools in Kenya. 
Pernille remains very keen on establishing this collaboration and moving forward. On March 25 we will have to present the project idea to the Board of the LEGO Foundation who seems interested in funding the project. As mentioned the aim is 160 schools - depending on the funding available.  
I explained to Pernille that we are OK to initiate the collaboration by simply acting as the procurer of products for building the schools. Human Practice Foundation will then themselves do the infrastructure part. I have asked Pernille to send us the specs for the items they wish for us to procure for the schools. Once they have sent that, I promised that we would revert with price estimates - upon which they could make a decision on whether it would be beneficial for them to work with us or not. 
I hope this is an OK approach for you? 
I am aware that this is not an entirely regular project - and that the funding level may be rather small to start with. However, initiating a collaboration with Human Practice Foundation could be a lever to - at a later stage - access more funding from private sector and philanthropic foundations in the Nordics. I therefore hope that together we can go the extra mile to ensure that this becomes a success.

 and energy-efficient cooling solutions in the date and dairy value chains across five areas in Tunisia. For reference, please find attached the proposal as well as an overview of UNOPS’ presence in North Africa. 
 
To summarise, the proposal focuses on enhancing access to solar energy and energy-efficient cooling solutions in Tunisia's date and dairy value chains. It aims

In the meeting, I also noted that Denmark could potentially be interested in supporting initiatives such as these projects carried out by UNOPS on behalf of our
 partners in Tunisia: Support to Tunisia's Border Control and Management of Migration Flows (Italy),

 Estimada Isabela,
 
 
 
  
 
 Gracias por su correo.
 
 
 
  
 
 Dos consultas.
 
 
 
  
 
 Choice of law: Con referencia a este tema, el BCIE también tiene privilegios e inmunidades. Sin embargo, someterse a una ley (idealmente para estos casos) no causa un “waiver” si se establece contractualmente que no se esta renunciando a privilegios e inmunidades otorgados por sus países miembros. ¿Podrían ampliar este punto?
 
 
 
  
 
 Seat of the Arbitration: ¿A qué se refieren con “deslocalizado”? El lugar del arbitraje debe tener una ubicación clara. Si dejamos deslocalizado es como decir en el aire, sin espacio geográfico claro para las partes, ¿Qué será por una vía electrónica?, ¿qué se definirá en el momento?, ¿cómo vamos a establecer una cláusula de resolución de conflictos que no atañe un lugar donde resolver la discrepancia? Por favor amplíen la explicación.
 
 
 
  
 
 Podemos incluir en el contrato ley aplicable y lugar del arbitraje dejando claro y por escrito que esto no implica una renuncia de los privilegios e inmunidades de los cuales gozan las partes; y así mitigamos ese riesgo que les preocupa.
 
 
 
  
 
 Muchas gracias.

Subject: Acuerdos: trabajo conjunto BCIE-UNOPS 2021
Body:
Queridos Manuel, Adriana y Ricardo,

Fue un gusto conversar con Ustedes en días pasados. En seguimiento a los acuerdo de nuestra reunión, les quisiera proponer lo siguiente:
1. Renovación del Convenio Marco de Cooperación.Este Convenio venció el 22 de Junio del 2019, y para su renovación, estamos trabajando con los equipos de project management, finanzas y legal para hacerles una propuesta de acuerdo con una plantilla estándar que nos permita agilizar tiempos. Esperamos hacerles llegar una primera versión para su consideración la semana entrante.
2. Trabajo conjunto en CubaEstamos en constante comunicación con Kerstin, y entendemos que aunque el Gobierno de Cuba no ha tomado una decisión al respecto. Mientras estamos preparándonos para para una rápida y efectiva respuesta, en base a nuestra experiencia en agua y saneamiento. 
3. Comunicación de alto nivel de logros junto a Gobiernos, BCIE y UNOPSVemos una gran oportunidad inicial hacer un plan de comunicación masiva: redes, medios, evento, editoriales a fin de comunicar sobre los grandes resultados obtenidos en Costa Rica. Podemos organizar un evento sobre “Gestión efectiva de proyectos de infraestructura”, junto al Presidente de Costa Rica, Presidente del BCIE y el Director Regional de UNOPS, y otra autoridad de alto nivel. 
Hasta el momento en Costa Rica, juntos hemos entregado: 2 pasos a desnivel en rotondas, 2 puentes sobre el Río Virilla, 2 ampliaciones de sistemas de agua potable; y tenemos 3 proyectos más en implementación, todo por una inversión total de USD 271.6 M en el país.
4. Futura publicación conjunta sobre resultados Podemos enfocarnos desde los aspectos de Gestión Pública Justa y Equitativa, y proponemos dejarlo para  el Q3- Q4.
Quedo atenta a sus comentarios, un bonito fin de semana,
Abrazo,
Erika

On Mon, Feb 15, 2021 at 11:54 AM Erika Cristina PAREDES SANCHEZ <erikacp@unops.org> wrote:
Hola Fabrizio, 
El viernes 12 de febrero el BCIE solicitó una reunión ya que estaban interesados en explorar la posibilidad de que les apoyemos a implementar un proyecto en Cuba.
1. Sobre la colaboración: BCIE tiene sus 2 primeros proyectos (vinculados a la emergencia del COVID) en Cuba, que lo implementa a través del PNUD. El tercero lo quisieran implementar con nosotros, para diversificar sus asociados en la Isla, y les gustaría que trabajemos de la misma manera que lo estamos haciendo en Nicaragua. Buscan trabajar con la ONU, PNUD y UNOPS, ya que tienen que adaptar su mecanismo de implementación, puesto que reconocen las sanciones de EEUU (propiedades, bienes, personas y moneda).


2. Buscan que UNOPS implemente el proyecto para el Plan de  Saneamiento en el río Luyanó: Valor $150 millones, de los cuales $23 son cofinanciados por la Agencia Francesa de Desarrollo (AFD), y el resto por el banco. La mayor parte es préstamos.La implementación sería bajo las normas y procedimiento de UNOPS, para 5 añosContraparte del BCIE: Banco Central de CubaContraparte Técnica: Instituto Nacional de Recursos Hidráulicos (INRH)En el caso de avanzar, al igual que otros países el BCIE firmaría el crédito Gobierno de Cuba, y nosotros en paralelo un acuerdo directo con el  Gobierno. La transferencia de recursos sería directo BCIE-UNOPS.
3. Próximos pasos:El BCIE propone hacer una reunión BCIE-Banco Central para ver si hay un interés del Gobierno para que UNOPS sea la agencia implementadora. Posteriormente, proponen hacer una reunión tripartita BCIE-Banco Central - ONU/UNOPS.De nuestro lado, hemos informado: i. Todo tiene que ser coordinado a través de la Coordinadora Residente, Consuelo Vidal;  ii. Que informaremos de inmediato a la Coordinadora Residente en cuanto a esta reunión; iii. El Gobierno de Cuba ha aceptado la inclusión del UNOPS en el Marco de Cooperación. iv. Tenemos que negociar el marco jurídico que permite la operación de UNOPS en el país.Les enviaremos al BCIE información sobre UNOPS, sus mecanismos de operación y experiencia en agua y saneamiento.
4. Por el BCIE participaron:Manuel Torres, Gerente del Sector Público SoberanoAna Lily Mejia, Especialista en Infraestructura ProductivaKerstin Morales, Ejecutiva de Proyectos
De ser posible, te propondría que lo conversemos, y canalicemos este correo con Consuelo Vidal, para que esté informada, y con ello tomaré contacto con mi contraparte Liudmila Curbelo.
Abrazo,
Erika

--

Subject: BCIE: Info sobre República Domincana
Body:
Hola Giuseppe, 
Un gusto saludarte y feliz año! Te comparto en este link el pipeline de operaciones del BCIE para República Dominicana. En resumen, sus operaciones activas:
Energía: Financiamiento para la generación de 80 megatavios de energía limpia renovable. (USD 350 M)
Agro: Fortalecimiento del sector agropecuario con enfoque tecnológico sostenible. (USD 60 M)Transporte: Ampliación de la red del metro Santo Domingo. (USD 500 M) 
Otros antecedentes relevantes:1. El contacto que tuvimos fue con Hostos Rizik Lugo, Director Ejecutivo del BCIE para RD, quien conversó con Alejandro para la compra de ambulancias.2. RD es el país con mayor mortalidad por accidentes de tránsito en LAC (30 muertes/100.000 habitantes). De UNOPS, el retainer Francisco Javier Lopez tiene contacto con el Ministerio de Transporte, la Dirección de carreteras, la Agencia Nacional de Seguridad Vial, y el Banco Europeo de Inversiones; para temas de formaciones/asesoramiento en seguridad vial. Actualmente UNOPS está en proceso de firmar una alianza con iRAP (International Road Assessment Programme) quiénes tienen interés y contacto con RD, para la mejora de carreteras con miras a incrementar la seguridad vial.3. En una entrevista que dió Dante Mossi, mencionó que se tiene previsto destinar fondos adicionales en los próximos dos años a los sectores: reducción del riesgo de desastres naturales (US$100 millones) y salud (US$30 millones)

Hej Anders
Tak for frokost og snak i dag! Super hygsomt! 
Som aftalt vedlægger jeg et par papirer, om de to skoler placeret i Zaporizhzhia, som mine kolleger i Kyiv har været i dialog med dine kolleger om (Anna Yanchenko og Yulia Stelmakh).  
Naturligvis op til jer at vurdere - tænker umiddelbart, at for Carlsberg kan genopbygning af skoler i Zaporizhzhia være en meningsfuld investering for lokalsamfundet, hvor især uddannelsesfaciliteterne er blevet meget hårdt ramt. Det kunne fx demonstrere, at Carlsbergs solidaritet med de samfund, hvor jeres medarbejdere bor - og at I investerer i den næste generation, landets genopretning og de svageste i samfundet.
Det ville være en meget konkret og synlig indsats, der vil efterlade et varigt aftryk og positionere Carlsberg som en virksomhed, der tager samfundsansvar alvorligt i en af Europas største humanitære og genopbygningsudfordringer.
Som nævnt mundtligt kan en evt. indsats naturligvis skaleres alt efter budget-ambitioner. Nedenfor et par hurtige informationer om de to skoler:
Zaporizhzhia Specialized Boarding School “Dzherelo”Specialskole for +300 studerende med autisme, downs syndrom og hørehæmmede 146 ansatte  Der er behov for, at børnene vender tilbage til fysisk undervisning, da onlineformatet er vanskeligt pga. børnenes handicapsKonkret er der behov for finansiering til a) genopbygning af skolen, b) etablering af beskyttelsesrum og v) indkøb af en skolebus til transport af børneneForeløbigt skønnet budgetestimat: ca. 8,5 millioner USD (knap 60 millioner DKK) Tidshorisont: ca. 1,5 årKhortytsia National AcademySkole som uddanner fysioterapeuter, mentalt handicappede, psykologer og socialarbejdere - som der særligt er behov for i lyset af de mange skadede i krigen Ca. 1.500 studerende og ca. 600 medarbejdere Opererer pt. med online-format, hvilket indebærer store udfordringer, da der er behov for fysisk træning af fx fysioterapeuterKonkret er der behov for finansiering til a) genopbygning af skolen og b) etablering af beskyttelsesrum Foreløbigt skønnet budgetestimat: ca. 7,2 millioner USD (ca. 50 millioner DKK)Tidshorisont: ca. 1,5 årLad mig endelig høre hvad I tænker, når I har haft lejlighed til at vende internt og med jeres kolleger i Ukraine. 
Hils derhjemme - og sig at hun er inviteret på frokost i FN-byen!
BhAsbjørn

Body:
Hej Anne Marie
Der er - så vidt jeg ved - ikke anmodninger udefra for møder med den danske minister for miljø og ligestilling. 
Jorge Moreira da Silva vil imidlertid gerne mødes med ministeren forud for CEB - hvis muligt. Jorge er FN Undergeneralsekretær, Executivdirektør for UNOPS og øverste chef for FN-Byen i København. 
Jorge vil bl.a. gerne drøfte indarbejdelse af miljø- og ligestillingshensyn i større infrastruktur- og indkøbsprojekter samt hvordan danske erfaringer med øget hastighed i implementeringen - balanceret overfor ovenstående hensyn - kan bringes ind i udviklingsprojekter i udviklingslande. Jorge vil herudover gerne drøfte, hvordan vi kan blive bedre til at udveksle erfaringer, viden, kapaciteter mv. mellem danske myndigheder og FN-Byen i København. Såfremt der er øvrige ønsker til emner for drøftelse, hører vi naturligvis også meget gerne fra jer.  
Lad mig meget gerne høre fra jer om ovenstående kunne være i ministeren interesse. I så fald vil jeg foreslå, at vi finder en dato, hvor Jorge kan komme forbi jer på Slotsholmen. I er naturligvis også meget velkomne herude i FN-Byen, hvis der er ønske om det. 
På forhånd mange tak. 
MvhAsbjørn

Der orienteres hermed om, at Danmark vil være værtsland for det årlige møde i FN’s Chief Executive Board (CEB) den 8.-9. maj.
 
CEB består af 31 topchefer i FN-systemet samt Verdensbanken og IMF, og ledes af FN’s generalsekretær. CEB sætter den overordnede strategiske retning for FN-systemet.
 I vedlagte liste fremgår CEB-medlemmerne. Deltagelse af alle medlemmer i mødet er dog endnu ikke bekræftet.

 
Statsministeren og Kongehuset forventes at afholde officielle receptioner i forbindelse med besøget hhv. den 7. maj og 8. maj om aftenen. Det forventes, at dele af
 regeringen vil blive inviteret til at deltage i disse receptioner.
 
Det kan forventes, at en lang række FN-chefer vil anmode om møder med regeringen i marginen af CEB-mødet, enten den 6., 7. eller 9. maj.
 
Der lægges fsva. bilaterale møder med ministre op til, at ressortministerier selv koordinerer og afholder sådanne møder, gerne i koordination med relevante enheder
 i Udenrigsministeriet.

Please take a look at the changes and let me know if you have any questions or further suggestions.

Subject: Application for Standby Partnership to UN Yemen Mine Action
Body:
Dear Mr. Behrouzi, 
I am reaching out to you to seek your guidance on the process for establishing a partnership within the Standby Partnership Network between UNOPS and FCDO for a UN Mine Action project in Yemen. 
The project aims to address explosive threats for the protection of civilians in Yemen, through survey and clearance of landmines and ERW contamination in most affected governorates in the South through INGO partners (by way of grants), enhanced coordination mechanism and enabling environment for the scaling up of Mine Action interventions in the country. Under this project, UNOPS provides operations support to the Yemen Mine Action Coordination Centre (YMACC) in order to ensure that critical functions of coordination are maintained. The project will be implemented in close coordination with the UN Resident Coordinator’s Office (Yemen).
We are now looking for possibilities within the Standby Partnership Network to fund the 6 months extension of a Humanitarian Mine Action Adviser based in Sana’a to continue  consultation and advisory to the Mine Action national institutions, UN and INGO partners engaged in Mine Action, and report against the obligations under the Antipersonnel Mine Ban Convention. We initially estimate this at approx. 275K USD. 
As we are unsure about the application process for applying for support within the Standby Partnership Network, we have taken the liberty of drafting a proposal which I am attaching to this email for your review. 
I would greatly appreciate your kind guidance and help and remain at your entire disposal for any clarifying inquiries. 
I look very much forward to hearing back from you. 
Thank you in advance. 
Best,Asbjørn  --

Kære kolleger på Asiatisk Plads, 
D. 5-6 maj kommer Executive Direktøren for The Sanitation and Hygiene Fund (SHF) - Dominic O'Nell - på besøg i København. Han har i den forbindelse udtryk ønske om at mødes med relevante i det danske Udenrigsministerium mhp. at orientere om SHF's arbejde. 
Vi ville derfor sætte stor pris på, om I evt- havde tid til at mødes på et tidspunkt d. 5. eller 6. maj, til en kort introduktion til SHF's arbejde? Lad mig meget gerne vide hvornår det kunne passe for jer. 
Til jeres baggrundsinformation arbejder SHF for at forbedre sanitære forhold i udviklingslande med fokus på at: Sikre adgang til toiletter og handvaskfaciliteter i skoler, sundhedscentre og lokalsamfundUddanne folk i god hygiejnepraksis, herunder håndvask, madlavning og affaldsbehandlingReducere spredningen af sygdomme som diarré, kolera og tyfus, der ofte er forbundet med dårlige sanitære forholdI dag mangler næsten halvdelen af verdens befolkning adgang til sikker og forsvarlig sanitet, og en ud af fire kvinder på verdensplan kan ikke håndtere deres menstruation sikkert. Det er disse forhold, som SHF arbejder på at forbedre - pt. primært i Kenya, Nigeria og Uganda med planer om udvidelse til Vestafrika og Asien.
Jeg vedlægger til jeres baggrundsinformation et par one-pagers om SHF's initiativer. 
Jeg ser frem til at høre fra jer. 
På forhånd mange tak. 
MvhAsbjørn

Dear Tommaso:


 



As you already know, most of our work in support of GEF projects is managed by WEC but there are some exemptions.


 


1. UNOPS manages the GEF project, ‘Implementing the strategic action programme for the South China Sea and Gulf of Thailand’, on
 behalf of UNEP. Working closely with the governments of Cambodia, China, Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam, the project aims to protect natural habitats, improve planning based on scientific knowledge, and encourage cooperation between countries
 in managing coastal areas.


2. UNOPS also manages the GEF project, ‘Protecting and restoring the ocean’s natural capital,
 building resilience and supporting region-wide Investments for sustainable blue socio-economic development (PROCARIBE+)’ on behalf of UNDP.


3. The GEF Small Grants Programme (SGP) is
 a global program implemented by UNDP-GEF and executed by UNOPS. UNOPS has been the implementing partner for the SGP since its inception in 1992. The SGP is a Corporate GEF program that provides grants to community-based organizations and NGOs working on environmental
 conservation and sustainable development.


UNOPS's role in the SGP is to provide a range of services, including:

·
Legal framework: UNOPS provides the legal framework for the SGP, ensuring that it operates in accordance with international standards.

·
Grant management services: UNOPS manages the grant application process, including reviewing proposals, awarding grants, and monitoring grant implementation.

·
Operations support: UNOPS provides operational support to SGP projects, including financial management, procurement, travel, and other administrative
 services.

·
Personnel recruitment: UNOPS assists with the recruitment of staff for SGP projects.

·
Procurement: UNOPS helps with the procurement of goods and services for SGP projects.

·
Financial management: UNOPS manages the SGP's finances, including accounting, budgeting, and reporting.

4. UNOPS is the executing agency for the GEF "Biodiversity conservation, sustainable land management
 and enhanced water security in Lake Tanganyika basin" for which UNEP is the implementing agency. The project aims to enhance transboundary cooperation and SAP implementation through sustainable fisheries co-management, biodiversity conservation and restoration
 of degraded landscapes in selected key biodiversity of Lake Tanganyika.


 


It's also worth mentioning that UNOPS hosts and manages a number of multi-stakeholder climate funds and initiatives
 such as the Initiative for Climate Action Transparency and the NDC Partnership.


 


I'm looping in our colleague Katrin Lichtenberg, who in light of her experience with the management of GEF funds may
 contribute to this effort of setting a general collaboration framework for implementation / execution.

Dear Sune







Thank you for your review and always rapid responses.







In the attached we have accepted the non-substantial track changes for other paragraphs than 5 and 8 to make it easier to read.







With regards to paragraph 5, we are concerned that using the term ‘promptly’ can be interpreted to mean an almost immediate notification, which in some cases may not be possible depending on a number of factors (eg. if the awareness came via whistleblowing
 process or via audit, time to look into its credibility, prioritisation of resources, etc.). We would therefore propose to remove the timing requirement and leave it as “UNOPS shall notify“.



- Would that be acceptable?







There is a need for an indication of timing, to avoid differences in opinion about what is acceptable. We have, including very recently, had unfortunate experiences where the lack of an agreed timeline led to reporting coming forward very  late. In other standard
 agreements with multilateral partners is the wording the following:







  *   The United Nations shall promptly notify the Ministry of any allegations of Financial Irregularities of which it has been informed or has otherwise become aware, provided, however, that (i) the allegations directly relate to the Project funded by the
 Contribution or

  *   XX will advise the donor immediately of credible allegations of fraud or corruption involving the contribution and will inform the Donor when an investigation is launched by XX, always subject to XX regulations, rules and procedures.







Would it be possible to say: UNOPS will notify the Funding Source immediately when an internal investigation is launched subject to credible allegations of fraud or corruption involving the contribution.







With regards to paragraph 8 our concern is that the agreement can be interpreted to mean that Denmark has the right to question the independent investigations or operations of our independent Investigations and Audit Group (IAIG), which we cannot agree to.
 In this respect we would like to make you aware of our operational directives regarding investigations (see attached OD.ED.2022.01). See especially section 6: Accountabilities of IAIG Personnel for further background as to IAIG’s role and accountability.







It remains unclear to us why para 8 is suggested deleted – all the more so since it is established policy with the UN Secretariat. The assertion that the MFA can question an internal investigation is correct, but the wording does not specify the IAIG – perhaps
 it is the absence of IAIG in the text that poses the challenge to UNOPS as the involvement of the IAIG normally would suggest ‘appropriate action’?







We therefore reiterate the suggestion that para 8 remains as is.







With UNOIOS, it would appear to us that Denmark already has some arrangements between your auditors and UNOIOS auditors to be able to agree to the language. With some donors, our IAIG has an established relationship with its counterpart on the donor’s side
 memorialized through an MoU or within a template agreement for example.







While we do not (yet) have any such MoU or template agreement between UNOPS and Denmark - I believe that it would be useful to aim for such an established relationship to be solidified in a potential upcoming MoU / template. However, given the timing of this
 engagement I do not think that it would be possible to finalise such an MoU / template in time. We will however commit to incorporate language on such a collaboration in an MoU / template - and we would also commit to amend any past engagements once such an
 MoU / template has been established between UNOPS and Denmark.







- Would that be acceptable?







Thank you in advance.







All the best,



Elene and Asbjørn

Subject: Documents for Executive Board Annual Session, June 2-5
Body:
Dear Roger and Katarina, 
As we are ramping up preparations for the Annual Session at the Executive Board on June 2-5, I wanted to provide you with a brief overview of the UNOPS relevant documents that have been shared and which are all available at the website.  
Once you have had a chance to glance over the topics for discussion, I was hoping that you might have time for a brief online, informal catch-up. Feel free to let me know when it might suit you. 
For your ease of reference please find below a list of the informal meetings relevant to UNOPS. 
Informal meetings relevant to UNOPS (see full overview here)28 February: Briefing by UNOPS Internal Audit and Investigation Group (IAIG) on its annual workplan and consolidated risk assessment25 March: Briefing by UNOPS on the Process Innovation and Digitalization programme25 April: Joint workshop on the development of the Strategic Plans 2026-2029 of UNDP, UNFPA, UNOPS, UNICEF and UN-Women12 May: Informal consultation on:Report on UNOPS Internal Audit and Investigation activities in 2024, and management responseReport of the UNOPS Audit Advisory Committee, and management response Report of the UNOPS Ethics Office on 2024 activities, and management response13 May: Briefing on the UNOPS Strategic Plan, 2026-202916 May: Joint informal consultation on implementation efforts on the repositioning of the United Nations development system19 May: Pre-session informal consultation on the annual session 2025 of the Executive Board of UNDP, UNFPA, UNOPS20 May: Informal consultation on the Annual Report of the UNOPS Executive Director:Progress report on the implementation of the UNOPS Restated Strategic Plan 2022-2025UNOPS report on the recommendations of the Joint Inspection Unit in 202421 May: Joint informal consultation on protection against sexual exploitation and abuse and sexual harassment22 May: Joint informal consultation on addressing racism and racial discrimination28 May: Informal consultations on draft decisions29 May: Informal consultations on draft decisions29 May: Closed informal consultations with UNOPS on the:UNOPS Ethics office on its workplan for 2025Unredacted report of the external third-party review of the Comprehensive Response PlanExternal formative evaluation of the Process Innovation and Digitalization Programme (PID)30 May: Informal consultations on draft decisions2-5 June: Annual Session of the Executive Board 
Documents for Annual SessionFor ease of reference - and completely on my shoulders - I have provided a very brief summary for some of the key documents - marked in italics below. 
Efforts on repositioning of the UNDSInformation note on UNOPS efforts on the repositioning of the UN Development SystemThe note shows how UNOPS actively supports the UNDS reform by helping make operations more efficient — think shared services and better coordination with Resident Coordinators. The next Strategic Plan also aims to ensure that UNOPS stay aligned with broader UN goals. Basically, UNOPS is staying practical and focused on getting things done to support the SDGs.
Internal Audit and InvestigationAnnual report of the Internal Audit and Investigations Group on internal audit and investigation activities in 2024UNOPS’ governance and risk management were deemed “partially satisfactory,” indicating that while systems are in place, there’s room for improvement. IAIG conducted 15 internal audits and 54 project audits, issuing 140 recommendations. 96% of these recommendations were implemented, reflecting the strong management commitment. IAIG received 370 complaints (a 17% increase from 2023), opened 167 cases, and completed 144 investigations. A third-party review confirmed that UNOPS is mostly ready to adopt the new 2025 Global Internal Audit Standards, with some areas needing enhancement.Annual Report of the UNOPS Audit Advisory Committee for 2024The Committee emphasizes the need for stronger internal controls and risk management, particularly in financial oversight and ethics.UNOPS management response to the 2024 annual report of the Audit Advisory Committee
EthicsActivities of the UNOPS Ethics Office in 2024The Ethics Office experienced a 22% rise in ethics-related matters, handling 1,582 cases, with about 60% related to services for personnel. Efforts continued to strengthen the whistleblower mechanism, focusing on completing reforms to rebuild trust internally and externally. The Office emphasizes training and awareness-raising activities to promote ethical standards and expected behavior among personnel.Information note on the UNOPS Management response to the 2024 Annual Report of the Ethics Office
Protection against sexual exploitation and abuse and sexual harassmentJoint information note on the Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment
Addressing racism and racial discriminationUpdates on the UNOPS efforts to implement JIU recommendations on racism and racial discriminationThe note shows how UNOPS is stepping up on inclusion — adding voluntary self-ID options, running anti-racism training, and making sure fair hiring and career growth are a priority. UNOPS is teaming up with other UN bodies and making accountability part of the plan. Basically: more awareness, more action, better culture.
Annual Report of the UNOPS Executive DirectorReport on the enhanced accountability framework of UNOPS + annexesThe report demonstrates how UNOPS has revamped the accountability framework to align with the latest UN standards, following a comprehensive review against the Joint Inspection Unit’s 2023 benchmarks. Key improvements include: ￼Clearer Roles: Defined responsibilities at all organizational levels to ensure transparency and effective decision-making; Ethical Conduct: Reinforced commitment to ethical behavior across the organization; Continuous Improvement: Plans to integrate lessons learned and best practices from within UNOPS and other UN entities. Starting in 2026, UNOPS will provide annual updates to the Executive Board on the progress of these accountability measures.Report on the implementation of the UNOPS Restated Strategic Plan, 2022-2025In 2024, UNOPS operated in over 130 countries and managed over 1,100 projects, totaling about $2.7 billion:Procurement: UNOPS handled $1.7 billion in procurement, sourcing goods and services from more than 5,800 suppliers worldwide. This played a big role in supporting partners’ operations on the ground.Grants: Over $380 million in grants were managed, supporting 1,700+ partners in implementing development projects.Human Resources: Managed contracts and salaries for nearly 9,600 personnel, helping to implement projects at the local level.Partnerships: In 2024, UNOPS signed agreements worth almost $4 billion.Annex 1: UNOPS contribution and management results frameworkAnnex 2: UNOPS framework for sustainable implementation approachesAnnex 3: UNOPS 2024 annual report on the recommendations of the Joint Inspection UnitAnnex 4: Internal oversight arrangementsSDG 1 Summary ReportSDG 11 Summary ReportCountry reports on UNOPS contributions for the GoalsCase studies of UNOPS contributions for the most vulnerable peopleUtilisation of the second tranche allotted for the implementation of the comprehensive response plan

Enjoy the reading and bon weekend when you get there!
All the best,Asbjørn
